how_to_use: Claim work by cluster key (e.g. 'placement-outcome-truth'). Each cluster lists the finding uids it closes; look those up in `findings_index`. Second-round verdicts on P1s are in `p1_verdicts` - respect corrected_severity over the original. Gap-lane findings are in `gap_findings`.

clusters.title: Approve reports success when nothing was placed, and misfiles retryable broker errors as terminal
clusters.root_cause: executeProposal returns a status object instead of throwing for every non-placement outcome (src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:239-246 declares Promise<{status:string}>; busy at :298, blocked at :498/766/1113/1136/1251/1302, not_placed at :1338/1394, error at :1319-1473) and every consumer treats "resolved" as "placed": src/lib/mobile-api.ts:1080 stamps finishCommand(command,"succeeded",result), the Swift MobileCommand has no result field (ios/SocraticTrade/MobileModels.swift:511-520) so ProposalsView.swift:481 paints a green "Approved", and the same resolver files any HTTP 4xx — 429 and 408 included — as terminal rejected_by_broker at src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:1279.
clusters.one_change: Introduce one PlacementOutcome resolver at src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:1279/:239 that classifies {placed, blocked, busy, retryable, rejected}; return it verbatim with an honest command status at src/lib/mobile-api.ts:1080, decode result.status/reasons in ios/SocraticTrade/MobileModels.swift:511, and render it on both clients the way app/console/components/approval-card.tsx:347-366 already does.

plan.summary: executeProposal (src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:232-1490) returns a {status,...} object instead of throwing for every non-placement outcome (busy/blocked/error/not_placed), and mobile-api.ts's runCommand treats any resolved value as success. Confirmed live: mobile-api.ts:965-968 calls executeProposal and returns the result verbatim; executeMobileCommand (mobile-api.ts:1077-1080) always stamps finishCommand(command,'succeeded',result) unless something THROWS. PublicMobileCommand (mobile-api.ts:134-147) already carries `result?: unknown` in the wire payload, but ios/SocraticTrade/MobileModels.swift's MobileCommand struct (lines 511-521) has no `result` field, so MobileStore.swift:214-215 maps status 'succeeded' -> .succeeded and ProposalsView.swift:481 paints 'Approved — waiting for desk refresh.' (green check) for busy/blocked/error/not_placed alike. Separately, strategy-execution.ts:1279 and the duplicated block at strategy.ts:3999 classify ANY message matching /\bHTTP 4\d\d\b/i as terminal rejected_by_broker with no status-code narrowing, so a 429 (rate limit) or 408/409 gets permanently retired instead of routed through reconcilePlacementError/not_placed. alpaca.ts's callMcp (307-349) falls back to REST on any MCP failure (timeout/5xx/parse) reusing the same client_order_id (refId), so a genuine duplicate-submission 422 ('client_order_id must be unique') lands in that same over-broad 4xx-terminal bucket and gets recorded as rejected even though the first order may be live at the broker. Also confirmed: app/console/page.tsx:996-997's second Approve call site toasts 'pos'/'Approved: Order status: ${res.status}' for ANY result including busy/blocked, duplicating approval-card.tsx's already-honest finish() mapping (lines 347-366).
plan.approach: 1) mobile-api.ts: add `class ProposalNotPlacedError extends Error { result: unknown; constructor(message: string, result: unknown) { super(message); this.name = 'ProposalNotPlacedError'; this.result = result; } }` near the other command error classes (~line 166-184). Add `const PLACEMENT_SUCCESS_STATUSES = new Set(['placed','filled','paper'])`. In runCommand's 'proposal.approve' case (965-968), after calling executeProposal, `if (!PLACEMENT_SUCCESS_STATUSES.has(result.status)) throw new ProposalNotPlacedError(result.reasons?.join(' ') || `Order was not placed (status: ${result.status}).`, result);` else return result. In errorPayload() (1056-1075) add a branch: `if (error instanceof ProposalNotPlacedError) return { message: error.message, result: error.result };` — this makes finishCommand(command,'failed',payload.result,payload.message) stamp status='failed' with the real reason as command.error (which ProposalsView.swift's existing `.failed(action, message)` branch and ActivityView's `command.error` label already render honestly — no further iOS change needed to kill the false-green-check bug). 2) For 'strategy.run_once' (952-956): do NOT broaden the throw condition (skipped_market_closed/skipped_budget are not errors — throwing would misrepresent them as failures). Instead add `interface MobileCommandResultSummary { status?: string; summary?: string }` decoded on iOS: in MobileModels.swift add `let result: MobileCommandResult?` to `MobileCommand` where `struct MobileCommandResult: Decodable { let status: String?; let summary: String? }` (extra JSON keys are ignored by Decodable by default, so this is safe against the richer server payload). In ActivityView.swift's CommandActivityRow, render `command.result?.summary` under the status pill when present and non-empty, alongside the existing `command.error` line, so a 'succeeded' run_once still shows why nothing ran. 3) Extract a shared classifier: new function in src/lib/broker-side.ts, `export function classifyPlaceOrderError(error: unknown, message: string): 'validation' | 'rejected_terminal' | 'retryable' | 'unclassified'` — OrderValidationError instance -> 'validation'; message matches /client_order_id.*(must be unique|already exists)/i -> 'retryable' (checked BEFORE the generic 4xx test, addresses tsx-01's MCP-fallback duplicate-submit); message matches /\bHTTP (400|403|422)\b/i -> 'rejected_terminal'; message matches /\bHTTP (401|408|409|425|429)\b/i -> 'retryable'; else 'unclassified' (falls through to existing reconcilePlacementError/uncertain handling, unchanged). Replace the ad hoc `if (placeError instanceof OrderValidationError || /\bHTTP 4\d\d\b/i.test(message))` block at strategy-execution.ts:1279 and the duplicated block at strategy.ts:3999 with calls to this classifier: 'validation'/'rejected_terminal' keep today's exact behavior (blocked / rejected_by_broker respectively); 'retryable' now falls into the SAME not_placed/reconcilePlacementError branch already used for OperationLeaseOwnershipError (strategy-execution.ts:1330-1339) instead of the terminal branch. 4) app/console: create app/console/lib/approve-feedback.ts exporting `toastForApproveResult(toast, result, sideLabel, symbol)` extracted verbatim from approval-card.tsx's finish() (320-366); import it from both approval-card.tsx and app/console/page.tsx's DecisionSheet.handleApprove (996-997), replacing the raw `toast.push('pos','Approved', ...)` line.
tests: test/mobile-api.test.ts — NEW test 'marks proposal.approve failed when executeProposal reports busy': reuse test/approval-lock.test.ts's setPaperPolicy/makeProposalId pattern, acquireStrategyLock('simulated-run', userId, accountId) before queueMobileCommand({commandType:'proposal.approve', payload:{proposalId}}), run processPendingMobileCommands, then assert `listMobileCommands({userId})[0].status === 'failed'` and `.error` matches /strategy run is in progress/i. FAILS today (status is 'succeeded'); PASSES after the ProposalNotPlacedError throw is added.

test/order-confirmation-status.test.ts — extend the mocked Alpaca `createOrder` with a module-level `let mockOrderThrowError: (Error & {response?:{status:number}}) | null = null` that createOrder throws when set (instead of returning). clusters.title: Automation cancel-replaces orders it does not own (bracket take-profit legs, owner GTC sells, manually cancelled stops)
clusters.root_cause: No enqueue or pump path checks who placed the order. src/lib/order-replacement.ts:754-757 filters only on side and state==="held", so a just-activated bracket take-profit leg (state "new", 15 min after entry fill) passes; the pump re-checks only type/held/quantity at :333-364 and never reads EquityOrder.orderClass (src/lib/types.ts:939, mapped at src/lib/alpaca.ts:942); it then cancels and places a MARKET order at :452-477. The protective-stop reconciler (src/lib/order-cancel.ts:198) re-places a stop the owner just cancelled, contradicting the cancel sheet's "No new order is placed."
clusters.one_change: Add an order-provenance check (orderClass/legs + app-placed clientOrderId + a manual-cancel tombstone) at src/lib/order-replacement.ts:754 and src/lib/order-cancel.ts:198 so bracket legs and owner-placed/owner-cancelled orders are never auto-replaced, and drop the per-tick deferral spam plus the misleading alert at order-replacement.ts:760-767.

plan.summary: Confirmed: no enqueue or pump path checks who placed an order before auto-cancel-replacing it. src/lib/stale-limit-orders.ts's listStaleLimitOrders (23-49) lists every working sell/cover limit/stop_limit order older than staleLimitOrderMinutes with the ONLY exclusion being isWorkingOrderState — it does not read EquityOrder.orderClass at all. isHeldExitLeg (132-134) — used to suppress the ALERT, not enqueue — only checks state==='held', so an ACTIVATED bracket take-profit leg (state flips held->new when its entry fills, orderClass stays 'bracket'/'oco'/'oto' per types.ts:939's comment) is neither excluded from listStaleLimitOrders NOR from the alert. src/lib/order-replacement.ts's autoRemediateStaleExitOrders (732-793) enqueues a cancel_requested row for every item in that list whose side is sell/cover and state!=='held' (line 756) — no orderClass check, no clientOrderId/provenance check — then stepReplacementState (300-480) cancels it and places a MARKET order (452-477) for the full remaining quantity. src/lib/broker-side.ts ALREADY has the exact tool needed and unused here: `isBracketOrderClass(orderClass)` (110-112) checks against BRACKET_ORDER_CLASSES=['bracket','oco','oto']. Separately (tsx-08): cancelWorkingOrder (src/lib/order-cancel.ts:121-213) — the shared console+mobile manual-cancel path — calls gateway.cancelEquityOrder (line 198) with NO broker_protective_stops bookkeeping; it never calls the existing cancelBrokerProtectiveStop (broker-protective-stops.ts:178) that DOES understand these rows. reconcileBrokerProtectiveStops's own tick (broker-protective-stops.ts:1092-1118) then sees the tracked order's now-canceled state, calls it 'stale_resting_row', deletes the local row (deleteBrokerProtectiveStop), and the placement loop at line 1343-1344 (`if (existing.has(sym)) continue;`) re-arms a fresh stop for the symbol within one tick — silently undoing the owner's explicit cancel, contradicting the cancel-sheet copy 'No new order is placed' at app/console/orders/cancel-sheet.tsx:87 and ios/SocraticTrade/OrderCancel.swift:125. NOTE: the cluster's root_cause paragraph mis-cites order-cancel.ts:198 itself as 'the protective-stop reconciler' — that line is just the cancel call; the actual re-place logic lives entirely in broker-protective-stops.ts. NOTE 2: ops-observability-admin:sre-12 (audit-only broker-declined-stop failures with no owner push, broker-protective-stops.ts:1542/1551/1588) does NOT share this cluster's root cause (auto-replace provenance) — it is a separate notification-gap defect that was mis-bundled by lane tag; recommend handling it as an independent S-effort item, not part of this plan.
plan.approach: 1) tsx-02 (AUTO cancel-replace must never touch a bracket leg or a non-app order): in order-replacement.ts's autoRemediateStaleExitOrders loop (~750-758), import `isBracketOrderClass` from './broker-side' and add, right after the existing `if (String(item.order.state...) === 'held') continue;`: `if (isBracketOrderClass(item.order.orderClass)) { out.deferred++; audit('stale_exit_auto_remediation_skipped_bracket_leg', {orderId: item.order.id, symbol, side, orderClass: item.order.orderClass}, userId, input.policy.connectedAccountId); continue; }` and `if (!item.order.clientOrderId) { out.deferred++; audit('stale_exit_auto_remediation_skipped_not_app_placed', {orderId: item.order.id, symbol, side}, userId, input.policy.connectedAccountId); continue; }` (our own placement always sets client_order_id=refId per alpaca.ts:746/674 and robinhood.ts:442 — absence means the owner placed it directly at the broker). Deliberately do NOT touch listStaleLimitOrders itself or replaceStaleLimitOrderWithMarket (order-replacement.ts:99-256, the owner-initiated manual replace) — an owner explicitly clicking 'replace with market' on their own resting take-profit leg is a legitimate intentional action, only the AUTOMATED 15-minutes-later path is the bug. 2) tsx-14 (misleading alert + audit spam on bracket legs): in stale-limit-orders.ts's notifyStaleLimitOrders loop (~66-68), broaden the existing suppression from `if (isHeldExitLeg(item.order)) continue;` to `if (isHeldExitLeg(item.order) || isBracketOrderClass(item.order.orderClass)) continue;` (isBracketOrderClass already imported for step 1) so an ACTIVATED bracket leg stops generating the 'cancel/reprice before replacing' push too. Route the per-tick 'stale_exit_auto_remediation_deferred' audit at order-replacement.ts:760-767 through `auditDeduped` (src/lib/audit-dedupe.ts:36, same pattern as broker-protective-stops.ts:76's auditStopSkipped) keyed by orderId so it fires once per streak instead of once per tick. 3) tsx-08 (owner-cancel of a managed stop must not be silently undone): in order-cancel.ts's cancelWorkingOrder, after the successful `await gateway.cancelEquityOrder(...)` at line 198, add: `const managedRow = listBrokerProtectiveStops(policy.accountNumber, userId).find(r => r.brokerOrderId === orderId); if (managedRow) { deleteBrokerProtectiveStop(managedRow.id, userId); setInternalSetting(ownerCancelledStopKey(userId, policy.accountNumber, managedRow.symbol), JSON.stringify({ at: new Date().toISOString(), positionQuantity: lookup.order ? undefined : undefined /* see below */ })); }` — capture the pre-cancel position quantity from `lookupCancelContext`'s already-fetched positions (thread it through CancelLookup as an optional `positionQuantity`) so the marker can self-invalidate on a real quantity change. Add `ownerCancelledStopKey(userId, accountNumber, symbol)` as a small exported helper (order-cancel.ts or db-settings.ts). In broker-protective-stops.ts's placement loop (~1343-1344), before `if (existing.has(sym)) continue;`, add: `const suppress = getInternalSetting<string>(ownerCancelledStopKey(userId, accountNumber, sym)); if (suppress) { const marker = JSON.parse(suppress) as {positionQuantity?: number}; if (marker.positionQuantity === undefined || Math.abs(marker.positionQuantity - pos.quantity) < POSITION_EPSILON) continue; /* still the same position the owner cancelled for; leave it stop-less */ /* else: quantity changed (partial exit/re-entry) — clear the marker, fall through to place fresh protection */ }`. Return `{...result, managedStopSuppressed: Boolean(managedRow)}` from cancelWorkingOrder so callers can vary copy. 4) Conditional copy: in app/console/orders/cancel-sheet.tsx and ios/SocraticTrade/OrderCancel.swift, detect a managed stop client-side via `order.clientOrderId?.startsWith('protstop-')` (the broker echoes back exactly this prefix per broker-protective-stops.ts:1506/1559) and swap the 'No new order is placed' sentence for 'This is an app-managed protective stop. It will not be re-placed automatically unless the position changes or you re-enable protection.'
tests: test/stale-limit-orders.test.ts — extend the existing 'alerts a bracket exit leg once it activates' fixture (line ~76) with `orderClass: 'bracket'` on the activated-and-stale order and add a NEW assertion `expect(listStaleLimitOrders([...], {staleLimitOrderMinutes:15}, now)).toEqual([])` when orderClass is bracket-family — mirrors the existing held-leg suppression test. This specific assertion FAILS today (bracket-class activated legs are still listed) and PASSES after notifyStaleLimitOrders's isBracketOrderClass check (note: only the alert-suppression call, not listStaleLimitOrders itself, changes — write the new assertion against notifyStaleLimitOrders's alerted count, not listStaleLimitOrders's raw listing).

NEW test in a file adjacent to order-replacement.test.ts (e.g. add to that file): construct a stale sell limit order with `orderClass: 'bracket'`, call autoRemediateStaleExitOrders, assert `out.attempted === 0` and no row was inserted into order_replacements for that orderId (query order_replacements directly). FAILS today (the bracket leg is enqueued and cancel-replaced); PASSES after the orderClass/clientOrderId guard.

NEW test: cancel a broker_protective_stops-tracked order via cancelWorkingOrder, then call reconcileBrokerProtectiveStops for the same symbol/position (unchanged quantity) and assert NO new broker order was placed (placed counter stays 0) and the position row remains stop-less. FAILS today (the stop is silently re-placed within the same tick); PASSES after the suppression marker.
plan.risks: test/order-replacement.test.ts (856+ region) and test/broker-protective-stops.test.ts pin a lot of existing cancel/replace/reconcile behavior with `order()`/fixture helpers that likely omit orderClass and clientOrderId by default (undefined) — verify the new guards don't accidentally exclude those fixtures' intended-eligible orders (undefined clientOrderId would now be treated as 'not app-placed' and skip auto-remediation; if any existing test relies on auto-remediation firing for a fixture with no clientOrderId set, it will need `clientOrderId: 'some-ref'` added). isBracketOrderClass(undefined) correctly returns false (typeof check), so untagged fixtures are unaffected by that half. The position-quantity-fingerprint marker in broker-protective-stops.ts needs care: getInternalSetting/setInternalSetting are unscoped by connectedAccountId today for other similar markers in this file (mirror the existing hwmKey/sodKey-style key construction exactly) — do not invent a new keying convention. sre-12 is explicitly OUT of this plan's diff.

clusters.title: Quote pipeline fabricates asOf and picks the wrong field as price, defeating the staleness gate
clusters.root_cause: Values that were not just observed are stamped with the wall clock: src/lib/data-providers.ts:1571-1590 takeScalar writes cascadeFetchedAt = new Date().toISOString() for any field lacking its own asOf, so a 6h-cached nasdaq-quote volume wins recency arbitration at src/lib/evidence-facts.ts:132-155 and overwrites base.volume; src/lib/market.ts:1548 (Yahoo quote-only) and src/lib/quotes-cascade.ts:397 (ROIC profile price) hardcode asOf: new Date(), so policy.ts:404-413's opening-order staleness gate always reads ~0s old; and src/lib/alpaca.ts:551-569 returns the ASK as price, which becomes the displayed price, watchlist price, alert trigger and stop mark.
clusters.one_change: Make asOf non-forgeable — carry the provider's own observation timestamp (or leave it undefined, which src/lib/quotes-cascade.ts:47-61 already treats as not-fresh) through takeScalar, toQuoteOnlyMarketQuote and the ROIC/CBOE/VWAP tiers, use mid/last instead of ask at alpaca.ts:551, and surface the resulting age in the drilldown, watchlist and scan chips.

plan.summary: Confirmed the core defect at all three cited anchors. (1) src/lib/data-providers.ts's takeScalar (~1560-1590): `asOf = supplied?.asOf ?? currentRecord?.fieldDates?.[field] ?? ... ?? cascadeFetchedAt` where `cascadeFetchedAt = new Date().toISOString()` (line 1534) — any provider field lacking its own timestamp (e.g. parseNasdaqQuoteInfo's price/change/volume, cached 6h under generic ttlMs()) gets stamped as observed 'now'. evidence-facts.ts's arbitrateFieldObservation (100-155) is recency-first for volume, so a 6h-stale cached value with a fabricated 'now' timestamp wins over a genuinely fresh Alpaca dailyBar.v. (2) src/lib/market.ts's toQuoteOnlyMarketQuote (1523-1528) hardcodes `asOf: new Date().toISOString()` even though `quote.asOf` (YahooFinanceQuote.asOf, yahoo-finance.ts:76-77 — derived from the REAL `meta.regularMarketTime`) is already computed and sitting unused on the same object. src/lib/quotes-cascade.ts:397 (ROIC profile price) does the identical `asOf: new Date().toISOString()`. This directly defeats policy.ts's opening-order staleness gate (395-413) and quotes-cascade.ts's isQuoteFresh/quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate (52-88), both of which ALREADY treat a missing/undefined asOf as stale/missing (`if (!quote.asOf) return false` / `missing: true`) — so simply not fabricating a value is the fix, not new gate logic. (3) src/lib/alpaca.ts's getEquityQuotes (~548-556) sets `price: ask ?? bid ?? 0` — confirmed verbatim — which becomes the displayed Price, watchlist price, alert-trigger price, and stop/take-profit mark app-wide (mergeQuoteData, watchlist page, price alerts, currentPricesFromScan), while intradayChangePct stays computed off a different source. The remaining 6 members (mdi-06/07/09/16/17/18) are independently confirmed via this session's read of the register's verify_notes (each cites a specific unread-field or unsafe-parse defect) but were not re-derived from source in this pass; treat those six as lower-confidence-but-plausible until spot-checked, and sequence them after the three P1/P2 anchors.
plan.approach: PRIMARY (do first, highest leverage): (a) market.ts:1523-1528 toQuoteOnlyMarketQuote — change `asOf: new Date().toISOString()` to `asOf: quote.asOf` (already on YahooFinanceQuote; undefined when Yahoo gave no regularMarketTime, which correctly falls through to isQuoteFresh's existing 'missing -> stale' branch). (b) quotes-cascade.ts:397 ROIC profile block — same swap: drop the fabricated `new Date().toISOString()`; if ROIC's response has no timestamp field, leave `asOf: undefined` rather than inventing one (checked: `isQuoteFresh` already handles undefined asOf as not-fresh, so downstream `if (isQuoteFresh(q, nowMs, maxAgeMs)) result[symbol] = q;` naturally excludes it — matches existing intent, just currently defeated by the fabrication). (c) alpaca.ts:548-556 getEquityQuotes — change `price: ask ?? bid ?? 0` to a real mid: `price: (typeof bid === 'number' && typeof ask === 'number') ? (bid + ask) / 2 : ask ?? bid ?? 0`, keep bid/ask on the BrokerQuote object unchanged (already present) so tooltips can still show ask/bid explicitly; do NOT touch intradayChangePct here (out of scope — that's computed elsewhere from prevClose, already tracked separately per mdi-05's own note). SECONDARY (data-providers.ts takeScalar, mdi-03 — larger, needs its own care because 20+ providers funnel through this one function): stop defaulting `fetchedAt`/`asOf` to `cascadeFetchedAt` for FIELDS that came from a cache write with no observation timestamp of their own — instead, when a provider's raw parse (e.g. parseNasdaqQuoteInfo) does not itself carry a timestamp, store `undefined` for that field's `asOf` (keep `fetchedAt: cascadeFetchedAt` — that one IS honestly 'when we fetched the cache entry', just not 'when the underlying value was true') and update evidence-facts.ts's `recency()` metric (114-119, already reads `asOf ?? observedAt ?? effectiveAt ?? fetchedAt`) to NOT fall through to fetchedAt for the volume/price-family fields specifically, or give those fields an explicit lowest-recency floor when asOf is absent, so a same-priority-tier candidate with a real asOf always outranks one with none. Give nasdaq-quote's price-family fields (lastSalePrice/percentageChange/volume) a short dedicated TTL cache bucket instead of sharing NEWS_CACHE_TTL_MS (6h) — new constant e.g. `NASDAQ_QUOTE_TTL_MS = 30_000` alongside the existing ALPACA_SNAPSHOT-style short TTL pattern already used elsewhere in this file. THEN (batch, lower priority — S effort each, execute per the register's already-verified line targets): mdi-06 pass `grouped.date` through to mergeGroupedBarData (currently only `grouped.bars` reaches it at app/api/scan/route.ts:110) and stamp VWAP's asOf from that date, not fetchedAt; mdi-07 guard symbol-drilldown.tsx:511's `new Date(view.asOf)` with a Date.parse check and stop persisting the Nasdaq sentence string as MarketQuote.asOf in market.ts's toMarketQuote; mdi-09 add a distinct `averageVolume` field alongside `volume` (do not let Robinhood's average-volume preference populate `volume` at data-providers.ts:2143); mdi-16 add `cached`/`source`/oldest-quote-asOf to MarketScanResponse and ios/SocraticTrade/ScanView.swift's subtitle; mdi-17 render `<Ago iso={quote.asOf}/>` plus % change on app/console/watchlist/page.tsx:253 (WatchlistQuote.asOf already exists on the type, just unrendered); mdi-18 convert alpaca.ts:569's `String(bar.time)` to a real ISO via the existing toBusinessDay-style helper and pass `bar.source` through instead of hardcoding 'yahoo-finance-delayed'.
tests: NEW unit test for market.ts's toQuoteOnlyMarketQuote: feed a YahooFinanceQuote with `asOf: '2026-08-15T14:00:00Z'` and a `now` several hours later; assert the returned MarketQuote.asOf equals the INPUT asOf (not a value close to `now`). FAILS today (asOf is always ~now); PASSES after the fix.

NEW unit test for quotes-cascade's isQuoteFresh/quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate integration: after the ROIC-block fix, assert a ROIC-sourced quote whose upstream gave no price timestamp is excluded from `result[symbol]` (i.e. `isQuoteFresh` returns false for it) rather than always passing. FAILS today (fabricated 'now' always passes); PASSES after removing the fabrication.

NEW unit test for alpaca.ts getEquityQuotes: mock getLatestQuotes returning `{bp: 199, ap: 201}`; assert `quotes[symbol].price === 200` (the mid), not 201 (the ask). FAILS today; PASSES after the mid-price change. Check existing tests asserting `price === ask` for this function first (grep test/*.ts for getEquityQuotes) and update them — they currently pin the ask-as-price bug.
plan.risks: policy.ts's staleness gate (395-413) and any other consumer of MarketQuote.asOf/BrokerQuote.asOf that currently relies on it always being a parseable recent timestamp (rather than sometimes undefined) needs auditing — grep for `new Date(quote.asOf)` / `Date.parse(...asOf)` call sites without a `quote.asOf &&` guard; the market.ts and quotes-cascade.ts fixes intentionally make asOf undefined more often, which is correct per isQuoteFresh's own contract but could newly surface a NaN-date bug in a caller that never expected undefined before. The alpaca.ts mid-price change affects any test asserting the current ask-as-price behavior (search test/*.ts for `getEquityQuotes` assertions on `.price`) — those pin the bug and must be updated, not left red. data-providers.ts's takeScalar is extremely high-fan-in (used by every enrichment provider); the mdi-03 change should land as its own careful S/M-scoped follow-up after the three P1/P2 anchors are verified in isolation, not bundled into the same PR — flagging this as a sequencing risk, not a reason to skip it.

clusters.title: Calendar-day freshness math freezes screener, OHLC and enrichment caches during live sessions
clusters.root_cause: Freshness is measured in calendar days, not trading sessions. src/lib/market-hours.ts:283-311 isWeekendOrHolidayClosureAhead returns true for the whole of Friday (and the whole day before any holiday), so expiresAtRespectingMarketClose pushes a 5-minute screener TTL to Monday's open — verified: a Fri 10:00 ET write expires Mon 09:30 ET. src/lib/history.ts:115-126 isBarSeriesFresh accepts a 3-calendar-day-old last bar, so a Monday write suppresses any refetch through Tuesday and Wednesday. The same module has no early-close calendar (market-hours.ts:35), and the universe/history cascades below it mix adjustment bases and a 2026-06-14 static index snapshot.
clusters.one_change: Replace the calendar-day helpers with a session-aware pair — extend TTL only after the session actually closes (src/lib/market-hours.ts:288/305) and measure bar freshness in elapsed sessions (src/lib/history.ts:115) — and add the half-day/early-close table the same module needs.

plan.summary: Verified both anchor functions directly. src/lib/market-hours.ts's isWeekendOrHolidayClosureAhead (288-292) is `if (!isEtCalendarTradingDay(today)) return true; return !isEtCalendarTradingDay(addEtCalendarDays(today, 1));` — for ANY time on a Friday, today IS a trading day (first branch false) but tomorrow (Saturday) is not, so this returns true for the ENTIRE Friday session, not just after close. expiresAtRespectingMarketClose (305-311) then extends any cache write made at any point on Friday to `nextMarketOpenStrictlyAfterMs` = Monday 09:30 ET, freezing 5-minute screener TTLs, OHLC caches, and 6h enrichment caches through what should be a fully live trading day (and identically the day before any holiday). src/lib/history.ts's isBarSeriesFresh (115-124) computes `ageMs = now - lastBarMs; return ageMs <= maxStalenessDays * 24h` with a default of 3 CALENDAR days; called at history.ts:241 to gate the local-cache short-circuit for fetchDailyOHLC. A Monday-written last bar stays 'fresh' (<=72h) through Tuesday and Wednesday, so a same-day PARTIAL bar persisted as if it were an EOD close (persistEodBarsToCache has no partial/EOD distinction) suppresses refetch for up to two full missed sessions. market-hours.ts additionally has NO early-close/half-day table at all (`const CLOSE = 16*60` in currentMarketSession is a single hardcoded constant with no per-date override, and getMarketHolidays only models FULL closures) — so on the ~4 NYSE half-days/year (day after Thanksgiving, Christmas Eve, July 3 when a weekday), currentMarketSession keeps reporting 'regular' until 4pm even though the exchange closed at 1pm, and the same TTL-extension logic reads the wrong close boundary. The cluster's other 4 listed members (mdi-08 universe security-type filter, mdi-11 adjustment-basis tagging, mdi-11 corporate-action splicing, mdi-12 Yahoo v7 crumb, mdi-15 static S&P 500 snapshot) do NOT share this cluster's 'calendar-day-vs-trading-session' root cause — they are independent market-data-integrity defects bundled in by lane tag only; excluded from this plan's diff and listed as separate follow-ups.
plan.approach: 1) market-hours.ts: replace isWeekendOrHolidayClosureAhead's calendar-day check with a session-boundary check. Add `const MARKET_CLOSE_HOUR_ET = 16; const MARKET_CLOSE_MINUTE_ET = 0;` (mirroring the existing MARKET_OPEN_HOUR_ET/MINUTE_ET at line 263) and an early-close table `const EARLY_CLOSE_DATES: Record<string, {hour:number;minute:number}> = {}` populated per-year the same way getMarketHolidays (113) builds its holiday set (day-after-Thanksgiving = 4th Thursday of Nov + 1 day; Christmas Eve = Dec 24 when a weekday; July 3 when a weekday and not itself a holiday) — export a `getEarlyCloses(year)` alongside the existing `getMarketHolidays(year)`. Rewrite isWeekendOrHolidayClosureAhead(nowMs) to: compute `todayParts = etDateParts(new Date(nowMs))`; if `!isEtCalendarTradingDay(todayParts)` return true (unchanged, correct); else compute today's actual close instant via `etWallClockToUtcMs(todayParts, closeHourFor(todayParts), closeMinuteFor(todayParts))` where closeHourFor/closeMinuteFor consult EARLY_CLOSE_DATES for today's Y-M-D key, defaulting to MARKET_CLOSE_HOUR_ET/MINUTE_ET; if `nowMs < todayCloseMs` return false (today's session hasn't ended yet — do NOT extend, a normal-TTL refetch is correct and desired); else (today's session has ended) fall through to the existing `!isEtCalendarTradingDay(addEtCalendarDays(todayParts, 1))` check unchanged. Also apply EARLY_CLOSE_DATES to currentMarketSession's hardcoded `CLOSE = 16*60` (8-60) so half-days correctly read 'closed' 13:00-16:00 ET (mdi-10) — thread the date through the existing Intl.DateTimeFormat parts already computed there. 2) history.ts: replace isBarSeriesFresh's flat 3-calendar-day window with a trading-session-aware check. New contract: `isBarSeriesFresh(bars, now)` (drop the maxStalenessDays parameter — a raw day-count no longer means anything) returns true only when the last bar's calendar date is >= the most recently EXPECTED complete trading session's date, computed as: if today (from `now`) is a trading day AND the session has closed (reuse the same close-time logic added to market-hours.ts above), expected date = today; else expected date = the previous trading day (reuse/extend market-hours.ts's existing previousTradingDayStart). Import `isTradingDay`/`previousTradingDayStart` from market-hours.ts rather than duplicating calendar logic in history.ts. Update the call site at history.ts:241 to drop the now-removed `3` argument.
tests: NEW test in a market-hours test file: `isWeekendOrHolidayClosureAhead` (or the exported `expiresAtRespectingMarketClose` it feeds) called with a Friday 2026-08-21T14:30:00Z (10:00 ET) and a 5-minute baseTtlMs — assert `expiresAtRespectingMarketClose(...)` returns `nowMs + 5*60_000` (the naive expiry), NOT Monday 09:30 ET. FAILS today (register verified: expires 2026-08-24T13:30Z); PASSES after the close-time gate.
Same function called with a Friday 2026-08-21T21:00:00Z (17:00 ET, after close) — assert it DOES extend to Monday open (the genuine weekend-closure case must still work).

NEW test for isBarSeriesFresh: build a bars array whose last bar is dated Monday, call with `now` = Wednesday same week (no early close/holiday between) — assert `isBarSeriesFresh` returns false (stale — Tuesday's session bar is missing) where the OLD 3-day-window version returned true. FAILS today; PASSES after the session-aware rewrite.

NEW test for getEarlyCloses/currentMarketSession: `currentMarketSession(new Date('2026-11-27T18:30:00Z'))` (13:30 ET, day after Thanksgiving) should return 'closed' or 'post', not 'regular' — the register's own tsx probe confirms today's code returns 'regular'.
plan.risks: expiresAtRespectingMarketClose and isBarSeriesFresh are both hot, widely-called cache-freshness primitives (screener, OHLC, enrichment, universe caches per mdi-01's evidence) — a mis-implemented close-time comparison could flip from 'never extends' (worse: burns provider quota every tick on weekends, the original bug this function was written to fix) to 'always extends' (reintroducing mdi-01) if the early-close/close-hour math has an off-by-one. Test both directions explicitly (Friday morning must NOT extend; Friday evening MUST extend) before landing. isBarSeriesFresh's signature change (dropping maxStalenessDays) is a breaking change to its exported contract — grep all callers (only history.ts:241 found in this pass, but re-grep before landing) and check test/*.ts files that call it directly with an explicit day count, which will need updating to the new signature.

clusters.title: Day P&L reads $0.00 and shorts mint phantom deposits: flows are inferred, not read, and the day is not the trading day
clusters.root_cause: app/console/lib/derive.ts:443 calls inferExternalCashFlows([baseline, fakeCurrent], []) with a hardcoded empty fill list, so on any day the strategy trades directionally tradeCash is 0 (src/lib/cash-flows.ts:157-164), the guard at :187-208 sets flow = deltaEquity, and Home prints exactly $0.00 (0.00%). src/lib/cash-flows.ts:164 also gives short/cover the wrong cash sign, minting a 2x-notional phantom deposit per short. Day keys are UTC (cash-flows.ts:33/129-142) while owner timestamps are Central, the risk-breaker HWM is UTC and not flow-adjusted (src/lib/risk-breaker.ts:86) and daily caps roll at NY midnight (src/lib/db-execution.ts:15). The broker's own equity/cash-activity ledger is implemented but unwired (src/lib/alpaca-account-insights.ts:167).
clusters.one_change: Make the broker cash-activity ledger the flow source — wire src/lib/alpaca-account-insights.ts:167 into the dashboard and benchmark paths — and keep inference only as a labeled fallback with the short/cover sign, the real fill list and one shared Central trading-day helper reused by risk-breaker.ts:86 and db-execution.ts:15.

plan.summary: Confirmed the core defects. deriveDayPnl (app/console/lib/derive.ts:416-454) has NO fills parameter in its signature at all, and its only caller (app/console/page.tsx:62) passes none — so line 443's `inferExternalCashFlows([baseline, fakeCurrent], [])` hardcodes an empty fill list on every call; whenever the strategy trades directionally that day, tradeCash computes to 0 inside cash-flows.ts's loop (140-165, since sortedFills is always []), the missing-fill guard at cash-flows.ts:187-208 treats the whole equity delta as a transfer or zeroes it out, and Day P&L can print exactly $0.00. Confirmed the short/cover sign bug precisely: cash-flows.ts:164 `tradeCash += f.side === 'sell' || f.side === 'cover' ? f.notional : -f.notional;` — a SHORT should INCREASE cash (broker credits short-sale proceeds) but falls into the else branch (-notional, wrong sign), and a COVER should DECREASE cash (buying back) but is grouped with 'sell' (+notional, wrong sign) — BOTH are backwards, and since `flow = deltaCash - tradeCash`, an understated-by-2x tradeCash for a short overstates flow by exactly 2x notional, minting the phantom-deposit effect described. Confirmed `fetchAlpacaAccountActivities` (src/lib/alpaca-account-insights.ts:209-230, wraps GET /v2/account/activities — Alpaca's own cash-activity/transfer ledger) has ZERO consumers anywhere in src/ or app/ (grep confirmed) — genuinely unwired as claimed. Confirmed risk-breaker.ts:82 `const day = now.toISOString().slice(0, 10);` is a raw UTC calendar day — a THIRD, ad hoc day boundary alongside cash-flows.ts/derive.ts's Central-Time display boundary (app/console/lib/format.ts's startOfCentralDay, whose own comment explicitly documents it as a client-safe DUPLICATE of db-execution.ts's `startOfDayInTimeZone`, 'not imported since that module pulls in better-sqlite3') and db-execution.ts's DAILY_RESET_TIME_ZONE='America/New_York' boundary already used for daily notional caps (db-execution.ts:15/18). The UTC boundary in risk-breaker.ts is not a deliberate choice — it's the only one of the three that matches nothing else in the app.
plan.approach: 1) SIGN FIX (smallest, highest-confidence, do first): cash-flows.ts:164 — change `f.side === 'sell' || f.side === 'cover' ? f.notional : -f.notional` to `f.side === 'sell' || f.side === 'short' ? f.notional : -f.notional` (short and sell both increase cash; buy and cover both decrease it — cover now correctly falls to the else/-notional branch). 2) REAL FILLS instead of []: give deriveDayPnl a `fills: FillEvent[]` parameter (app/console/lib/derive.ts:416-421 signature), pass real same-day fills at line 443 instead of `[]`. Thread this from the caller: app/console/page.tsx:62 needs a fills list scoped to [baseline.timestamp, now] — add a small server-side query (new function in src/lib/db-fills.ts, e.g. `listFillsSince(accountNumber, source, sinceIso, userId)`, a thin wrapper filtering the account's fills by filledAt >= sinceIso) exposed through the dashboard snapshot (src/lib/dashboard.ts's computeDashboardSnapshot, ~343+) as e.g. `snapshot.recentFillsForDayPnl`, and pass that array into deriveDayPnl at page.tsx:62. 3) PRIMARY SOURCE per the register's own recommendation — wire the broker's own ledger ahead of inference: in dashboard.ts (or a new small helper module), call `fetchAlpacaAccountActivities(userId, { activityTypes: ['CSD','CSW','ACATC','ACATS','FEE','DIV'] })` (deposit/withdrawal/transfer/fee/dividend activity types) for the account's active period, sum net_amount for transfer-class activities into a `brokerReportedFlow` figure, and have deriveDayPnl prefer `brokerReportedFlow` when present/non-Alpaca-account-agnostic-empty, falling back to the (now-fixed) fills-based inference only when the broker ledger call fails or returns nothing (non-Alpaca brokers). Label which source won on the DayPnl result (`cashFlowAdjusted: 'broker-ledger' | 'inferred' | false`) so the UI can show an honest provenance chip instead of a bare number. 4) DAY BOUNDARY: fix risk-breaker.ts's day-key bug specifically — change `const day = now.toISOString().slice(0, 10);` (risk-breaker.ts:82) to reuse db-execution.ts's already-exported `startOfDayInTimeZone(now, DAILY_RESET_TIME_ZONE)` (NY time, matching the SAME boundary the daily notional cap already uses, so a fill straddling midnight UTC is graded against the identical 'day' both systems agree on) — import `{ startOfDayInTimeZone, DAILY_RESET_TIME_ZONE }` from './db-execution' and derive the day key from that Date's ISO date portion instead of the raw `now`. Do NOT change cash-flows.ts/derive.ts's Central-Time display boundary (startOfCentralDay) in this pass — that is a deliberate, documented, owner-directed DISPLAY convention (distinct concept from the exchange's own trading-session boundary); flag full three-way unification as a separate product decision requiring an explicit owner call, not silently bundled into this correctness fix.
tests: NEW unit test in test/cash-flows.test.ts (or wherever cash-flows tests live): construct two equity-curve points with a SHORT fill of notional 1000 between them and no external transfer; assert `inferExternalCashFlows(...)` returns an EMPTY flow map (or a flow within materiality threshold of 0), not a ~2000 phantom deposit. FAILS today (short's wrong sign mints a 2x-notional flow); PASSES after the sign fix.

NEW test for deriveDayPnl: pass a real fills array containing one directional buy fill between baseline and now, plus a portfolio.cash delta consistent with ONLY that trade (no external transfer) — assert `pnl` reflects the mark-to-market move, not $0.00. FAILS today (deriveDayPnl has no fills param, so trade-driven cash movement is always misread as either a transfer or zeroed); PASSES once fills flow through.

NEW test for risk-breaker.ts: call recordAndEvaluateDrawdownBreaker with `now` set to 7:30pm CT (which is after UTC midnight the 'next' calendar day) on two consecutive calls representing the 'same' NY trading day; assert `startOfDayEquity` is NOT reset between them. FAILS today (UTC day-key rolls over mid-evening CT, resetting startOfDayEquity a day early); PASSES after switching to startOfDayInTimeZone(now, 'America/New_York').
plan.risks: deriveDayPnl and app/console/page.tsx are on the money-facing Home dashboard's most-viewed tile — any regression here is immediately visible to the owner. The broker-activities wiring (step 3) is the largest, riskiest piece (new external API call in the dashboard's parallel-fetch chain, needs a timeout/failure fallback so a slow/failed Alpaca activities call never blocks or breaks the dashboard — mirror the existing `Promise.race`/timeout pattern already used elsewhere in dashboard.ts) and should land as a separate PR after the sign-fix + fills-plumbing land and are verified; do not bundle all four steps into one commit. Existing tests likely pin the CURRENT `[]`-fills / UTC-day behavior — grep test/derive*.ts, test/cash-flows*.ts, and test/risk-breaker*.ts before changing signatures; any test asserting `flow === 0` purely because fills were empty (rather than because there truly was no transfer) needs its fixture updated to pass real fills. Robinhood/other non-Alpaca brokers have no equivalent activities endpoint wired — the fallback-to-inference path must stay fully functional for those accounts, not just Alpaca.

clusters.title: Realized-P&L ledger reads the oldest fills and mismatches lots, so P&L, win rate, tax and wash-sale locks are wrong
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/db-fills.ts:332 is SELECT ... ORDER BY filled_at ASC LIMIT ? — the OLDEST N rows — while the sibling listPortfolioSnapshots (db-fills.ts:221-243) was already fixed to a newest-DESC subquery for this exact bug; all 16 callers pass 500 and src/lib/strategy-tuning.ts:418 passes 30, so the paid tuner's "recentFills" are provably the account's first 20 fills. The matcher on top is also wrong: closes with no app lot are silently dropped (src/lib/performance.ts:599), a lot is graded on its first partial exit only (src/lib/outcome-engine.ts:966), partial closes count as round trips (performance.ts:1707), short-side lots are skipped in tax (src/lib/tax.ts:352), a synthetic 20bps haircut is applied to real fills (performance.ts:244), and FillEvent carries no fees.
clusters.one_change: Fix the read to the newest-DESC subquery already used at db-fills.ts:221-243 and make the lot matcher round-trip aware in src/lib/performance.ts:599-1707 (group partials per lot, book unmatched closes into an explicit pre-app bucket, include short lots in tax, drop the synthetic haircut).

plan.summary: Confirmed the primary defect precisely. src/lib/db-fills.ts's listFillEvents (329-337) is `ORDER BY filled_at ASC LIMIT ?` — with the sibling listPortfolioSnapshots (221-243) already fixed for this exact class of bug via a newest-DESC-subquery-then-ASC pattern (documented inline: 'ASC+LIMIT previously kept the OLDEST slice and dropped recent equity'), listFillEvents was never given the same fix. Confirmed 18 call sites across the codebase pass `limit=500` (dashboard.ts:675-676, experience-memory.ts:263, outcome-engine.ts:964, performance.ts:460-493, robinhood-pnl-crosscheck.ts:60, strategy-tuning.ts:335/409-410/417-418, tax.ts:337, strategy.ts:824-825, app/api/llm-usage/model-stats/route.ts:58) and strategy-tuning.ts:418 passes 30 — every one of these is asking for 'the most recent N fills' but the SQL returns the OLDEST N once an account/source exceeds the limit. No existing test in test/*.ts exercises the >limit-rows case for listFillEvents (all fixtures use small counts), which is why this slipped through despite the sibling function's fix. Also confirmed the lot-matcher issues layered on top: performance.ts:591-599's FIFO closer breaks (drops) a closing fill with no matching same-side open lot with zero counter/audit (a real gap for pre-app/manual positions per db-fills.ts:405's own comment 'fill_events is not a complete ledger'); outcome-engine.ts:962-970's findRealizedLot does `closedLots.find(...)` (first match only) so a scaled-out position's decision grade is taken from the FIRST partial trim, not the round trip; performance.ts:1707-1710's winRate counts ClosedLots (one per closing fill against a lot) not round trips, so 2 profitable trims + 1 stopped-out remainder reads as 67% win rate on a losing trade; tax.ts:352 `if (lot.side !== 'long' || ...) continue;` drops every closed SHORT from short-term-realized/wash-sale detection; performance.ts:239-268's paper execution-cost model is applied inconsistently (not universally as originally summarized) — an immediately-known-price paper fill is booked cost-adjusted while a later-reconciled paper fill is overwritten with raw broker truth (strategy-execution.ts:1643-1647), so ONE account's realized P&L mixes shaded and raw prices; FillEvent (types.ts:2742) has no fee/commission/dividend field at all, so all P&L is gross of broker costs.
plan.approach: 1) PRIMARY, do first (fixes P&L/tax/tuning/experience-memory/dashboard/LLM-context all at once): rewrite listFillEvents (db-fills.ts:329-337) to the same newest-DESC-subquery pattern already proven at listPortfolioSnapshots (221-243): `SELECT * FROM (SELECT * FROM fill_events WHERE account_number = ? AND source = ? AND user_id = ? ORDER BY filled_at DESC LIMIT ?) newest ORDER BY filled_at ASC` (and the no-source variant identically). No caller signature changes needed — every one of the 18 call sites keeps working, just correctly. 2) Round-trip-aware grading (perf-09, S-effort once #1 lands): in outcome-engine.ts's findRealizedLot (962-970), instead of `closedLots.find(...)` (first match), collect ALL ClosedLots sharing the same `entryAt`, sum their `pnl`, and only treat the case as terminal once the summed closed quantity reaches the entry fill's quantity (compare against `entryFill.quantity`) — partial trims should keep the case open, not grade it early. 3) Round-trip win rate (perf-11, M-effort, larger — group before counting): add a `groupClosedLotsByRoundTrip(lots: ClosedLot[]): ClosedLot[][]` helper (key = entryAt + symbol + side, or an explicit entryRunId if ClosedLot carries one) in performance.ts, and change winRate (1707-1710) and the avg-return aggregator to operate on ONE synthetic aggregated-pnl entry per round trip (sum pnl across the group, mark won/lost by the group's summed pnl) rather than raw ClosedLots; update every UI copy that says 'n=' trades to reflect round trips, not lot-closes. 4) Unmatched-close visibility (perf-12, S-effort): in performance.ts's FIFO loop (~591-599), when `idx === -1` (no matching open lot), instead of a bare `break`, increment a counter (e.g. `unmatchedCloses++`) and push an audit-style entry to a new returned array `unmatchedClosingFills: FillEvent[]`; surface a 'N closing fills had no tracked opening lot (pre-app or manual position)' note on Results wherever the realized-P&L figure renders. 5) Short-side tax parity (perf-07, S-effort): tax.ts:352 and :305 — change `lot.side !== 'long'` guards to include `side === 'short'` lots in shortTermRealized/wash-sale detection (a closed short is always short-term regardless of holding period — do not attempt to apply a long-term rate to it). 6) Consistent paper cost model (perf-10, S-effort): performance.ts:239-268 — either book price = broker truth always and move the modeled haircut into a new `FillEvent.modeledCostBps` field consumed only by the learning loop's net-of-cost stats (keeps Realized P&L == broker-reported), or (simpler, smaller diff) apply the SAME cost-adjustment retroactively when strategy-execution.ts:1643-1647 later overwrites a reconciled fill's price, so every paper fill in an account is consistently either all-shaded or all-raw, never mixed. 7) Fees (perf-20, out of scope for this pass — flag as a separate M-effort follow-up requiring new broker-activity plumbing shared with the cash-flow-and-trading-day cluster's Alpaca-activities wiring; do not attempt inline here).
tests: NEW test in a fill-events test file: insert 501 fill_events rows for one account/source with strictly increasing filled_at timestamps, call `listFillEvents(accountNumber, source, 500, userId)`, assert the returned array's LAST element's `filledAt` equals the 501st (newest) inserted fill's filledAt, not the 500th-from-the-start. FAILS today (returns rows 1-500, i.e. the oldest, so the newest fill is absent); PASSES after the DESC-subquery fix. Mirror this pattern from any existing listPortfolioSnapshots regression test if one exists, else model it fresh.

NEW test for outcome-engine's findRealizedLot: build fills for one entry + two partial closing fills (a profitable trim, then a stopped-out remainder) sharing the same entryAt; assert the graded outcome's pnlUsd equals the SUM of both closes (net loss), not just the first trim's profit. FAILS today (find() returns only the first ClosedLot); PASSES after the aggregation fix.

NEW test for tax.ts: construct one closed SHORT lot with a loss; call the short-term-realized aggregator; assert it appears in shortTermRealized. FAILS today (side!=='long' skips it); PASSES after the guard fix.
plan.risks: The listFillEvents fix alone touches 18 call sites' EFFECTIVE data (not their code) — any test asserting a SPECIFIC ordering or exact subset of fills from a fixture with MORE than `limit` rows will change output; grep test/*.ts for fixtures inserting >500 (or >30 for strategy-tuning) fills before landing (none found in this pass, but re-check). The round-trip win-rate regrouping (step 3) changes a widely-displayed metric's NUMBER (not just its label) on Results/Home 'By thesis' tables — needs explicit product sign-off on the grouping key (entryAt+symbol+side vs an explicit run/episode id) since a wrong key could merge two genuinely separate round trips on the same symbol. The paper-cost-model consistency fix (step 6) changes historical-looking realized P&L for the paper book — confirm with the owner whether 'book broker truth always' (simpler, matches owner's 'an account is an account' framing — paper is a real broker account) is preferred over 'retroactively re-shade reconciled fills' before choosing a direction; recommend the former as the more owner-ruling-aligned default.

clusters.title: Performance tiles print numbers without the basis or window they were computed on
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/performance.ts:497 caps the "Versus the market" TWR at ~100 snapshots (≈7 trading days) while app/console/results/page.tsx frames it as account performance; "Realized/Unrealized P&L" means lot-ledger on Results, broker cost on Home and broker positions on iOS with no label on any of them (results/page.tsx:957-994); win rate 0% and avg return +0.00% render for accounts with zero closed lots; app/console/lib/derive.ts:804 divides by NET signed cost basis so shorts inflate the percentage; and performance.ts:1664 fabricates a $100 paper equity base that is rendered as money.
clusters.one_change: Attach an explicit basis + window label (and an em-dash empty state instead of 0%) to every performance figure at app/console/results/page.tsx:940-1000, ios/SocraticTrade/ResultsView.swift and app/console/lib/derive.ts:804, sourced from the same struct that computed the number.

plan.summary: Confirmed the core shape. app/console/results/page.tsx's BucketCard (940-1000) renders 'Realized P&L' / 'Unrealized P&L' / 'Win rate' / 'Avg return / closed capital' with a basis tooltip ONLY on the 'Avg return' field (title attribute at line ~975) — Realized and Unrealized carry no basis label at all, and per the register's independently-verified note, the THREE surfaces compute genuinely different numbers for the same nominal metric: Results' Unrealized comes from perf.liveUnrealizedPnl (calculatePnl over app-booked lots, performance.ts:640-660), Home's derive.ts:797-800 deriveMarkToMarket uses broker averageCost x quantity (a different basis), and iOS's ResultsView.swift AccountMetrics.displayedUnrealized prefers broker positions with a ledger fallback (MobileModels.swift:254-270) — a third basis. Confirmed performance.ts:497-498 `listPortfolioSnapshots(accountNumber, 'live', 100, userId)` caps the 'Versus the market' TWR window to ~100 snapshots (~7 trading sessions at the 60-min default run cadence, 2 snapshots/run) — but results/page.tsx:237 DOES already show `${startDate} -> ${endDate}` under the 'Your account' stat, so the window is disclosed as dates, just not NAMED as a bounded/accidental rolling window (register's verifier downgraded this to P2 on exactly this basis: 'what is missing is that it is an accidental rolling cap with a moving start, not a chosen window'). Confirmed win rate/avg-return render fabricated non-dash values (0% / +0.00%) for accounts with zero closed lots: results/page.tsx:957's `hasAny` gate is true for any account with equity-curve activity (nearly always true), and performance.ts:1707-1710's winRate/averageReturn both return 0 (not undefined) for an empty lot list; iOS's ResultsView.swift:71-84 has no gate at all. Confirmed derive.ts:804 `unrealizedPct: costBasis > 0 ? (unrealizedPnl / costBasis) * 100 : undefined` uses the NET SIGNED cost basis (shorts subtract from the sum), while the per-position row on the same page (positions.tsx:56-57) divides by `Math.abs(costBasis)` — inconsistent within one page. Confirmed performance.ts:1658-1666 fabricates `equity: 100 + realized` as a synthetic paper-curve base when paperSnapshots is empty, and results/page.tsx:985 renders it through the money-formatting EquityChart with no synthetic-data caveat. perf-19 (OOS backtest annualization bias, src/lib/backtest.ts) does NOT share this cluster's 'missing UI basis/window label' root cause — it is an admin-only (/api/admin/backtest-ic) statistical-methodology defect bundled in by lane tag only; excluded from this plan.

clusters.title: Identity resolution falls back to the owner instead of failing closed
clusters.root_cause: middleware.ts:385-388 sets trustedEmail = PRIMARY_EMAIL whenever isAuthConfigured() is false, and nothing asserts AUTH_SECRET in production — instrumentation.ts:47 asserts only ENCRYPTION_KEY — so a selective env regression makes every anonymous request the owner, with x-authenticated-user-email stamped at middleware.ts:420 and no route outside src/lib/auth/admin.ts checking identity provenance. The same shape repeats at src/lib/request-user.ts:28-34 (missing header → DEV_USER_ID 'local') and across 228 db functions that default userId="local" (src/lib/db-learning.ts:12); middleware.ts:435's matcher additionally skips any path ending in a static extension.
clusters.one_change: Assert AUTH_SECRET at boot when DB_BOOTSTRAP=live alongside the existing ENCRYPTION_KEY assert (instrumentation.ts:47), gate the middleware.ts:385 local fallback on that same production marker (the dev branch is pinned by ~20 tests, so add rather than remove), and drop the userId="local" defaults so a forgotten argument is a type error.

plan.summary: Confirmed all three cited mechanisms precisely, and confirmed the existing test suite's shape so the fix can be scoped to ADD a gate without breaking pinned dev/test behavior. middleware.ts:165-167 `isAuthConfigured()` returns `Boolean(process.env.AUTH_SECRET) || isFlagOn(process.env.CF_ACCESS_TRUST_EMAIL_HEADER)`. middleware.ts:384-388 (exact lines, confirmed): `if (!trustedEmail && !isAuthConfigured()) { trustedEmail = PRIMARY_EMAIL; identitySource = AUTHENTICATED_IDENTITY_SOURCES.localFallback; }` — this fallback fires for EVERY request whenever AUTH_SECRET is unset and CF Access trust is off, with NO check for whether this is a real production boot; a selective env regression (AUTH_SECRET dropped from Coolify/Infisical while the app otherwise boots fine) silently makes every anonymous request resolve as the owner (PRIMARY_EMAIL), forwarded via `x-authenticated-user-email` (line 420) to every route handler. instrumentation.ts's register() (9-50+) DOES already fail-fast-in-production for a missing/invalid ENCRYPTION_KEY via `assertEncryptionKeyConfiguredInProduction()` (db-api-keys.ts:103-111, gated on `env.NODE_ENV !== 'production' -> return`) but has NO equivalent assertion for AUTH_SECRET. Confirmed `DB_BOOTSTRAP === 'live'` is this codebase's established, more-precise 'this is really the live production deployment' signal (already used exactly this way at src/lib/r2-usage.ts:553, and set only by scripts/coolify-prod-start.sh:184 for the real Coolify boot) — a better gate than NODE_ENV alone since NODE_ENV=production can occur in build/CI/other contexts that are not the live server. Confirmed test/middleware-auth.test.ts's Test 4 ('no auth env (authConfigured=false) -> PRIMARY_EMAIL fallback (dev/test behavior)', line 478) and Test 5 (line 490) stub `AUTH_SECRET=''`/`CF_ACCESS_TRUST_EMAIL_HEADER=''` but do NOT stub NODE_ENV or DB_BOOTSTRAP — so gating the fallback on `DB_BOOTSTRAP === 'live'` leaves these (and the rest of the ~34-test file's dev-fallback-dependent tests) completely unaffected under vitest's default env. Confirmed src/lib/request-user.ts's resolveRequestUserFromEmail (28-31) falls back to `DEV_USER_ID` ('local') whenever the `x-authenticated-user-email` header is empty/missing/has-no-'@' — middleware ALWAYS explicitly sets this header (even to `''`) on every request it forwards (line 420), so in normal operation this only fires for the two intentional token-carveout branches (admin-token/bearer routes) or the local-fallback path above; the residual risk is a route reached WITHOUT going through middleware at all (a config.matcher gap, or a handler invoked directly in a future refactor) silently resolving as 'local'. The finding's broader recommendation to remove the `userId: string = "local"` default from all ~228 db-* functions (making a forgotten argument a compile error) is a real, large, separate mechanical refactor — NOT attempted in this plan; flagged as an explicit out-of-scope follow-up.
plan.approach: 1) Boot-time assertion (mirrors assertEncryptionKeyConfiguredInProduction's exact pattern): new small module src/lib/auth-secret-guard.ts exporting `export function assertAuthSecretConfiguredInProduction(env: NodeJS.ProcessEnv = process.env): void { if (env.DB_BOOTSTRAP !== 'live') return; if (env.AUTH_SECRET && env.AUTH_SECRET.trim().length > 0) return; if (isFlagOn(env.CF_ACCESS_TRUST_EMAIL_HEADER) && env.CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN?.trim() && env.CF_ACCESS_AUD?.trim()) return; throw new Error('AUTH_SECRET is missing in a live production boot (DB_BOOTSTRAP=live) and Cloudflare Access trust is not fully armed either. Refusing to boot: without a real identity source configured, every request would resolve as the owner via the dev/local fallback. Set AUTH_SECRET (or fully configure CF_ACCESS_TRUST_EMAIL_HEADER + CF_ACCESS_TEAM_DOMAIN + CF_ACCESS_AUD) before starting.'); }` (reuse/import the same `isFlagOn` helper middleware.ts already has, or duplicate the tiny predicate — check whether it's exported from middleware.ts first since middleware.ts is edge-runtime-only and this guard needs to run in instrumentation.ts's Node runtime). Call it in instrumentation.ts's register() (~47), immediately after the existing `assertEncryptionKeyConfiguredInProduction()` call, same style/position. 2) Middleware fallback gate (the core fix — one added condition): change middleware.ts:384-388's guard from `if (!trustedEmail && !isAuthConfigured())` to `if (!trustedEmail && !isAuthConfigured() && process.env.DB_BOOTSTRAP !== 'live')`. When DB_BOOTSTRAP==='live' and auth is unconfigured, trustedEmail stays null/empty and execution falls through unchanged to the existing final `else { fail closed: 401 for /api/*, redirect to /login otherwise }` branch (no other code path changes needed — the fail-closed branch already exists and already does the right thing, it's just unreachable today whenever the dev fallback fires first). 3) request-user.ts defense-in-depth: in resolveRequestUser (34-45), distinguish 'header explicitly present but empty' (the two legitimate token-carveout routes — must keep resolving to DEV_USER_ID, unchanged) from 'header genuinely absent' (request reached a handler without going through middleware's identity-setting path at all): check `request.headers.has(AUTHENTICATED_EMAIL_HEADER)` — if DB_BOOTSTRAP==='live' AND the header is entirely absent (not merely empty), throw a new small `UnauthenticatedRequestError` (401) instead of silently resolving to DEV_USER_ID; when the header IS present (even as ''), keep today's exact behavior unchanged. Callers of resolveRequestUser that don't already catch/convert errors to a 401 response need a check — grep call sites and confirm each API route already has error-boundary handling (most Next.js route handlers here throw straight through to a 500 today for unexpected errors, which is an acceptable fail-closed outcome even before adding a dedicated 401 mapping, but note it as a follow-up polish).
tests: NEW test in a new/adjacent instrumentation or auth-secret-guard test file: `assertAuthSecretConfiguredInProduction({DB_BOOTSTRAP:'live'})` (no AUTH_SECRET, no CF Access config) throws; `assertAuthSecretConfiguredInProduction({DB_BOOTSTRAP:'live', AUTH_SECRET:'x'})` does not throw; `assertAuthSecretConfiguredInProduction({DB_BOOTSTRAP:'fresh'})` (dev/non-live boot) does not throw regardless of AUTH_SECRET. FAILS today (function doesn't exist / instrumentation.ts never checks this); PASSES once added.

NEW test in test/middleware-auth.test.ts: `vi.stubEnv('DB_BOOTSTRAP','live'); vi.stubEnv('AUTH_SECRET',''); vi.stubEnv('CF_ACCESS_TRUST_EMAIL_HEADER','');` then call middleware() on `/api/dashboard` with no session cookie — assert `res.status === 401` (or redirect for a page route), NOT 200 with `x-authenticated-user-email` set to PRIMARY_EMAIL. FAILS today (the dev fallback fires unconditionally, returns 200 as the owner); PASSES after the DB_BOOTSTRAP gate. Explicitly re-run the file's existing Test 4/5 (lines 478, 490) UNCHANGED afterward and confirm they still pass (they don't stub DB_BOOTSTRAP, so they should be unaffected).

NEW test for request-user.ts: call `resolveRequestUser(request)` with DB_BOOTSTRAP='live' stubbed and a Request object that has NO `x-authenticated-user-email` header at all (not even empty) — assert it throws/refuses rather than returning `{userId: 'local'}`. FAILS today; PASSES after the has()-vs-empty distinction is added. Also assert the token-carveout case (header explicitly set to '') still resolves to DEV_USER_ID unchanged.
plan.risks: This is the highest blast-radius plan in the set — a wrong DB_BOOTSTRAP check in local/CI/Cursor-Cloud environments (which do NOT set DB_BOOTSTRAP at all) would leave the dev fallback fully intact there (DB_BOOTSTRAP undefined !== 'live'), which is exactly the desired outcome, but double-check the Coolify prod boot script (scripts/coolify-prod-start.sh:184) actually exports DB_BOOTSTRAP into the Next.js server process's env (not just a wrapper shell's env) before relying on it in middleware.ts's edge/node runtime — verify with `docker exec` or the ops-snapshot script rather than assuming. The ~34-test middleware-auth.test.ts suite and the two request-user.ts-adjacent test files must ALL be re-run green before landing (do not just add new tests — confirm zero regressions in the existing dev/test-fallback-dependent tests, since this is exactly the class of change the file's own header comment flags as security-critical: 'regression test for the NODE_ENV-edge-inlining IDOR bug'). The 228-call-site `userId="local"` default removal is explicitly NOT part of this plan — do not attempt it inline; it needs its own dedicated, carefully-tested PR given its size, per the owner's 'sole user today, no compat-shim churn' framing this should be sequenced behind, not ahead of, real product need.

clusters.title: Price alerts stop evaluating silently — no active account, one broker, swallowed errors, no age check
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/alerts.ts:67-69 returns [] whenever the console-active account has no accountNumber (zero connected accounts, or the active one was deleted — deleteConnectedAccount at src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1376 promotes nobody), even though PriceAlert rows are user-scoped; :73-78 catches any gateway throw in an empty catch with no log or audit, so a Public.com/eToro API error is indistinguishable from "nothing to check"; :83 acts on the price with no staleness check although quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate exists; and :17's SYMBOL_RE disagrees with isValidAppSymbol (src/lib/index-universes.ts:311), so malformed symbols sit armed forever. Zero tests cover the evaluation loop.
clusters.one_change: Switch checkPriceAlerts to the user-scoped fetchFreshQuotesCascade(symbols, userId) (src/lib/quotes-cascade.ts:149) instead of gateway.getEquityQuotes on the active account — this closes the no-account gate and the single-broker error in one edit — then log the caught error, apply quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate, share isValidAppSymbol, and add the evaluation tests.

plan.summary: checkPriceAlerts (src/lib/alerts.ts:63-116) gates on the console-active account's accountNumber, calls only that one broker gateway, swallows any gateway error into an empty result with no log/audit, applies no staleness check, and validates symbols with a looser regex than the rest of the app — confirmed exactly as described; premise holds.
plan.approach: In src/lib/alerts.ts: (1) delete `getBrokerGateway` import and the `accountNumber`/gateway-based quote fetch at lines 67-78; replace with `const policy = getPolicy(userId);` (still needed for sendNotification) plus `const quotes = await fetchFreshQuotesCascade(symbols, userId)` imported from './quotes-cascade' — this is USER-scoped (cascades across every connected broker plus Alpaca/Yahoo/ROIC fallbacks per its own doc comment at quotes-cascade.ts:132-148), so it works with zero, one, or many connected accounts and never needs an active account's accountNumber. (2) Wrap the cascade call's catch block to `console.error` and `audit("alert.check_error", { userId, symbols, error }, userId)` before returning `[]`, so a real provider outage is distinguishable from "nothing armed" in the audit trail (mirrors the pattern already used at quotes-cascade.ts:236-238 for its own internal levels). (3) Inside the per-alert loop (current lines 80-114), after resolving `quote = quotes[alert.symbol]`, call `quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate(quote, Date.now())` (imported from './quotes-cascade') and `continue` (skip, don't trigger) when `missing` or `ageSec > (policy.maxQuoteAgeSec ?? 120)` — mirrors the exact isStale formula at src/lib/policy.ts:413. (4) Delete the local `SYMBOL_RE` regex at line 17 and its use in `createAlert` (line 33); import and use `isValidAppSymbol` from './index-universes' instead, so an alert can never be armed on a symbol the rest of the app (watchlist/universe) would already reject.
tests: New test/price-alerts-evaluation.test.ts (file does not exist today — zero tests cover this loop): (a) 'triggers with zero connected accounts, using cascade market data alone' — seed a user with an armed alert and NO connected accounts, mock/stub fetchFreshQuotesCascade (or seed a real Yahoo-fallback-capable quote path per existing quotes-cascade test conventions) to return a hit price, call checkPriceAlerts, assert it is returned triggered — MUST FAIL today because alerts.ts:69 `if (!accountNumber) return [];` short-circuits before any quote lookup even runs.

(b) 'logs and audits a cascade failure instead of returning silently' — force fetchFreshQuotesCascade to reject, call checkPriceAlerts, assert an 'alert.check_error' audit row exists — MUST FAIL today because the empty catch at alerts.ts:76-78 has no audit/log call.

(c) 'does not trigger on a stale quote' — seed an armed alert whose threshold the quote crosses, but stamp the quote's asOf older than policy.maxQuoteAgeSec, assert the alert stays armed (not triggered) — MUST FAIL today because current code has no staleness check at all (line 83-86 acts on any numeric price regardless of age).

(d) 'rejects a symbol createAlert would reject elsewhere' — call createAlert with a symbol isValidAppSymbol rejects but the old SYMBOL_RE accepted (e.g. a leading-dot or double-dot string), assert { error: 'INVALID_SYMBOL' } — MUST FAIL today since the old regex accepts it.
plan.risks: fetchFreshQuotesCascade is heavier than a single gateway.getEquityQuotes call (it tries multiple providers in series) — checkAllUserPriceAlerts (alerts.ts:118-122) already runs per-user sequentially on a scheduler cadence, so latency grows modestly per user with armed alerts; acceptable since alerts already tolerate a several-second cascade elsewhere in the app. Tightening symbol validation via isValidAppSymbol is a behavior change for createAlert: it now allows digits (old regex disallowed them entirely) and rejects leading/double/trailing dots the old regex allowed — grep test/watchlist-alerts.test.ts and any other createAlert callers (chat-injection.test.ts, chat-orchestrator.test.ts, atlas-golden-eval.test.ts) before landing to confirm no test relies on a symbol shape isValidAppSymbol would now reject; the two existing watchlist-alerts.test.ts cases ('AAPL', '') are unaffected. No persisted-schema change — PriceAlert rows are untouched.

clusters.title: Account-scoped write paths have no guards: one click can arm Autopilot or reactivate a draining account
clusters.root_cause: importAccountSettings (src/lib/db-profiles.ts:895) strips only identity and user-level fields, so strategyAuthority copies through and a single "Import settings" click can flip a live account from Ask-first to Autopilot with none of the TypedConfirm ceremony app/console/guardrails/page.tsx:700 requires; applyProfileToAccount (db-profiles.ts:731) and activateStrategyProfile (:685) do not strip it at all. setActiveConnectedAccount (src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1323) never reads is_draining, and nothing ever clears the flag that deleteConnectedAccount sets at :1381, so a disconnected account can be re-loaded as the live target while the scheduler drains and purges it.
clusters.one_change: Treat strategyAuthority and is_draining as account-owned state in src/lib/db-profiles.ts:685/731/895 and src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1323 — preserve authority the way systemState already is, refuse or clear draining on activate and on re-upsert — and route any authority change through the existing typed-confirm gate.

plan.summary: Verified exactly as described. strategyAuthority is an account-level TradingPolicy field (not in USER_LEVEL_POLICY_FIELDS, src/lib/db-profiles.ts:21-48) so it flows unguarded through copyPolicyConfigToActiveAccount (:382-403, used by createStrategyProfile/updateStrategyProfile/activateStrategyProfile), applyProfileToAccount (:731-764), and importAccountSettings (:862-918) — all three preserve the target's systemState but none preserves strategyAuthority, so a saved profile or another account's settings can silently arm/disarm Autopilot with zero TypedConfirm ceremony. Separately, setActiveConnectedAccount (src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1323-1336) never checks is_draining, and deleteConnectedAccount (:1376-1384) never clears it or promotes another account, so a disconnected/draining account can be re-selected as the live target while the scheduler's drain sequence (scheduler.ts:850-881) is still cancelling its orders and about to purge it.
plan.approach: In src/lib/db-profiles.ts: (1) copyPolicyConfigToActiveAccount (:382-403) — change `const currentState = peekPolicy(userId, account.id).systemState;` to capture the whole current policy (`const current = peekPolicy(userId, account.id);`) and spread `strategyAuthority: current.strategyAuthority` alongside the existing `systemState: current.systemState` in the `policy:` object passed to writeAccountStrategyState (this single choke point fixes create/update/activateStrategyProfile in one edit, mirroring the existing systemState-preservation comment at :391-396). (2) applyProfileToAccount (:731-764) — change `const currentState = getPolicy(userId, connectedAccountId).systemState;` to `const current = getPolicy(userId, connectedAccountId);` and add `strategyAuthority: current.strategyAuthority` to the mergePolicy(...) call at :745-750 alongside the existing `systemState: currentState`. (3) importAccountSettings (:862-918) — change `const targetSystemState = peekPolicy(userId, targetConnectedAccountId).systemState;` to `const targetPolicy = peekPolicy(...)` and add `strategyAuthority: targetPolicy.strategyAuthority` to the mergePolicy(...) call at :896-901 alongside `systemState: targetSystemState`. No new TypedConfirm ceremony is added — the fix is that authority simply never travels through these three copy paths, so the ONLY way to change it stays the existing guardrails-page TypedConfirm flow (app/console/guardrails/page.tsx:700-725), consistent with the owner's 'no new blocking ceremony' rule. In src/lib/db-api-keys.ts: setActiveConnectedAccount (:1323-1336) — inside the existing db.transaction(), change the `exists` SELECT to also fetch `is_draining`, and throw `new Error("This account is disconnected and being wound down — it can no longer be made active.")` when `is_draining === 1`, before either UPDATE. The existing callers (app/api/connected-accounts/[id]/activate/route.ts:12-13 and src/lib/mobile-api.ts:979) already catch and surface any thrown Error as a 400, so this needs no new route-layer plumbing.
tests: test/copy-config-preserves-arming.test.ts — add a case mirroring the existing systemState pair (lines 17-53): active account's strategyAuthority is 'propose'; activate a library profile whose saved policy.strategyAuthority is 'decide'; assert db.getPolicy(u, acct).strategyAuthority stays 'propose' — MUST FAIL today (currently flips to 'decide').

test/settings-import.test.ts — add a case mirroring 'preserves the target's systemState' (lines 58-75): target's strategyAuthority is 'propose', source's is 'decide'; importAccountSettings(userId, source, target); assert result.strategyAuthority and db.getPolicy(userId, target).strategyAuthority are both 'propose' — MUST FAIL today.

New assertion (can live in a new test/set-active-connected-account-draining.test.ts or alongside persistence-notification.test.ts's existing 'missing-account' throw test at line 146): upsertConnectedAccount, deleteConnectedAccount(id) to mark it draining, then expect(() => setActiveConnectedAccount(id)).toThrow(/wound down|draining/i) — MUST FAIL today (currently succeeds and flips is_active=1 on a draining row).

Double-check src/lib/db-profiles.ts:150 (`isTieredWrite`) and any other reader of USER_LEVEL_POLICY_FIELDS is unaffected since strategyAuthority is not being added to that set, only explicitly re-pinned at three write sites. clusters.title: Bull strict JSON schema is invalid, so every OpenAI-family Green seat 400s before generation
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/strategy.ts:5870 declares exitPlan inside the Bull item's properties while BULL_PROPOSAL_REQUIRED_KEYS (strategy.ts:6653, used at :5851 for the required array) omits it, under additionalProperties:false — OpenAI strict mode requires required ⊇ properties, so any native-OpenAI or openai/* routed seat is rejected at the API layer 100% of the time (the fast 400 misdiagnosed as 'terra unservable' in #2831). The same file then trusts provider schema enforcement on json_object transports (strategy.ts:6115) where nothing enforces it.
clusters.one_change: Derive required from properties at src/lib/strategy.ts:5851 (or add exitPlan to BULL_PROPOSAL_REQUIRED_KEYS at :6653), add the invariant test that required ⊇ properties, and add a post-parse validator for the json_object transports.

[], ... }` block a few hundred lines after :6100, immediately following the successful-parse `try`): route `parsed.proposals` through the SAME per-item completeness predicate filterRepairedProposals already applies (key presence + type checks) before returning them, not only on the jsonrepair fallback path — so a json_object transport (DeepSeek, or a Gemini schema-translation fallback) that returns syntactically-valid but incomplete JSON gets its bad proposals dropped here too, instead of only when jsonrepair's error branch is hit.
