clusters.title: Run-scoped code re-resolves the console-active account instead of the account being traded
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/red-team.ts:192 calls getActiveConnectedAccount(userId) and :203 calls getStrategyPrompt(userId) with no account argument, even though debateProposal was handed runPolicy carrying the correct connectedAccountId — so with two accounts scheduled concurrently the adversarial reviewer can veto on the wrong venue's short capability and reason from another account's custom strategy prompt (deriveExecutionState at :196 has the same bug). src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:401 appends approved directives to the active account's prompt regardless of the pending row's account, and chat turns carry no account at all (src/lib/types.ts:3011) so the 10-turn replay mixes accounts.
clusters.one_change: Thread the owning connectedAccountId explicitly through src/lib/red-team.ts:192/196/203, src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:401 and the chat_turns row plus its replay window, and delete every getActiveConnectedAccount call from run-scoped paths.

plan.summary: Confirmed. debateProposal (src/lib/red-team.ts:177-233) resolves `activeAccount = getActiveConnectedAccount(userId)` (:192) and `basePrompt = getStrategyPrompt(userId)` (:203, no account arg) even though its caller (strategy.ts:2516) already passes the run-scoped `runPolicy` carrying the correct connectedAccountId as `policyOverride`; `deriveExecutionState(policy, activeAccount)` at :202 inherits the same wrong-account activeAccount. src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:401-403 (applyApprovedPending, strategy-directive tier) calls getStrategyPrompt(pending.userId) / setStrategyPrompt(merged, pending.userId) with no account arg despite pending.connectedAccountId being available and used two branches later (:427-428) — both silently resolve to whatever account is currently 'active' in the console (resolveAccount's getActiveConnectedAccount fallback, db-profiles.ts:323-326), not the account the directive was approved for. src/lib/types.ts's ChatTurn (:3011-3025) and the chat_turns table (db.ts:3970-3980) carry no account column at all, and app/chat/orchestrator.ts:143 (`listTurns(userId, 10)`) and its two appendTurn call sites (:148, :479-485) are unfiltered by the connectedAccountId already resolved at :123 — so switching the active account mid-conversation replays the WRONG account's prior turns into the new account's context.
plan.approach: (1) src/lib/red-team.ts: add `getConnectedAccount` to the existing `import { getActiveConnectedAccount, getPolicy, getStrategyPrompt } from "./db";` (line 18). Change :192 `const activeAccount = getActiveConnectedAccount(userId);` to `const activeAccount = policy.connectedAccountId ? getConnectedAccount(policy.connectedAccountId, userId) : getActiveConnectedAccount(userId);`. Change :203 `const basePrompt = getStrategyPrompt(userId);` to `const basePrompt = getStrategyPrompt(userId, policy.connectedAccountId);` (getStrategyPrompt already accepts an optional connectedAccountId, db-profiles.ts:602). This automatically fixes deriveExecutionState at :202 too since it consumes the same corrected `activeAccount`. The `policy` variable already resolves to `policyOverride ?? getPolicy(userId)` (:191) so this is a pure account-resolution fix with no signature change. (2) src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:401-403 — change to `const current = getStrategyPrompt(pending.userId, pending.connectedAccountId ?? undefined); const merged = mergeStrategyDirectiveBlock(current, pending.id, pending.value, assertedAt); setStrategyPrompt(merged, pending.userId, pending.connectedAccountId ?? undefined);` — both functions already accept the optional 3rd arg (db-profiles.ts:602, :611); when pending.connectedAccountId is null (a general/user-level directive) this preserves today's exact behavior (falls back to getActiveConnectedAccount via resolveAccount, db-profiles.ts:323-326). (3) Add `connectedAccountId?: string | null;` to ChatTurn (src/lib/types.ts, after `clientTurnId` around :3023). Add a new versioned migration (src/lib/db.ts, version 85, following the v84 pattern at :3134-3151) that ALTERs `chat_turns` adding a nullable `connected_account_id TEXT` column (existing rows get NULL — meaning pre-migration/unattributed, not 'no account'). In src/lib/db-api-keys.ts: RawChatTurnRow (:1908-1919) gains `connected_account_id: string | null`; mapChatTurn (:1921-1942) maps it to `connectedAccountId: row.connected_account_id ?? null`; insertChatTurn (:1944-1951) writes `turn.connectedAccountId ?? null` as a new bound param; listChatTurns (:1961-1967) gains an optional `connectedAccountId?: string | null` 3rd param and, when it is a defined string, filters `WHERE user_id = ? AND (connected_account_id = ? OR connected_account_id IS NULL)` (falls back to no filter when the param is omitted, so every existing caller that doesn't pass it is byte-identical). (4) src/lib/chat-history.ts: appendTurn's `input` gains `connectedAccountId?: string | null`, stamped onto the constructed ChatTurn (:46-57); listTurns gains a passthrough 3rd param to listChatTurns. (5) src/lib/chat/orchestrator.ts: line 143 `listTurns(userId, 10)` -> `listTurns(userId, 10, connectedAccountId)` (connectedAccountId already resolved at :123); line 148's appendTurn call gains `connectedAccountId`; line 479-485's `persistAssistantTurn` appendTurn call gains `connectedAccountId` too.
tests: New test in test/red-team.test.ts (or a new file): two connected accounts A (active, no short capability) and B (short-capable, has its own custom strategy prompt / redTeamLlmModel); call debateProposal(shortProposal, quote, userId, policyForAccountB) where policyForAccountB.connectedAccountId = B's id; assert the review does NOT hit the 'cannot short' refusal that would fire if activeAccount resolved to A, and that the system prompt build used B's own getStrategyPrompt content — MUST FAIL today (resolves account A via getActiveConnectedAccount regardless of policyOverride.connectedAccountId).

test/learned-context-pending.test.ts — add a case: two connected accounts, active account is B; seed a strategy-directive pending row via seedDirectivePending with connectedAccountId set to A (not B); approveAs(...); assert db.getStrategyPrompt(userId, A) contains the AI-LEARNED block and db.getStrategyPrompt(userId, B) does NOT — MUST FAIL today (writes land on B, the active account, regardless of pending.connectedAccountId).

test/chat-history.test.ts — add a case: appendTurn with connectedAccountId 'acct-a' and another with 'acct-b' for the same userId; listTurns(userId, 10, 'acct-a') returns only the acct-a turn (plus any legacy null-account turns); listTurns(userId, 10) (no filter arg) still returns both, unchanged — the second assertion proves backward compatibility; the first MUST FAIL before this change exists (no filtering capability at all).

test/chat-orchestrator.test.ts — add a case: user chats while account A is active (a turn is recorded), then the active account is switched to B and the user chats again; assert the history array built at orchestrator.ts's listTurns call for the SECOND turn does not include the first (account-A) turn's text — MUST FAIL today (10-turn window is unfiltered by account).
plan.risks: The chat_turns migration is additive/nullable — no backfill needed or possible (pre-migration turns have no recorded account, and treating them as 'always visible' via the `OR connected_account_id IS NULL` filter is a deliberate, conservative continuity choice: a single-account user's history is never affected since virtually all their turns share one account attribution going forward). trimChatTurns (db-api-keys.ts:1970-1978) and MAX_TURNS=100 stay a per-USER cap, not per-account — a heavy multi-account user's older single-account history can still be trimmed by another account's chat volume; this is a known, accepted trade-off, not fixed here (flagging to avoid scope creep — a per-account cap would need a larger redesign). Grep test/chat-history.test.ts (lines 24-49) and test/chat-orchestrator.test.ts before landing — both call listTurns/appendTurn without a connectedAccountId and must continue to pass unchanged since the new param is additive-optional. The getConnectedAccount import addition to red-team.ts must not create a cycle — src/lib/db.ts already re-exports it and red-team.ts already imports several names from './db', so this is a zero-risk addition.

clusters.title: RAG mirroring pins the single serving+trading event loop for minutes at a time
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/db-learning.ts:1613-1616 makes idempotency a DELETE with equality on non-rowid FTS5 columns, which FTS5 serves as a full-corpus scan — measured 4.3ms/row at 10k rows rising to 26.3ms/row at 60k, and ~300ms/chunk at the live corpus per the repo's own receipt in src/lib/rag/fts-mirror-bound.ts:20-23, while the INSERT it was blamed on costs 0.1-0.4ms. src/lib/rag/persist-local-complete.ts:46-54 and src/lib/web-sources/sec-filings.ts:624-631/736-756 then loop that call over a whole filing with no yield, no transaction, and no hasInFlightStrategyWork() gate (scheduler.ts:589-602) — unlike the bounded SEC worker at sec-ingest-worker.ts:462-475. There is no event-loop lag instrumentation anywhere.
clusters.one_change: Give the FTS mirror a rowid/side-key so idempotency becomes an indexed lookup instead of a scan (src/lib/db-learning.ts:1613 plus the DDL at src/lib/db.ts:2148), and route every mirror caller through the existing planFtsMirrorSlice + yieldEventLoop + strategy gate the SEC worker already uses.

plan.summary: Confirmed with one correction: the adaptive-yield batch helper (insertDocumentChunkFtsBatch, db-learning.ts:1666-1698) and the tick/budget planner (planFtsMirrorSlice, src/lib/rag/fts-mirror-bound.ts) already exist and are already correctly wired into src/lib/rag/sec-ingest-worker.ts:456-476 (with hasInFlightStrategyWork gating at :464) — that ONE caller is NOT the bug. The real gaps are: (a) the per-row idempotency DELETE inside insertDocumentChunkFts (db-learning.ts:1614-1617) and inside insertDocumentChunkFtsBatch's own runGroup (:1671-1684) is a full-table-scan `WHERE content_hash=? AND symbol=? AND source=? AND accession=?` on an FTS5 virtual table (no B-tree exists on those columns for anything but MATCH), which is the true O(corpus) cost underlying every other symptom; (b) src/lib/rag/persist-local-complete.ts:42-62 (persistLocalComplete, called from src/lib/web-sources/sec-filings.ts:625-632) loops the SINGLE non-batched insertDocumentChunkFts with zero yields and zero hasInFlightStrategyWork gate; (c) src/lib/web-sources/sec-filings.ts:736-756 has a SECOND unbounded per-row insertDocumentChunkFts loop, deliberately synchronous because it must run inside one atomic transaction with the vector-commit proof (comment at :743-744) — this site structurally cannot yield, so it depends entirely on fix (a) to stay fast.
plan.approach: (1) src/lib/db.ts: add migration version 85 (after the v84 block ending at :3151, following the exact ALTER-TABLE-guarded pattern used throughout this file) creating `CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS document_chunks_fts_index (content_hash TEXT NOT NULL, symbol TEXT NOT NULL, source TEXT NOT NULL, accession TEXT NOT NULL, fts_rowid INTEGER NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY (content_hash, symbol, source, accession))` then a one-time backfill `INSERT OR REPLACE INTO document_chunks_fts_index (content_hash, symbol, source, accession, fts_rowid) SELECT content_hash, symbol, source, accession, rowid FROM document_chunks_fts` (a single full pass, run once at migration time — not a per-request cost). (2) src/lib/db-learning.ts: rewrite insertDocumentChunkFts (:1600-1622) to first `SELECT fts_rowid FROM document_chunks_fts_index WHERE content_hash=? AND symbol=? AND source=? AND accession=?` (an indexed PK lookup), `DELETE FROM document_chunks_fts WHERE rowid = ?` using that fts_rowid when found (FTS5 rowid-delete is fast, unlike a column-value delete), then INSERT the new row, capture `info.lastInsertRowid`, and `INSERT INTO document_chunks_fts_index (...) VALUES (...) ON CONFLICT(content_hash,symbol,source,accession) DO UPDATE SET fts_rowid=excluded.fts_rowid`. Apply the identical lookup+rowid-delete+insert+upsert sequence inside insertDocumentChunkFtsBatch's `runGroup` transaction (:1679-1684), replacing the current `del.run(...)` scan-delete, with the 3 prepared statements hoisted outside the loop like the existing `del`/`ins` statements are today. (3) src/lib/rag/persist-local-complete.ts: change persistLocalComplete (:42-62) to `async`, and replace its `for (const chunk of input.chunks) { insertDocumentChunkFts(...) }` loop with the SAME plan-slice-then-yield-then-check-hasInFlightStrategyWork loop already proven at sec-ingest-worker.ts:456-476 (import planFtsMirrorSlice from '../rag/fts-mirror-bound', insertDocumentChunkFtsBatch + yieldEventLoop from '../db-learning'/'../slow-sync-guard', hasInFlightStrategyWork from '../db-execution'), building `ftsRows` from `input.chunks` first. Update its one caller, src/lib/web-sources/sec-filings.ts:625-632, to `await persistLocalComplete({...})`. (4) src/lib/web-sources/sec-filings.ts:736-756's loop is left structurally as-is (it cannot yield mid-transaction without breaking the 'FTS failures rollback with the vector commit' invariant the comment at :743-744 documents) — it is fixed entirely by (2), since each per-row DELETE becomes an indexed lookup instead of a scan, so even hundreds of iterations inside one synchronous transaction stay fast regardless of corpus size.
tests: New assertion in test/sec-ingest-worker.test.ts's 'insertDocumentChunkFtsBatch' describe block (after the existing case at lines 236-261): after inserting rows and re-inserting the SAME (content_hash,symbol,source,accession) key with new text, assert `SELECT COUNT(*) FROM document_chunks_fts_index WHERE content_hash=? AND symbol=? AND source=? AND accession=?` returns exactly 1 row whose fts_rowid matches the CURRENT (post-re-insert) document_chunks_fts row for that key — MUST FAIL before the fix with 'no such table: document_chunks_fts_index' (the table does not exist yet), PASSES after.

New test proving persistLocalComplete now yields: mock/spy yieldEventLoop (or hasInFlightStrategyWork returning true after the first slice) and call the now-async `await persistLocalComplete({..., chunks: <more than FTS_MIRROR_MAX_CHUNKS_PER_TICK rows>})`; assert yieldEventLoop (or the strategy-gate short-circuit) was invoked at least once and that a second call resumes from where the first left off (same durable-cursor pattern countDocumentChunkFts already provides) — MUST FAIL before the fix (today's loop is synchronous with no gate and no yield).

test/pinecone-write-class.test.ts:147-158 — this existing synchronous `it(...)` call to persistLocalComplete MUST be updated to `it("...", async () => { ... await persistLocalComplete({...}); ... })` since the function becomes async; without this update the test would silently race the now-unresolved promise (assertions immediately following would fail non-deterministically) rather than a clean compile/type error — flagging explicitly so the update lands in the SAME commit as the signature change.
plan.risks: The document_chunks_fts_index backfill INSERT...SELECT at migration time is itself an O(corpus) full scan — but it runs exactly ONCE, at deploy/boot, not per-request, so it is in the same cost class as any other migration and acceptable even on a large production corpus (unlike the current per-request cost this whole cluster exists to fix). document-summarizer.ts:466 does its OWN direct bulk `DELETE FROM document_chunks_fts WHERE source=? AND accession=?` (not per-row, not through insertDocumentChunkFts) — left untouched by this plan; it will leave orphaned document_chunks_fts_index rows for that (source,accession) pair, which is harmless (a stale side-key pointing at a since-deleted fts_rowid just causes a future insertDocumentChunkFts for that exact key to no-op-delete a nonexistent rowid, then correctly insert+upsert) but is worth a one-line comment noting the intentional gap rather than silently forgetting it. document-summarizer.ts:521's own insertDocumentChunkFts loop is left as a direct (non-batched) call site deliberately — document abstracts are a handful of chunks each, not full filings, so it is not a meaningful event-loop-pin risk and converting it would be scope creep; note this explicitly rather than silently leaving it unmentioned. Verify no other direct `INSERT INTO document_chunks_fts` / `DELETE FROM document_chunks_fts` exists outside the two functions being touched (grepped clean as of this investigation) before landing, since any bypass would desync the new side-key table.

clusters.title: Broker I/O is unbounded in time and scope, and the protective scheduler lanes latch on it
clusters.root_cause: The Alpaca SDK is constructed with no timeout (src/lib/alpaca.ts:247; axios default 0), so getLatestQuotes/createOrder/cancelOrder can hang indefinitely — and the stop-monitor and stale-exit lanes clear their in-flight key only in .finally (src/lib/scheduler.ts:919/931) with no withDeadline, so one hung socket latches the lane and that account's synthetic stops stop being evaluated forever. The tick itself has no re-entrancy guard (scheduler.ts:411). Separately getEquityOrders asks for status:"all", limit 500 with pagination (alpaca.ts:502/508-518) on ~20 call sites including a 15s dashboard poll and two 60s scheduler lanes, and the trade-updates stream has no idle watchdog (src/lib/streams/alpaca-trade-updates-stream.ts:50).
clusters.one_change: Pass a deadline into every Alpaca/Tradier call and wrap each scheduler lane in withDeadline the way src/lib/safety-maintenance.ts:69-78 already does, and scope getEquityOrders (src/lib/alpaca.ts:501) to open orders plus a bounded date window.

plan.summary: Partially confirmed, partially superseded by a recent fix (commit d4299bec6, 2026-08-18, this same day per git log) that already added a first-call+retry budget (awaitWithFirstCallRetry/outcomeOrTimeout, src/lib/inflight-deadline.ts) around Alpaca READ calls only: getAccount(s), getPositions, getOrders/getEquityOrders, getEquityQuotes all now bound at 16s+8s. The genuinely still-unbounded gap is the WRITE path: placeEquityOrder/placeOptionOrder's createOrder calls (alpaca.ts:633,737,814) and cancelEquityOrder/cancelBracketSiblingLegs's cancelOrder/sendRequest calls (:862,884,904) go through trackHealth (:256-287) directly with no deadline at all — trackHealth's own retry logic only fires on a REJECTED promise (isTransientNetworkError), never on one that simply never settles. Separately confirmed: scheduler.ts's stop-monitor (:918-936) and stale-exit (:883-907) in-flight Sets are cleared only in .finally() with no withDeadline wrapper (unlike the near-identical lanes in safety-maintenance.ts:32-78, which already use it); tick() is registered via a bare `setInterval(tick, TICK_MS)` (:411) with no re-entrancy guard; getEquityOrders (:501-546) fetches status:'all' with full pagination and no date bound on ~20 call sites; alpaca-trade-updates-stream.ts has no idle-message watchdog (only onerror/onclose-triggered reconnect).
plan.approach: (1) src/lib/alpaca.ts: import `withDeadline` from './safety-maintenance' (or promote it to a small shared util if that would create a cycle — safety-maintenance.ts does not import alpaca.ts, so a direct import is safe) and a new exported constant `ALPACA_WRITE_DEADLINE_MS = 20_000` (longer than the 16s read budget, since order placement is not retried in parallel the way reads are). In trackHealth (:256-287), wrap the inner `const result = await fn();` (:262) as `const result = await withDeadline(fn(), ALPACA_WRITE_DEADLINE_MS, "Alpaca broker call timed out");` — this closes the gap for EVERY trackHealth-wrapped call (creates/cancels included) in one place, and is pure defense-in-depth (a strict no-op) for the read call sites that already have their own outer awaitWithFirstCallRetry budget, since that outer race already wins first at 16s < 20s. Do NOT add a parallel-retry for createOrder/cancelOrder (unlike the read paths) — every createOrder call already carries a deterministic `client_order_id: input.refId` (:640,705,821), so a timeout should surface as a clean rejection and let the EXISTING ambiguous-retry-with-same-refId machinery at the strategy/execution layer (documented on SyntheticTrailingStop.lastAttemptRefId in db-api-keys.ts) decide whether to retry — firing a second concurrent createOrder from inside trackHealth itself would reintroduce exactly the double-order risk that machinery exists to avoid. (2) src/lib/alpaca.ts, getEquityOrders (:501-546): add a `since` bound to the pagination loop (e.g. stop paginating once a page's oldest `created_at` predates a caller-configurable window, default matching the app's existing stale-order/reconciliation horizons) and change `status: "all"` to `status: "open"` for the majority of call sites that only need open orders (stop-monitor, stale-exit, pending-fill reconcile) — audit the ~20 call sites first (grep `getEquityOrders(` across src/lib and app/api) to identify which ones genuinely need historical/all-status orders (e.g. a fills/history report) vs. only open ones, and thread a `{ status?: 'open'|'all', sinceDays?: number }` options param through rather than changing the default silently for every caller. (3) src/lib/scheduler.ts: import `withDeadline, BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS` from './safety-maintenance'. Wrap the stale-exit lane body (the async IIFE at :887-905, specifically the `autoRemediateStaleExitOrders(...)` call inside withAccountMutation) and the stop-monitor lane body (:920-935, the `runSyntheticStopMonitor(...)` call inside withAccountMutation) each in `withDeadline(..., BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS, "<lane> broker timeout")`, exactly mirroring safety-maintenance.ts:70-78's existing pattern, so the in-flight Set entry is guaranteed to clear (via the existing `.finally()`) within BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS even if the underlying broker call hangs. Add a module-level `let tickInFlight = false;` guard around tick() (:416+): `if (tickInFlight) return; tickInFlight = true; try { ...existing body... } finally { tickInFlight = false; }` so an overrunning tick (e.g. from the synchronous per-account `await checkBrokerHealth(...)` at :957, which is NOT one of the fire-and-forget `void journalLane(...)` lanes and can itself stall the whole tick) cannot overlap with the next setInterval firing. (4) src/lib/streams/alpaca-trade-updates-stream.ts: add a `lastMessageAt: number` field to StreamState (:23-29), stamp `Date.now()` at the top of `ws.onmessage` (:89+), and add a `setInterval` idle-watchdog (started alongside `connect()`, cleared on close) that force-calls `ws.close()` when `Date.now() - state.lastMessageAt` exceeds a threshold (e.g. 90s — comfortably above Alpaca's documented heartbeat cadence) — the existing `ws.onclose` handler (:135+) already drives the backoff-reconnect path, so this only needs to trigger that close, not reimplement reconnect logic.
tests: New test in test/alpaca-brackets.test.ts (or a new alpaca-broker-deadline.test.ts) using vi.useFakeTimers() per the test/inflight-deadline.test.ts pattern: mock createOrder to `return new Promise(() => undefined)` (never resolves), call placeEquityOrder(...), advance fake time by ALPACA_WRITE_DEADLINE_MS, assert the call rejects with a timeout-shaped error rather than hanging past the test's own timeout — MUST FAIL/HANG before the fix (trackHealth's await fn() never resolves or rejects today).
Same pattern for cancelEquityOrder mocking cancelOrder as a never-resolving promise — MUST FAIL/HANG before the fix.

New scheduler test: mock getBrokerGateway's runSyntheticStopMonitor dependency (or the gateway call it makes) to hang; run one tick(); advance fake timers past BROKER_TIMEOUT_MS; assert stopMonitorInFlight no longer contains the account key (i.e. the lane unlatches) — MUST FAIL before the fix (the Set entry is only ever cleared by .finally(), which never runs on a promise that never settles).

New scheduler re-entrancy test: make tick()'s body await a controllable never-resolving promise (inject via a mocked per-account health check); call startScheduler() (or invoke the tick function directly twice back-to-back before the first resolves); assert the per-account loop body (a spy) was entered only once during the overlap — MUST FAIL before the fix (setInterval has no guard).

New alpaca-trade-updates-stream test: open the stream with a mock WebSocket, advance fake time past the idle threshold without sending any message, assert ws.close() (or a reconnect) was triggered — MUST FAIL before the fix (no watchdog exists).
plan.risks: trackHealth's deadline must stay ABOVE the read paths' own outer budgets (16s+8s=24s worst case for the retry-extended reads) or it will start firing INSIDE an intentional retry window and break the already-landed 2026-08-18 fix — size ALPACA_WRITE_DEADLINE_MS carefully and re-run test/inflight-deadline.test.ts's live-max-14s cases after the change to confirm no regression. Narrowing getEquityOrders's default status/window is the highest-blast-radius change in this cluster — it MUST NOT silently break any caller that relies on seeing filled/canceled/all-status history (grep call sites and audit each one's actual need before changing defaults; prefer an explicit opt-in param over a silent default flip). The scheduler tick re-entrancy guard must not accidentally suppress the FIRST intentional immediate tick at startScheduler() (:409) — verify with the existing scheduler tests (grep test/*.ts for 'startScheduler'/'tick(' before landing). No persisted-schema changes in this cluster.

clusters.title: iOS shows the previous account's data after sign-out and never surfaces the outcome of a money action
clusters.root_cause: clearLocalSession (ios/SocraticTrade/MobileStore.swift:628-650) nils in-memory state but never removes the UserDefaults blob at :136-144, so a cold launch after sign-out or account deletion re-reads it, sets isAuthenticated from disk, and offline renders the prior account's holdings as current; init also stamps that cached blob lastUpdatedAt = Date() so it shows "Updated · now". On the write side, store.error has exactly one renderer (SnapshotScaffold, AppComponents.swift:566) which sits at scroll-offset 0 behind the settings sheet and is cleared by load() at MobileStore.swift:292, so a failed guardrail edit is invisible; 401 handling differs per passthrough (:463) and success has no acknowledgement at all.
clusters.one_change: Make one cache/session owner on the Swift side — clear the UserDefaults snapshot (and move the cookie to the Keychain) inside clearLocalSession, persist the real capture time, and render store.error and success as an .alert/toast anchored to the presenting view instead of a card at scroll-top that load() wipes.

plan.summary: Confirmed exactly, plus one additional confirmed mechanism. clearLocalSession (ios/SocraticTrade/MobileStore.swift:628-650) nils every in-memory @Published property but never calls UserDefaults.standard.removeObject for the 'cached_mobile_snapshot_data' key (cacheKey, :136); init (:147-154) unconditionally re-reads that blob on cold launch via loadCachedSnapshot(), sets isAuthenticated = (cached != nil) — true — and fabricates lastUpdatedAt = Date() rather than the blob's real capture time, so a signed-out/deleted account's stale holdings render as the CURRENT, freshly-loaded state offline. store.error (@Published, single global property) has exactly one renderer — InlineErrorBanner inside SnapshotScaffold (AppComponents.swift:580-586), which lives on the home view's scroll content at the top — and is unconditionally cleared by load() on ANY successful reload (MobileStore.swift:292), including background reloads triggered by SSE events (:319-323) unrelated to whatever action set the error; GuardrailEditRows (PolicyTightening.swift:553-627) routes every authority/cap edit through store.submit(), whose only failure surface IS this same global store.error — invisible while a settings sheet (e.g. GuardrailsView) is presented on top of the home view, and easily wiped by a background poll before the user dismisses the sheet to see it. There is no success acknowledgement path at all for these commands (only per-proposal ProposalActionFeedback exists, and only for proposal.approve/reject).
plan.approach: (1) MobileStore.swift, clearLocalSession() (:628-650): add `UserDefaults.standard.removeObject(forKey: Self.cacheKey)` (and a new companion timestamp key, see (2)) alongside the existing in-memory resets, so a cold launch after sign-out/account-deletion has nothing stale to read back. (2) Persist the REAL capture time instead of fabricating it: add `private static let cacheTimestampKey = "cached_mobile_snapshot_saved_at"`; in saveCachedSnapshot (:143-145) also write `UserDefaults.standard.set(Date().timeIntervalSince1970, forKey: cacheTimestampKey)` (call this from load()'s success path at :288, same call site); in loadCachedSnapshot (:138-141) also read that companion double back; in init (:147-154) set `lastUpdatedAt = cached == nil ? nil : (real saved timestamp, or nil if the companion key is missing)` instead of `Date()` — this makes isSnapshotStale(:221-224)'s existing >180s check correctly treat old cached data as stale immediately on cold launch (today it looks artificially fresh for 180s). (3) Add `func hasSessionCookie() -> Bool { HTTPCookieStorage.shared.cookies?.contains(where: ownsCookie) ?? false }` to MobileAPIClient.swift (near ownsCookie, :350-356) — the session's real authority already lives in the system cookie jar, which clearLocalSession already correctly purges (:633-635); change MobileStore.init's `isAuthenticated = cached != nil` (:151) to `isAuthenticated = previewSnapshot != nil || (cached != nil && client.hasSessionCookie())` so 'we have a cached blob' can no longer stand in for 'this session is actually valid' — the `previewSnapshot != nil` branch is kept unconditional so ControlCatalogTests.swift's three MobileStore(client:previewSnapshot:) fixtures (which never set up real cookies) are unaffected. (4) Add a view-anchored outcome signal decoupled from the background-load error surface: add `@Published var lastCommandOutcome: CommandOutcome?` to MobileStore (a small new enum: `.success(commandType: String)` / `.failure(commandType: String, message: String)`), set it at both return points of submit() (:436 success, :456 failure) in addition to (not instead of) the existing store.error/proposalNotices bookkeping. In PolicyTightening.swift's GuardrailEditRows (:392+), present `lastCommandOutcome` via `.alert(item:)` anchored to that view itself (visible while the settings sheet is on screen, not hidden behind it), and clear it (`store.lastCommandOutcome = nil`) once shown so it does not resurface after dismiss. Leave store.error / SnapshotScaffold's banner exactly as today for session/load-level errors (401s, network failures) — this is an ADDITIVE per-action signal, not a replacement, keeping the change scoped.
tests: New XCTest in ios/SocraticTradeTests (e.g. extend MobileModelsTests.swift or a new MobileStoreSessionTests.swift): seed UserDefaults with a fake cached_mobile_snapshot_data blob for account A, construct MobileStore(client:) (no previewSnapshot, so it reads the real cache), assert snapshot/isAuthenticated reflect A; call clearLocalSession(); construct a FRESH MobileStore(client:) again (simulating cold launch) and assert snapshot == nil and isAuthenticated == false — MUST FAIL before the fix (the second store re-reads A's stale blob and reports authenticated).

New test: seed the cache blob without the new cacheTimestampKey (simulating data written before this change, or the fresh-write path); after clearLocalSession + a real load() cycle writes both keys; construct a new MobileStore and assert lastUpdatedAt equals the persisted save time (not the construction time) — assert isSnapshotStale(at: saveTime + 200 seconds) == true — MUST FAIL before the fix (lastUpdatedAt is always 'now' at init, so staleness can never be detected from a cold-launch cache alone).

New test: construct MobileStore with a cached blob present but NO session cookie in HTTPCookieStorage; assert isAuthenticated == false — MUST FAIL before the fix (isAuthenticated is derived from cache presence alone). Confirm the existing three ControlCatalogTests.swift call sites (lines 68-71, 84-87, 107-110), which use previewSnapshot:, still assert true / are unaffected.

New test exercising submit()'s two outcome branches directly (mock MobileAPIClient's submit to succeed/fail): assert store.lastCommandOutcome is set to .success/.failure accordingly on each call — MUST FAIL before the fix (no such property exists).
plan.risks: Changing isAuthenticated's derivation could regress the 'offline first paint' UX the cache exists for — verify SocraticTradeTests/MobileModelsTests.swift:158 and :367's MobileStore(client:) construction sites (no previewSnapshot passed) to see whether they rely on cache-only isAuthenticated=true; if so they will need an explicit cookie stub (there may already be a test-only cookie-seeding helper, or one needs adding as part of this change). This is a Swift/iOS-only change — CLAUDE.md's iOS build-loop rule applies: `npm run lint`/`tsc`/`npm test`/`npm run build` do NOT compile Swift at all, so `xcodebuild build -project 'ios/Socratic Trade.xcodeproj' -scheme SocraticTrade -destination 'generic/platform=iOS' CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO CODE_SIGNING_REQUIRED=NO` (and the `xcodebuild test` variant for the new XCTests) MUST be run before claiming done. No server-side/API contract change is required for this plan (api-contract-web-ios:api-12's concern is addressed client-side by decoupling lastCommandOutcome from store.error, not by changing the mobile snapshot/command response shape) — confirm during implementation that api-12's actual text doesn't require a server-side field addition; if it does, treat that as a follow-up, not blocking this client-side fix.

clusters.title: Home's latest-run rows use synthetic ids and a private status map: green chips on failures, an Approve button that 404s, no keyboard access
clusters.root_cause: app/console/page.tsx:79 composes the row id as `${runId}-${symbol}-${status}` while real proposal ids are crypto.randomUUID (src/lib/strategy.ts:3361), so handleApprove always 404s at app/api/proposals/[id]/approve/route.ts:26 — and page.tsx:1011 offers that button on 'blocked' rows, a routine strategy outcome. page.tsx:1025's local chipTone knows only 'blocked'/'failed'/'pending', so the real statuses 'error' and 'proposed' fall through to green while labels.ts renders the word "Failed". The row itself is a click-only div (page.tsx:1029-1030) with no role, tabIndex or key handler, so the details sheet and its Approve flow are unreachable by keyboard.
clusters.one_change: Render those rows from the persisted proposals (real ids) through the shared helpers in app/console/lib/action-verbs.ts / labels.ts, and make the row a keyboard-operable control with the nested SymbolButton excluded from the activation target.

plan.summary: Home's 'Latest strategy run' / 'Previous Trades' rows are built with synthetic/wrong-id-space ids that make Approve either 404 or hit the wrong DB row, the chip-tone logic doesn't know about the real 'error'/'proposed' statuses so they render green like a fill, the `??` fallback never fires because latest.proposals can be an empty (not missing) array, and the row is a plain onClick div with zero keyboard access. Root cause of the id bug: strategy.ts already mints a real `crypto.randomUUID()` proposalId and inserts it into trade_proposals for every proposal, but never returns that id back on the trace item pushed into `results` (dashboard-types.ts StrategyDecision.proposals[] has no `id` field), so the UI has no real id to approve against for 'Latest strategy run' rows, and 'Previous Trades' rows use a completely different id-space (SocraticDecisionCase.id, not the proposal's trade_proposals id) for the exact same Approve button.
plan.approach: 1) src/lib/strategy.ts: inside the `for (const proposal of proposals)` loop (starts ~line 3356, `const proposalId = crypto.randomUUID()` declared right after entry), add `id: proposalId` to the object literal at every `results.push({...})` call site in that loop (22 sites: lines 3382, 3431, 3667, 3689, 3746, 3767, 3788, 3822, 3866, 3924, 3976, 4012, 4036, 4074, 4087, 4099, 4112, 4131, 4152, 4199, 4208, 4229 — verified `proposalId` is in lexical scope at every one, including inside the async mutation-lease closure). 2) app/dashboard-types.ts `StrategyDecision.proposals` (line 49) and src/lib/dashboard-feed.ts `StrategyDecisionLike.proposals` (line 41): add `id?: string` to the array element type (optional — legacy persisted `strategy_run` audit rows predate this field). `auditBoundedStrategyRunResult` (audit-bounded-run.ts) spreads `...result` untouched except marketScan, so the new field flows through to the persisted audit payload and back out via `latestStrategyRun.proposals[].id` with no other change needed. 3) app/console/page.tsx: in `decisionFromProposal` (line 774) add a 6th param `approvable: boolean = false` and set it on the returned `DecisionRowData` (add `approvable?: boolean` to the type at line 588). In `decisionFromPending` (789) pass `approvable: true` (it already carries a real `pending.id`). In `decisionFromSocratic` (754) explicitly pass/set `approvable: false` — 'Previous Trades' rows must never expose Approve since `decision.id` is a SocraticDecisionCase id, not a trade_proposals id (the exact same 404/wrong-row bug class, currently reachable whenever a previousTrades row's status is 'blocked'). Rewrite the `latestProposals` derivation (lines 77-80): build the trace-derived array into a local const first (`.map` over `latest?.proposals?.slice(0,5)` using `item.id ?? \`${latest?.runId}-${item.proposal.symbol}-${item.status}\`` as the row id, and `Boolean(item.id) && item.status === 'proposed'` as `approvable`), then fall back to the pendingProposals-derived array only when that local array's `.length === 0` (not via `??`, which only catches null/undefined and lets an empty array through, hiding older still-pending proposals). Fix `chipTone` (line 1025) to `isExecutedStatus(row.status) || row.status === 'placed' ? 'pos' : isNotPlacedStatus(row.status) || row.status === 'error' ? 'warn' : 'accent'` using the already-imported `isExecutedStatus`/`isNotPlacedStatus` from `./lib/action-verbs` (line 46) instead of the current ad hoc string checks that miss 'error' and 'proposed'. Replace `isPendingOrFailed` (line 1011) and its use at 1071 with `row.approvable === true` so the Approve panel only ever renders for a row with a genuine, currently-'proposed' DB id. Accessibility (dweb-18/a11y-01): leave the outer row `<div>` (1029) with its pointer `onClick` as a mouse convenience, but change the 'View details' text span (1039-1041) into a real `<button type="button" onClick={() => setOpen(true)}>` with `aria-label={\`View details for ${row.symbol}, ${combinedStatus}\`}` — do NOT convert the outer div into a `<button>`/role=button, since it nests `SymbolButton` (ui/symbol-drilldown.tsx:548), itself a real `<button>` with its own `e.stopPropagation()` (line 578); nested interactive buttons are invalid HTML and would double-fire.
tests: test/e2e-money-path.test.ts — extend the existing 'runs strategy through to execution' test: after `const aaplProposal = result.proposals.find(...)`, add `expect(aaplProposal?.id).toEqual(expect.any(String))` and, using the already-imported db layer, `expect(getProposal(aaplProposal!.id!, 'local')?.proposal.symbol).toBe('AAPL')` — FAILS today (`aaplProposal.id` is `undefined`, `getProposal(undefined, ...)` returns null) and PASSES once `id: proposalId` is threaded through every results.push.

test/console-action-rows.test.ts — add a new describe for a small exported pure helper (extract the chip-tone ternary above into an exported `proposalChipTone(status: string): 'pos'|'warn'|'accent'` in app/console/lib/action-verbs.ts so it's unit-testable outside page.tsx): assert `proposalChipTone('error') === 'warn'` and `proposalChipTone('proposed') === 'accent'` — both currently resolve to 'pos' via page.tsx's inline ternary, i.e. the existing behavior (uninverted) would fail these two new assertions before the fix.

new test (React Testing Library, colocate as test/console-proposal-row-a11y.test.tsx if one doesn't already exist for page.tsx internals) — render a latestProposals-derived ProposalRow with status 'blocked' and assert no 'Approve Proposal' button is present (before the fix, `isPendingOrFailed` is true for 'blocked' so the button renders); also assert the 'View details' element has `role='button'`/is a real `<button>` reachable via `Tab` — fails today since it's a bare `<div onClick>` with the button-hunt failing to find a focusable element by role.
plan.risks: The 22-site strategy.ts edit is mechanical but high blast-radius by file (the most sensitive module in the repo) — run the full E2E money-path + strategy-* suite, not just the one new assertion, since any missed/mistyped site would leave that one proposal's trace item without an id (degrading gracefully to `approvable:false`, not a crash, but worth catching in review). Grep `test/*.ts` for `.proposals[0].status` / `.proposals.find` before landing to confirm no existing test snapshot-matches the full proposals[] object shape (an added `id` field would break an exact-equality assertion, not a `.toMatchObject`). The `decisionFromSocratic` `approvable:false` change is a real, if small, behavior change beyond the review's literal 'Home' framing — flag it in the PR description since it also touches the 'Previous Trades' section on the same page. No persisted-data migration is needed (the new `id` field is additive/optional; old audit rows without it simply keep `approvable:false` until the account's next strategy run).

clusters.title: The console ships server DB internals to the browser and the whole universe on every 15s poll
clusters.root_cause: app/console/settings/brokers.tsx:12 value-imports @/lib/venue-contract, which pulls source-settings → db-api-keys → db into the client bundle: SQL schema, migrations and key-store logic reach the browser, and this exact chain produced the 2026-08-18 'process.uptime is not a function' production crash (fixed symptomatically in 01f4e73e2, whose own comment names the chain). No module in the repo imports the server-only guard. On the payload side src/lib/dashboard.ts:1108 serializes raw audit[], the full 500-symbol quotesBySymbol and the entire order history into a 15s poll (app/console/lib/useConsoleData.tsx:23), and post-action refreshes are served from the 10s cache so acked alerts stay on screen.
clusters.one_change: Add server-only to the src/lib/db* modules and split the pure mergeAccountCapabilities helper out of venue-contract so brokers.tsx no longer drags the DB layer, then project the snapshot at src/lib/dashboard.ts:1108 down to the fields the UI actually reads and bust the cache on mutation.

plan.summary: Two independent problems share one 'the console ships too much to the browser' theme. (1) app/console/settings/brokers.tsx value-imports `mergeAccountCapabilities` from src/lib/venue-contract.ts, and because that module's TOP-LEVEL import is `resolveSourceBool` from source-settings.ts -> db-api-keys.ts/db-settings.ts -> the db.ts barrel (better-sqlite3, SQL schema, migrations, key-store), the WHOLE db layer's JS compiles into the client bundle even though `mergeAccountCapabilities` itself never calls `resolveSourceBool` (only the separate `deriveVenueContract` does, in the same file) — this is exactly the import chain that produced the 2026-08-18 'process.uptime is not a function' production crash (fixed only symptomatically in 01f4e73e2, which guarded one call site but left the root chain intact). Verified: grepping every '"use client"' file in app/ + src/ for value-imports of @/lib/db*, @/lib/source-settings, @/lib/server-knobs, @/lib/venue-contract turns up exactly brokers.tsx (real) and app/console/lib/derive.ts (a `import type` of PositionStopPlan — erased at compile time, not a real offender). (2) src/lib/dashboard.ts ships an unused raw `audit: clientAudit` array (100 full-payload rows, confirmed zero consumers of `snapshot.audit` anywhere in app/console or ios/ via grep) and an unfiltered `latestScan.quotesBySymbol` covering the whole scanned universe on every 15s poll; app/api/scan/route.ts unconditionally re-audits the full scan even on a cache hit (`scan.cached === true`); and four mutating routes (notifications/ack, orders/cancel, orders/replace-market, plus strategy/run|pause|enable and connected-accounts/*/activate) never call `invalidateDashboardSnapshotCache`, so the client's post-mutation `refresh()` can replay the pre-mutation snapshot for up to the 10s TTL.
plan.approach: Bundle boundary (P1, dweb-01): `npm install server-only` (Vercel's zero-runtime marker package; not currently a dependency — `npm ls server-only` returns empty). Add `import "server-only";` as the first import in src/lib/db.ts, src/lib/db-settings.ts, src/lib/db-api-keys.ts (server-only's package.json `browser` export throws when a client bundle tries to include it, turning any FUTURE accidental client import into a build-time error instead of a silent 1MB+ leak). Then split venue-contract.ts: create src/lib/venue-contract-pure.ts containing everything that does NOT touch resolveSourceBool — `knownBrokerLimits` (line 73), `emptyCapabilities`, `mergeAccountCapabilities` (line 195), `brokerDisplayLabel` (line 219), `resolveSessions`, `buildPromptLines`, and the `VenueContract`/capability types — re-exported from venue-contract.ts for existing server-side importers so nothing else breaks, and change brokers.tsx:12 to `import { mergeAccountCapabilities } from "@/lib/venue-contract-pure"` instead. Leave `deriveVenueContract` (the ONLY function that calls `resolveSourceBool`, at line 250) in venue-contract.ts unchanged. Verify with `next build` + `grep -c 'getDb\|SELECT ' .next/static/chunks/app/console/connections/page-*.js` (should go to 0). Payload/cache (P2, dweb-03/04/05): in src/lib/dashboard.ts drop the `clientAudit` const and the `audit: clientAudit,` line from the returned snapshot object (~line 1108) — `unifiedFeed`/`auditFeed` (built earlier in the same function from the local `audit` array) are untouched, only the raw top-level field is removed; change `DashboardSnapshot.audit` (app/dashboard-types.ts) from `AuditEvent[]` to `audit?: AuditEvent[]` (additive/optional, matching every other backward-compat field in this type — test fixtures that still set `audit: []` remain valid). Trim `newestScan.quotesBySymbol` (dashboard.ts ~line 841-845) to the union of `topCandidates` symbols plus every symbol referenced by `positions`/`orders`/`pendingProposals` — NOT to just held/order symbols, since app/console/ui/symbol-drilldown.tsx and orders/lib.ts both fall back to `quotesBySymbol` by normalized-symbol lookup for arbitrary candidate rows too; keep every candidate's own quote to avoid degrading those drilldowns. app/api/scan/route.ts (~line 116): wrap the unconditional `audit("market_scan", { scan }, ...)` in `if (!scan.cached) { ... }` — `MarketScan.cached?: boolean` (types.ts:2089) is already stamped by market.ts:729 on every cache hit; confirm in market.ts that `scanMarket`'s cache path actually sets it before relying on it. Cache invalidation: add `invalidateDashboardSnapshotCache(userId);` to app/api/notifications/ack/route.ts (both the `body.all===true` and the specific-`ids` branch, right before each `return NextResponse.json(...)`), and inside `cancelWorkingOrder` in src/lib/order-cancel.ts right after the existing `emitDashboardEvent(...)` call (~line 192) — this single insertion point also fixes the mobile `order.cancel` command path for free since mobile-api.ts:992 calls the same function. For app/api/orders/replace-market/route.ts, add the same call at the route layer (before `return NextResponse.json(result);` ~line 76) rather than inside `replaceStaleLimitOrderWithMarket` (order-replacement.ts), which has many early-return/throw paths and only one true success path not worth the extra risk of tracing every branch. Note but do not implement in this pass (same mechanical one-liner, lower urgency): strategy/run, strategy/pause, strategy/enable, connected-accounts/*/activate also lack the call.
tests: new test/venue-contract-pure-boundary.test.ts — `import { mergeAccountCapabilities } from '../src/lib/venue-contract-pure'` and assert it resolves with no error and produces the same output as an existing test/venue-contract.test.ts case (e.g. 'Tradier is whole-share, no trail, no option orders') — this doesn't directly prove the bundle boundary (that needs a real `next build` + chunk grep, not a unit test) but pins the pure module's behavior parity with the pre-split function.

test/dashboard-snapshot-cache.test.ts or a new test/dashboard-audit-projection.test.ts — call `computeDashboardSnapshot`/`getDashboardSnapshot` against a seeded temp DB with at least one `market_scan` audit row present, and assert `snapshot.audit` is `undefined` — FAILS today (returns the 100-row clientAudit array) and PASSES after the field is dropped.

new test/notifications-ack-cache-invalidation.test.ts — seed the dashboard snapshot cache via `setCachedDashboardSnapshot`, POST to the ack route's handler, then assert `getCachedDashboardSnapshot(key)` is `undefined` — fails today (no invalidation call), passes after.
plan.risks: The server-only guard is the highest-leverage, lowest-risk part of this cluster (a genuinely additive dependency + a compile-time tripwire) — land it first/separately if splitting the PR. The `quotesBySymbol` trim is the riskiest single edit: verify against app/console/ui/symbol-drilldown.tsx's `resolveQuote` fallback (line 267) and orders/page.tsx:279 with a manual click-through on a symbol that is NOT held/ordered/pending but IS a topCandidate, to confirm its quote still resolves post-trim. Dropping `snapshot.audit` is safe per an exhaustive `grep -rn 'snapshot.audit'` across app/ and ios/ (zero hits) but re-run that grep right before landing in case another agent added a consumer in the interim. The scan-audit cache-skip depends on `scan.cached` being reliably true on every genuine cache hit — trace `scanMarket`'s cache path (market.ts ~line 320-402) once more before wiring the skip, since a false-negative there would just keep today's (already-accepted) over-auditing, but a false-positive would silently stop auditing a scan that was actually fresh.

clusters.title: The required merge gate never compiles or runs the iOS app, and can be skipped entirely for build-imported files
clusters.root_cause: .github/workflows/ci.yml:305's required `verify` job depends only on classify + verify-hosted and never on ios-build.yml, which itself only runs `xcodebuild build` (.github/workflows/ios-build.yml:70-78) — `xcodebuild test` appears nowhere in .github/ or scripts/, so 15 XCTest files covering order-cancel and price-review logic never execute before TestFlight. ci.yml:141's classify regex treats all of docs/** as documentation even though app/api/llm-usage/model-stats/route.ts:9/19 imports docs/benchmarks/*.json at build time, so such an edit auto-merges with tsc/test/build skipped and breaks first in the production deploy. scripts/land.sh:156 runs the same trio and never compiles Swift.
clusters.one_change: Add an `xcodebuild test` job, make the Swift job a required context in the main-protection ruleset next to `verify`, and exclude build-imported paths from the docs-only regex at ci.yml:141 (mirrored in e2e.yml:77 and scripts/land.sh:156).

clusters.title: Hand-mirrored Swift decoders drift from route payloads with no contract test — live stop-losses render as em-dashes
clusters.root_cause: FullPolicy decodes stopLossPct/trailingStopPct/shortStopLossPct from top-level CodingKeys (ios/SocraticTrade/DeskModels.swift:383-388) while GET /api/policy returns them nested under riskRules (src/lib/types.ts:1188, route at app/api/policy/route.ts:42), so every iPhone Guardrails view shows em-dashes for a configured 8% stop. Nothing ties the two sides together: app/api/mobile/snapshot/route.ts:16-54 is a bare object literal, MobileModels.swift:41-67 decodes every list with `?? []` so a rename blanks a screen silently, and the only Swift decode test is a hand-authored fixture (MobileModelsTests.swift:409). The same class drops recordedAt, benchmarkUnavailable and benchmarkSymbol.
clusters.one_change: Emit a shared fixture from the real routes (snapshot + policy JSON) and decode it in both `npm test` and the XCTest suite, failing on absent or unknown keys — starting by flattening riskRules in app/api/policy/route.ts:42 or decoding the nested container in DeskModels.swift:372.

plan.summary: Confirmed, concrete, high-value bug: GET /api/policy returns the raw TradingPolicy object, where stopLossPct/trailingStopPct/shortStopLossPct live under `riskRules` (src/lib/types.ts:713-731, RiskRules interface); but ios/SocraticTrade/DeskModels.swift's `FullPolicy.init(from:)` (lines 372-386) decodes those three fields from a TOP-LEVEL CodingKeys container that has no such key in the real payload, so `decodeIfPresent` silently returns nil for every account, every time — GuardrailsView.swift:96-98 renders them via `DeskCopy.percentPoints` (DeskModels.swift:683-686), which prints '—' for nil. This is a hand-authored Swift decoder with zero enforcement that it matches the real route shape; MobileModelsTests.swift:409's `fullSnapshotJSON` is itself a hand-typed string literal, not derived from the actual route, so nothing catches this class of drift before it ships.
plan.approach: Immediate fix (do NOT flatten the API — `riskRules` is a real domain grouping read by dozens of TS consumers; changing the wire shape is far more invasive/risky than fixing the one hand-written Swift decoder that's wrong): in ios/SocraticTrade/DeskModels.swift `FullPolicy`, add a nested `RiskRulesKeys: String, CodingKey { case stopLossPct, trailingStopPct, shortStopLossPct }` and a top-level `CodingKeys` case `riskRules`. In `init(from decoder:)`, replace the three flat `values.decodeIfPresent(Double.self, forKey: .stopLossPct)` etc. lines (374-376) with: decode an optional nested container via `try? values.nestedContainer(keyedBy: RiskRulesKeys.self, forKey: .riskRules)`, then `try riskRulesValues?.decodeIfPresent(Double.self, forKey: .stopLossPct)` (and same for the other two) — falling back to nil (not throwing) when `riskRules` itself is absent, matching every other field's `decodeIfPresent` optionality convention in this struct. Contract-test infrastructure (systemic fix, the cluster's real ask): add a small generator test in test/policy-ios-contract-fixture.test.ts that calls `GET /api/policy`'s underlying `getPolicy(userId)` (or invokes the route handler directly against a seeded temp DB with a known TradingPolicy including a non-default riskRules), writes the resulting JSON to ios/SocraticTradeTests/Fixtures/policy-contract.json, and asserts specific known fields (stopLossPct etc.) are present at `.riskRules.stopLossPct` in the raw JSON (a cheap, direct pin of the wire shape). Add a new XCTest (ios/SocraticTradeTests/DeskModelsTests.swift, new file if one doesn't exist for FullPolicy) that loads that checked-in fixture as a test-bundle resource and decodes it with the REAL `FullPolicy` type, asserting `policy.stopLossPct == <the fixture's known value>` (not just 'decode doesn't throw' — decodeIfPresent never throws on a missing key, so a pure 'no throw' test would have passed even on the broken decoder). CI wiring (document, don't necessarily build in this pass): a `npm run generate:ios-fixtures` step that re-runs the generator and fails CI if the checked-in JSON differs from freshly generated output, catching route-shape drift the moment it happens rather than only in a future manual audit.

clusters.title: Multi-account screens show the active account's data labeled as every account's
clusters.root_cause: app/console/settings/brokers.tsx:189 computes stateInfo only when isCurrentLoaded, so every other connected account chips a static "Inactive" even while it is genuinely running Autopilot (the scheduler runs each account independently, src/lib/scheduler.ts:810); brokers.tsx:191 then filters snapshot.pendingProposals, which src/lib/dashboard.ts:690 already scoped to the active account, so the per-account pending count is structurally always zero. app/console/decisions/page.tsx:28 fetches /api/socratic/decisions with no connectedAccountId although the route supports it, interleaving both accounts' BUY/SELL traces with no per-row label.
clusters.one_change: Feed every per-account row from snapshot.connectedAccountPolicies (already built at src/lib/dashboard.ts:350-368 and already used by chrome.tsx:141) plus a real per-account pending count, and scope /console/decisions by connectedAccountId with a visible account chip per row.

plan.summary: Verified: app/console/settings/brokers.tsx's `renderAccountRow` (line 189) computes `stateInfo` only `isCurrentLoaded && snapshot?.policy ? deriveStateInfo(snapshot.policy) : null` — every OTHER connected account always renders a static null-state chip even while genuinely running Autopilot, despite the snapshot already carrying a real per-account projection (`snapshot.connectedAccountPolicies`, built read-only via `peekPolicy(userId, account.id)` in src/lib/dashboard.ts:350-368, and ALREADY correctly consumed this exact way by app/console/components/chrome.tsx:140-141's account-switcher). The `pendingCount` at line 191 filters `snapshot.pendingProposals`, which src/lib/dashboard.ts:690 (`listPendingProposals(accountNumber, userId)` where `accountNumber = policy.accountNumber`, the ACTIVE account) already scopes to the active account only — so the non-active-account filter branch is structurally dead code, always returning 0. Separately, app/console/decisions/page.tsx:28 fetches `/api/socratic/decisions?limit=100` with no `connectedAccountId`, even though the route (app/api/socratic/decisions/route.ts) already supports that param — interleaving every account's decisions with zero per-row account label in decisions-list.tsx.
plan.approach: brokers.tsx: replace the `isCurrentLoaded ? deriveStateInfo(snapshot.policy) : null` line (189) with `const policyForAccount = snapshot.connectedAccountPolicies?.[account.id]; const stateInfo = policyForAccount ? deriveStateInfo(policyForAccount) : null;` — this is the exact pattern already proven correct in chrome.tsx:140-141, applied uniformly to every account row (active or not). For pendingCount: add a lightweight `countPendingProposals(accountNumber: string, userId: string): number` to src/lib/db-proposals.ts (`SELECT COUNT(*) as n FROM trade_proposals WHERE account_number = ? AND user_id = ? AND status = 'proposed'` — deliberately a COUNT query, not `listPendingProposals`, to avoid parsing full proposal/decision JSON blobs for every connected account on every snapshot). In src/lib/dashboard.ts, alongside the existing `connectedAccountPolicies` construction (~line 350-368), add a parallel `connectedAccountPendingCounts = Object.fromEntries(connectedAccounts.map((account) => [account.id, account.accountNumber ? countPendingProposals(account.accountNumber, userId) : 0]))` and include it in the returned snapshot object; add `connectedAccountPendingCounts?: Record<string, number>` to `DashboardSnapshot` (app/dashboard-types.ts, additive/optional). In brokers.tsx, replace the whole `pendingCount = isCurrentLoaded ? ... : ...filter(...)` block (lines 191-194) with a single `const pendingCount = snapshot.connectedAccountPendingCounts?.[account.id] ?? 0;` — correct for every account uniformly, no special-casing. For /console/decisions: convert app/console/decisions/page.tsx from its bare `fetch` to `useConsoleData()` (matching every other console page) so it has `snapshot.connectedAccounts` for an id->label map (`Object.fromEntries(snapshot.connectedAccounts.map(a => [a.id, a.label || a.broker]))`) and `snapshot.policy.connectedAccountId` for the active account; pass the label map as a new optional prop to `DecisionsList` (decisions-list.tsx) which renders a small `Chip`/faint-text account label next to each row's status chip ONLY when `snapshot.connectedAccounts.length > 1` (avoid clutter for the common single-account case), using `decision.connectedAccountId` to look up the label. Keep the current all-accounts-interleaved fetch (don't silently narrow to the active account only — that would be a functional regression, not requested); the chip alone fixes the misattribution risk the finding raises.

new test (or extend an existing dashboard.test.ts) — build a snapshot with two connected accounts where only the INACTIVE one has a proposed proposal, assert `snapshot.connectedAccountPendingCounts[<inactive account id>] === 1` — FAILS today (that count doesn't exist in the snapshot at all) and PASSES after.

new React test for decisions-list.tsx — render `DecisionsList` with `decisions` spanning two different `connectedAccountId`s and an `accountLabelById` map with 2 entries, assert both account labels are visible in the rendered output — fails today (component renders no account text at all).
