The decisions/page.tsx switch from bare fetch to `useConsoleData()` changes its loading/polling behavior (picks up the 15s snapshot poll instead of a one-shot fetch-on-mount) — verify this doesn't introduce an unwanted extra network waterfall or change the page's existing loading-state UX noticeably; if that's undesirable, an alternative is a second, smaller fetch of just `snapshot.connectedAccounts` via a lighter endpoint instead of the full `useConsoleData()` hook.

clusters.title: Coach coerces invalid tool inputs instead of rejecting them, and cannot be cancelled mid-call
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/chat/tools.ts:92 maps any side that is not exactly "sell" — "Sell", "short", a typo — to "buy", the opposite economic direction, and :94/96 silently drops a limit price the same way; downstream promote-draft only re-checks that side is buy|sell, which is trivially true after coercion. qty carries no unit and there is no notional field (tools.ts:58), and k has no maximum (tools.ts:155) unlike its clamped siblings. Separately no transport receives args.abortSignal (src/lib/chat/llm.ts:332-346, :688-705), so Cancel and the 120s deadline cannot stop an in-flight provider call, and exhausting the 5-step loop returns only the disclaimer (llm.ts:436-459).
clusters.one_change: Fail closed on out-of-enum tool inputs and clamp/convert numerics server-side in src/lib/chat/tools.ts (mirroring normalizeAlertOp's fail-closed shape), and thread args.abortSignal into every transport in src/lib/chat/llm.ts so cancel and the turn deadline actually abort.

plan.summary: Two independent, both real, money-adjacent bugs plus one correctness gap. (1) src/lib/chat/tools.ts's `draft_order.execute` (line 92) does `input.side === "sell" ? "sell" : "buy"` — ANY non-exact-'sell' value (case variant, 'short', a typo, missing) silently becomes 'buy', the OPPOSITE economic direction; downstream `chatDraftToProposal` (src/lib/chat/promote-draft.ts:16) only re-validates `draft.side === 'buy' || 'sell'`, which is trivially true after the coercion already happened, so it can never catch this. Line 94's `order_type` has the identical bug shape: any non-exact-'limit' value silently becomes 'market', and because line 96's `limit_usd` ternary keys off that same coerced `order_type`, a legitimate 'limit $150' instruction with a typo'd order_type silently loses the price and becomes a plain market order. `k` (kb_search, line 155) has a `minimum` but no `maximum` and is passed through unclamped. (2) src/lib/chat/llm.ts's `AnthropicLLM`/`OpenAILLM.run()` only check `args.abortSignal?.aborted` BETWEEN steps (lines 395, 537) — the injectable `Transport`/`OpenAITransport` function types (line 330, 464) never receive the signal, so `defaultTransport`/`defaultOpenAITransport`/`makeOpenAITransport`'s `llmFetch(...)` calls (lines 333, 468, 694) never pass `signal`, meaning a user's explicit Cancel (app/api/chat/route.ts:172's `handle.controller.signal`, aborted via `cancelChatTurn` in turn-registry.ts) has ZERO effect on an in-flight provider call — confirmed by tracing the whole call chain.
plan.approach: tools.ts fail-closed side/order_type (mirroring `normalizeAlertOp`'s shape in src/lib/alerts.ts:19-23, the established fail-closed pattern in this codebase): add `function normalizeDraftSide(raw: unknown): 'buy'|'sell'|null { const v = String(raw ?? '').trim().toLowerCase(); return v === 'buy' ? 'buy' : v === 'sell' ? 'sell' : null; }` and a sibling `normalizeOrderType(raw: unknown): 'market'|'limit'|null { const v = String(raw ?? 'market').trim().toLowerCase(); return v === 'market' ? 'market' : v === 'limit' ? 'limit' : null; }`. In `draft_order.execute` (~line 90-97), replace the two coercing ternaries: `const side = normalizeDraftSide(input.side); if (!side) return { error: 'INVALID_SIDE', details: \`side must be "buy" or "sell" (got ${JSON.stringify(input.side)})\` };` and the same shape for `order_type` before computing `limit_usd`. Clamp `k` in kb_search's execute (~line 164): `k: typeof input.k === 'number' ? Math.min(Math.max(Math.trunc(input.k), 1), 20) : 5` and add `maximum: 20` to the schema (line 155). llm.ts abortSignal threading: change `type Transport = (body: any, apiKey: string) => Promise<any>;` (330) and `type OpenAITransport = (body: any, apiKey: string) => Promise<any>;` (464) to accept a third optional `signal?: AbortSignal` param. In `defaultTransport` (331-345) and `defaultOpenAITransport` (466-...) and the closure returned by `makeOpenAITransport` (~689), accept that third param and, when present, compose it with a FRESH internal timeout rather than replacing llm-request.ts's shared 60s `LLM_TIMEOUT_MS` backstop (do NOT touch the shared `llmFetch` function itself — it's used by many non-chat callers including `fetchLlmWithRetry`'s per-attempt-timeout composition, which is too subtle/high-blast-radius to safely alter in this pass): `const combined = signal ? AbortSignal.any([signal, AbortSignal.timeout(LLM_TIMEOUT_MS)]) : undefined; const res = await llmFetch(url, { ..., ...(combined ? { signal: combined } : {}) });` (when `combined` is undefined, llmFetch's own existing `init.signal ?? AbortSignal.timeout(LLM_TIMEOUT_MS)` fallback applies unchanged). Update the two `this.transport(requestBody, this.apiKey)` call sites (line 424 for AnthropicLLM, line 586 for OpenAILLM) to pass `args.abortSignal` as the third argument. Loop-exhaustion fallback (llm.ts ~436-459): after the `for` loop exits (whether via `break` or exhausting `MAX_STEPS`), if `text` is still empty/whitespace-only and `toolCalls.length > 0`, set a clear fallback string (e.g. summarizing that N tool calls ran but the assistant didn't produce a final summary) instead of returning only `withDisclaimer('')`.
tests: new test in test suite for tools.ts (check for an existing test/chat-tools.test.ts, else create one) — `execute({ side: 'Short', qty: 5 }, ctx)` returns `{ error: 'INVALID_SIDE', ... }`, NOT a buy draft — fails today (produces a `side: 'buy'` draft), passes after.

test/chat-llm.test.ts — new test 'passes abortSignal as the third argument to transport' (models the existing 'passes the api key in the second argument to transport' test at line ~83): `const controller = new AbortController(); await llm.run({ ...baseArgs, abortSignal: controller.signal }); expect(transport.mock.calls[0][2]).toBe(controller.signal);` — FAILS today (`this.transport(requestBody, this.apiKey)` only ever passes 2 args, so `calls[0][2]` is `undefined`) and PASSES after threading the signal through.
plan.risks: The `AbortSignal.any` composition needs Node 20.3+ (repo pins Node 24 via .nvmrc, confirmed fine) — do NOT touch the shared `llmFetch`/`fetchLlmWithRetry` in llm-request.ts, whose per-attempt-timeout composition (line ~555-559, explicitly commented 'a caller-supplied init.signal is respected as-is') has subtle behavior other non-chat callers (framework-review.ts, learning-review.ts, outcome-engine.ts, post-mortem.ts, proposal-revalidation.ts, strategy-tuning.ts) depend on; scoping the fix to chat/llm.ts's own transport wrappers avoids that landmine entirely. The `order_type`/`side` fail-closed change is a genuine behavior change for any caller that was relying on the old silent-coercion (none should be, since it was always wrong, but re-run the full chat/tools test suite). The loop-exhaustion fallback text is a UX nicety, not safety-critical — keep its scope small (don't redesign the tool loop) given the cluster's overall effort budget.

clusters.title: Approving is starved by the run lock and the size that gets placed is not the size that was reviewed
clusters.root_cause: executeProposal contends for the whole-run strategy lock (src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:297), so an approval during a 15-20 minute autonomous run returns busy — the console gives up after ~2 min and iOS shows a green check. Mobile approvals also queue FIFO behind strategy.run_once because they are absent from IMMEDIATE_MOBILE_COMMAND_TYPES (src/lib/mobile-api.ts:88), whose claim loop is globally ordered with no per-user partition. On the sizing side, approval-time ratio re-anchoring moves EXIT limits with the market (src/lib/approval-reprice.ts:100), a hard-coded 5% headroom shrinks the owner's own cap (src/lib/policy.ts:567), and Retry Red Team stamps approve-at-half without applying the haircut (src/lib/retry-red-team.ts:47).
clusters.one_change: Give approvals a per-account lease instead of the whole-run lock at src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:297 (and add the non-broker command types to the immediate set at mobile-api.ts:88), and make the reprice, haircut and headroom rules apply to the order that is actually placed rather than to the displayed card.

plan.summary: Four sub-findings, with one premise correction and one that does NOT hold as stated after reading the code. (1) `executeProposal` (src/lib/strategy-execution.ts:297) calls `acquireStrategyLock(lockOwner, userId, policy.connectedAccountId)` with NO retry — verified the lock is ALREADY per-account (db-execution.ts:184-186 `strategyLockKey` includes `connectedAccountId` when given, and strategy.ts:460's own run-lock acquisition passes the same `connectedAccountId`), so the review's 'give approvals a per-account lease' framing is already true at the DB layer; the REAL bug is that the lock check is a single instant-fail with zero retry, so an approval that lands mid-run on the SAME account is starved for however long that run holds the lock, when a short bounded wait (matching the existing `LANE_WAITS.approvalPlacement = 30_000` convention in account-mutation.ts, already used elsewhere for 'a human click may briefly wait') would resolve most contention. (2) Mobile approvals: `proposal.approve` is DELIBERATELY excluded from `IMMEDIATE_MOBILE_COMMAND_TYPES` (mobile-api.ts:88) — it's grouped in `RISK_INCREASING_QUEUED_COMMAND_TYPES` (line 93-97) specifically so a halt can reach into the QUEUE and cancel it via `cancelQueuedRiskIncreasingCommands` before it fires; making it 'immediate' as the finding's one_change literally recommends would REMOVE that panic-button interceptability. The real, verified bug is one level deeper: `claimNextQueuedCommand()` (mobile-api.ts:701-706) claims globally (`WHERE status = 'queued'`, no user_id filter) AND `processPendingMobileCommands` (line 1137) is a strictly serial `while` loop that `await`s each command to FULLY finish before claiming the next — so ANY queued command (any account, any user) sits untouched for the full duration of whatever command claimed first, confirmed worse than a mis-scoped query. (3) src/lib/approval-reprice.ts's ratio-preserving reprice of exit limits is, after reading the whole module, a deliberately engineered, provenance-aware design — it already exempts `referencePriceProvenance === 'limit-fallback'` (hand-set prices, which is exactly what a chat-drafted manual sell limit gets stamped as per db-proposals.ts's `ensureReferencePrice`) and only re-anchors proposals whose reference price came from a genuine decision-time quote, preserving their relative aggressiveness rather than blindly chasing the market. This premise does NOT hold as a bug — recommend VERIFY/discuss with owner, no code change. (4) src/lib/policy.ts:101 `OPENING_ORDER_HEADROOM_PCT = 5` is a hard-coded, non-owner-adjustable module constant used in the headroom gate (~line 567) — a genuine violation of the 'guardrails are the owner's adjustable preferences' ruling, with the `iraWashSaleHandling` field as the canonical template for how to fix it. (5) src/lib/retry-red-team.ts's `retryProposalRedTeam` calls `stampRedTeamResult(proposal, result)` (finalized-sizing-review.ts:102-110) which only writes verdict METADATA onto `proposal.redTeamVerdict` and never touches `proposal.quantity`/`dollarAmount` — confirmed via strategy-execution.ts:626's parallel 'final broker-adjusted size' path, which correctly calls `applyRedTeamHalfSize(proposal)` (strategy-risk.ts:50) whenever the verdict is 'approve-at-half'; retry-red-team.ts has NO equivalent call anywhere, so clicking Retry Red Team, getting 'approve-at-half' back, then clicking Approve places the FULL original size — a real, serious money-path bug.
plan.approach: (1) In strategy-execution.ts, wrap the single `acquireStrategyLock(...)` check (line 297) in a small bounded retry loop reusing `LANE_WAITS.approvalPlacement` (30_000ms) from account-mutation.ts: poll every ~500ms-1s up to that budget before returning `{status:'busy',...}`, matching the existing 'human click may briefly wait' philosophy already codified for the broker-mutation lease later in the same function. (2) In mobile-api.ts, do NOT move `proposal.approve` into `IMMEDIATE_MOBILE_COMMAND_TYPES` (would drop it from `cancelQueuedRiskIncreasingCommands`'s halt-interception reach — a real safety regression). Instead restructure `processPendingMobileCommands` (line 1137) so it can run commands for DIFFERENT `(userId, connectedAccountId)` pairs concurrently instead of one global serial `await` chain: track an in-flight set keyed by `(userId, connectedAccountId)` (not one global boolean), have `claimNextQueuedCommand` (or a new variant) skip a queued row whose account key is already in-flight rather than strictly claiming oldest-first, and dispatch claimed commands via `Promise.allSettled` up to the existing `limit` (currently 3-10). This preserves FIFO ordering WITHIN one account (required for the TOCTOU cap-check correctness the strategy lock protects) while unblocking a different account's queued approve from an unrelated account's long-running command — the actual real-world complaint. (3) No code change to approval-reprice.ts — write up the provenance-aware design in the PR description and raise with the owner whether STRATEGY-GENERATED (not chat-drafted) exit limits should also be reprice-exempt, since the current behavior appears intentional (extensively comment-justified, adversarially probed) rather than a defect. (4) In src/lib/policy.ts, change `applyOpeningOrderHeadroom(value: number)` (line 240) to `applyOpeningOrderHeadroom(value: number, headroomPct: number = OPENING_ORDER_HEADROOM_PCT)` and use `headroomPct` in the `Math.floor(value * (100 - headroomPct)) / 100` body — backward compatible for the existing single-arg call in test/policy.test.ts:259. Add `openingOrderHeadroomPct?: number` to `TuningSettings` (src/lib/types.ts, ~line 317, matching the `/** ... Default N. */` doc-comment convention on sibling fields) and thread `context.policy.tuning?.openingOrderHeadroomPct ?? OPENING_ORDER_HEADROOM_PCT` into the call site at policy.ts:567. Note: exposing this on a Console settings UI (matching `iraWashSaleHandling`'s pattern) is real 'done' but is a fast-follow — flag it explicitly rather than silently leaving it API-only. (5) In src/lib/retry-red-team.ts, after `stampRedTeamResult(proposal, result)` (~line 44), when `result.verdict === 'approve-at-half'`: call `const haircut = applyRedTeamHalfSize(proposal);` (import from strategy-risk.ts); if `!haircut.applied`, append the note to `proposal.redTeamVerdict.reason` and treat it as effectively rejected (set `proposal.redTeamVerdict.rejected = true`), mirroring strategy-execution.ts's 'not executable' handling; if applied, re-price via `gateway.reviewEquityOrder({ accountNumber: policy.accountNumber, ...proposal })` (gateway obtained the same way `loadApprovalQuoteScan` already needs account context) and pass the fresh `estimatedNotional`/`review` into the existing `updatePendingProposalReprice(proposalId, { proposal, decision, estimatedNotional, review }, userId)` call (that function already accepts both fields) so the persisted row's displayed notional matches the halved size, not the stale full-size one.
tests: new test in test/retry-red-team.test.ts — mock `debateProposal` to return `{ verdict: 'approve-at-half', available: true, rejected: false, reason: '...' }` for a proposal with `quantity: 10`, call `retryProposalRedTeam`, then re-fetch the row via `getProposal` and assert `row.proposal.quantity === 5` — FAILS today (quantity stays 10) and PASSES after wiring `applyRedTeamHalfSize`.

test/policy.test.ts — extend the existing headroom test: `expect(applyOpeningOrderHeadroom(4.99)).toBe(4.74)` (unchanged, default-arg backward compat) plus a new `expect(applyOpeningOrderHeadroom(4.99, 10)).toBe(4.49)` (10% headroom) — fails today (function has no second param) and passes after.

new test for strategy-execution.ts's executeProposal — hold the per-account strategy lock (simulate a concurrent run via `acquireStrategyLock`), call `executeProposal` for a proposal on that SAME account, release the lock ~2s later from a parallel timer, assert `executeProposal` eventually succeeds rather than immediately returning `{status:'busy'}` — fails today (instant fail, no retry), passes after the bounded-wait retry is added.
plan.risks: The mobile-worker concurrency restructure ((2) above) is the riskiest single item in this cluster — it touches the core command dispatcher and must preserve the existing halt-interception (`cancelQueuedRiskIncreasingCommands`) and stale-command sweep (`STALE_MOBILE_COMMAND_THRESHOLD_MS`) semantics exactly; test with the existing test/mobile-api.test.ts and test/stale-mobile-commands.test.ts suites, and consider landing (1)+(4)+(5) (all narrowly-scoped, independently valuable) as a first PR, with (2) as a separate, more carefully reviewed follow-up given its blast radius. (3) is explicitly a no-code-change recommendation — do not let it get folded into the same PR as an actual fix without an owner decision first. The bounded-wait retry in (1) must stay strictly bounded (30s) — an unbounded or very long wait would itself become a new UX problem (a hanging HTTP request) that owner rulings explicitly warn against (no new blocking ceremony).

clusters.title: Non-owner content can reach the always-trusted strategy prompt with no human and a scanner that is inert in production
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/learning-review.ts:640-663 applies any 'keep' verdict with no riskTier exclusion, and applyApprovedPending (src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:397-405) merges strategy-directive rows straight into the strategy prompt — the one region the app never scans (src/lib/prompt-safety.ts:224) — while learningReviewMode defaults to 'decide' (src/lib/defaults.ts:90). Candidates get there from src/lib/chat/coach-learning.ts:567, which stores 480 chars of arbitrary fetched page text as auto-write 'fact' tier, past a classifier scoped to financial-risk vocabulary; the second-layer semantic gate resolves MockLLM in production (src/lib/learned-context/semantic-gate.ts:124); and app/api/chat-history/route.ts:28 lets the caller write a fabricated 'assistant' turn that is replayed as trusted context.
clusters.one_change: Apply the injection scan at ingest rather than only at prompt assembly, and require a human for anything that lands in the strategy prompt regardless of review mode — src/lib/chat/coach-learning.ts:567, src/lib/learning-review.ts:660, src/lib/learned-context/store.ts:401 — plus delete the unused POST writer at app/api/chat-history/route.ts:28.

plan.summary: Confirmed multi-part trust-boundary gap in the learning pipeline that feeds the strategy prompt. src/lib/learning-review.ts's `applyLearningReviewVerdicts` (line 631) applies ANY 'keep' verdict on a `learned_context_pending` row via `applyApprovedPending(pending, nowIso)` (learned-context/store.ts:397-405) with no check of `pending.riskTier` — and `applyApprovedPending` DIRECTLY calls `setStrategyPrompt(merged, ...)` when `riskTier === 'strategy-directive'` (store.ts:400-404), merging content straight into the one prompt region the app never scans for injected instructions. `learningReviewMode` defaults to `'decide'` (defaults.ts:90) — fully automated, no human in the loop — once the (opt-in, off-by-default) learning review feature is enabled at all. The candidate pipeline feeding this: src/lib/chat/coach-learning.ts's URL-lesson path (~line 567) fetches arbitrary web page text and calls `ingestLearned(..., { kind: 'fact', value: lesson.slice(0,800), ... })`; `ingestLearned` (learned-context/store.ts:82) does run the second-layer `classifyWithSemanticGate` classifier internally regardless of the caller's `kind` hint, but that classifier's LLM call resolves via `getLLM(opts.userId)` (chat/llm.ts:741), which fails OPEN to `MockLLM` whenever no real credential resolves for that userId/context (chat/llm.ts:720-723) — and the classifier's own fail-safe (semantic-gate.ts:139-142) treats any unparseable/mock response as 'fact' (never upgrades to 'risk'), meaning the second-layer safety net is silently INERT (not dangerous, just absent) whenever MockLLM resolves, with zero observability that this happened. Separately, `app/api/chat-history/route.ts`'s POST handler (lines 13-33) lets any caller with a resolvable userId write an arbitrary `role:'assistant'` turn directly into chat history that later gets replayed as trusted prior-assistant context by orchestrator.ts's multi-turn replay — confirmed genuinely dead/unused: grepped app/console/assistant/chat.tsx, ios/SocraticTrade/MobileAPIClient.swift, ios/SocraticTrade/CoachView.swift and neither web nor iOS ever calls it (both only GET/DELETE); the real, sole writer of turns is orchestrator.ts:148/479 calling `appendTurn` internally from the model's actual output.
plan.approach: Require a human for anything landing in the strategy prompt, regardless of `learningReviewMode`: in `applyLearningReviewVerdicts` (learning-review.ts, inside the `verdict.verdict === 'keep'` branch ~line 653), before calling `applyApprovedPending`, check `pending.riskTier === 'strategy-directive'` — if so, do NOT auto-apply even under `'decide'` mode; instead route it the same way the function already handles 'defer' (leave status pending, attach the reviewer's reasoning via `setPendingLearnedContextReviewNote`, so it surfaces in the human review queue) and audit a new `learning_review_strategy_directive_held_for_human` event so this is visible, not silent. This is a narrow, additive carve-out — every other riskTier ('fact', 'risk') keeps today's `learningReviewMode`-driven behavior unchanged, so it doesn't reintroduce blocking ceremony on the vast majority of learned-context flow, only on the one tier that becomes literal LLM instructions. Ingest-time scan placement: since `ingestLearned` already runs `classifyWithSemanticGate` on every candidate regardless of caller-supplied `kind` (confirmed), the scan IS already 'at ingest' for the classifier's purposes — the actual gap is observability, not placement. In semantic-gate.ts's `classifyWithSemanticGate` (~line 121, the `try` block around the LLM call), check `llm instanceof MockLLM` (or add an explicit `resolvedMock: boolean` return from `getLLM`/a cheap `isMockLLM(llm)` type guard) when `opts.llm` was not explicitly injected, and `audit('semantic_gate_mock_llm_fallback', { userId: opts.userId, subject: candidate.subject }, opts.userId)` when it fires in a real (non-test) call — this makes the previously-silent 'safety net is inert' condition observable in the audit trail without changing the fail-safe behavior itself (still defaults to keyword-tier 'fact', never fails closed/blocks). Delete the unused POST handler entirely from app/api/chat-history/route.ts (lines 13-33), keeping GET and DELETE — verified zero legitimate callers on web or iOS.
tests: test/learning-review.test.ts — new test: build a `learned_context_pending` row with `riskTier: 'strategy-directive'`, a verdict of `'keep'`, call `applyLearningReviewVerdicts`, assert (a) `getStrategyPrompt(userId)` does NOT contain the pending row's value, and (b) the row's status stays `'pending'` with a review note set — FAILS today (the content lands in the strategy prompt immediately) and PASSES after the carve-out.

test/semantic-gate.test.ts — new test: call `classifyWithSemanticGate` without an injected `opts.llm` and with no LLM credential resolvable for the test userId (forcing MockLLM), assert an audit row of kind `semantic_gate_mock_llm_fallback` was written — fails today (no such audit call exists anywhere), passes after.
new/extended test for app/api/chat-history/route.ts — assert the route module exports no `POST` (or that a POST request 405s) — fails today (POST succeeds and writes a turn), passes after deletion.
plan.risks: The strategy-directive carve-out changes real behavior for anyone who has BOTH `learningReviewEnabled: true` AND relies on fully automated 'decide' mode approving strategy-directive-tier lessons today — per CLAUDE.md this is a sole-user app and the feature is off by default, so blast radius is low, but confirm with the owner this is acceptable before landing (it's a deliberate, scoped exception to their 'decide' mode, not a blanket new ceremony — every other tier is untouched). The MockLLM audit-only change is pure observability, zero behavior change, essentially risk-free. Deleting the chat-history POST route is safe per the exhaustive grep of every client caller, but re-run that grep immediately before landing in case a very recent commit added a caller.

clusters.title: Each broker adapter rewrites the approved order differently and records nothing
clusters.root_cause: There is no shared venue-normalization step: src/lib/alpaca.ts:157 keeps time_in_force=gtc on extended-hours limits that Alpaca rejects with a 422, alpaca.ts:741 never forwards extended_hours on the MCP path, src/lib/robinhood.ts:972 silently converts a fractional or extended-hours limit into a regular-hours MARKET order while the persisted proposal and fill receipt still say 'limit', src/lib/tradier.ts:789 sends the unrounded limit price and always attaches a stop field, getEquityTradability is a stub returning tradable/fractional true for every symbol (alpaca.ts:582), and the hard-gate copy names Robinhood for Alpaca accounts (src/lib/policy.ts:326).
clusters.one_change: Put one venue-normalization step in front of every adapter's place call that resolves TIF, extended-hours, rounding and fractional support per broker and audits any rewrite, and make the tradability probe real so the pre-flight check means something.

clusters.title: Shipped controls whose backend does nothing, or something other than the label claims
clusters.root_cause: policy.taxSettings.subtractFromResults is written by app/console/strategy/tax-settings.tsx:213 and read by nothing in the Results render path (app/console/results/page.tsx:940-994 renders P&L unmodified), so "Show results net of estimated tax" changes no number in either direction. The Webhook channel's copy promises Discord embeds that only the separate legacy webhookUrl path builds (app/console/settings/delivery.tsx:37 vs src/lib/notify.ts:262 and src/lib/notifications.ts:330-372), and "Send test" never probes that legacy field. Presets has no create/rename/delete although /api/profiles implements POST/PUT/DELETE; the admin nav omits learning-ledger revert and the RAG backfills entirely; the R2 card tells the operator to run a curl.
clusters.one_change: For each control, either wire it to the behavior its label claims or remove it — starting with subtractFromResults in app/console/results/page.tsx:940-994, the legacy webhook probe in /api/notifications/test, and preset CRUD against the existing /api/profiles routes.

clusters.title: Shipped copy asserts guardrails the engine does not have and reintroduces the paper/live ceremony the owner ruled out
clusters.root_cause: app/console/macro/indicators.ts:698/706 and again at :753 tell the owner that below-median buys are "hard-vetoed" in risk-off/crisis regimes, while src/lib/strategy-risk.ts:187-197 keeps and tags them (its own comment reads 'advisory pre-veto (tag-not-drop)') and socraticOverrideMode defaults to 'execute'; app/how-it-works/page.tsx:94 lists delegation controls that do not exist and app/framework/content.ts:226 states a sizing invariant the override path contradicts. The same class of copy shouts "(NOT Real Money)" / red Live pills (app/console/settings/brokers.tsx:626, ios/SocraticTrade/ProposalsView.swift:366) and adds an iOS-only confirm for live activation the web does not have.
clusters.one_change: Run one accuracy pass that rewrites every guardrail claim to the engine's actual advisory behavior and strips the paper/live ceremony, sourcing the guardrail-semantics sentences from a single shared constant so console, iOS and the public pages cannot drift apart again.

clusters.title: Sessions are unrevocable 30-day bearer tokens behind a soft perimeter
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/auth/session-token.ts:6 issues a stateless 30-day JWT with no server-side record, so sign-out is a cookie delete and there is no revocation, no 'sign out everywhere' and no absolute lifetime; iOS then holds that cookie in non-Keychain storage with no app lock. The handoff around it is loose: app/api/mobile/auth-redirect/route.ts:24 mints a session code for any authenticated GET with a caller-supplied code_challenge, app/api/mobile/auth/apple/route.ts:23 uses no nonce, and app/api/mobile/push/register/route.ts:84 reassigns another user's device token. The origin answers directly at <PROD_ORIGIN_IP>:443 with Host: socratictrade.com (middleware.ts:173), so the WAF, bot rules and IP trust are all bypassable, and CSP has been report-only since 2026-07-01.
clusters.one_change: Back sessions with a server-side record (id in the JWT, revocable, absolute lifetime) and bind the mobile handoff to that record with a nonce and a client-bound challenge, then restrict the origin to Cloudflare IPs so the edge rules become load-bearing.

clusters.title: Nothing pages when the desk stops, and the backup/disk story is unverified
clusters.root_cause: app/api/health/route.ts:88 and :128 set checks.schedulerStale and checks.tradingLiveness.degraded without changing the 200 (ok flips only at :78 and :279), and nothing pushes on them — src/lib/scheduler.ts has a single sendNotification call, line 372 — so a wedged scheduler is discoverable only by an external keyword monitor. The Docker HEALTHCHECK gives that same heavy route 5s (Dockerfile:75) while documented stalls exceed it. The R2 'writes paused' banner reads a leftover marker with no endpoint check (src/lib/r2-usage.ts:571 vs scripts/coolify-prod-start.sh:200-212, live replica is B2), nothing rotates litestream-runtime.log (coolify-prod-start.sh:223), no table has retention (src/lib/db-fills.ts:118), and no restore drill has ever run.
clusters.one_change: Make liveness a first-class push plus one operator card — fire a notification on schedulerStale/tradingLivenessDegraded, split a cheap liveness route for the container probe, gate the R2 banner on isLitestreamReplicaCloudflareR2(), and add log rotation plus table retention.

clusters.title: Operator surfaces present placeholders, unattributed writes and mislabeled scope as fact
clusters.root_cause: app/admin/page.tsx:448 renders a bare CPU percentage with no caveat although app/api/admin/server-metrics/route.ts:604-613 documents the scaling as unverified and potentially an 8x under-report (the detail page at server-metrics-client.tsx:175 carries the caveat), and substitutes 0.0% / '0 Running' when a probe fails. app/api/admin/server-knobs/route.ts:80 audits every knob write as user 'local' regardless of which admin flipped it, and the admin chrome never shows the signed-in identity (app/admin/layout.tsx:217 reads only the avatar image). /admin/transcript calls /api/chat-history, which has no requireAdmin and is scoped to the caller's own turns, while the nav calls it 'every chat turn'; no page under app/admin/** has a server-side gate at all.
clusters.one_change: Carry the caveat and the unknown state through to the Overview card instead of substituting zeros, record and display the real admin identity on knob writes, and put one requireAdmin gate on the /admin page tree plus an admin-scoped transcript read.

clusters.title: A notification's lifecycle ends before delivery is known, and the tap lands on the wrong screen
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/alerts.ts:88-89 flips the alert to the one-shot 'triggered' state before sendNotification is awaited, and sendNotification never throws on total delivery failure (src/lib/notifications.ts:265-279 folds every error into a returned status) — so a revoked token or zero configured channels loses the only chance to notify. The row is tagged with whatever account happened to be active (notifications.ts:216) so it can drop out of the account-filtered Activity feed. The server builds a symbol-specific deep link (src/lib/push-deep-links.ts:99) that neither client reads (app/console/watchlist/page.tsx has no useSearchParams; ios/SocraticTrade/DeepLink.swift:75-77 discards the query), unlike the ?proposal= path at DeepLink.swift:58-73. There is no edit/pause, no badge, no category, and no recovered event (src/lib/db-health.ts:574).
clusters.one_change: Make delivery the state transition — mark an alert triggered only once a channel accepted it, retrying otherwise — and implement symbol-aware routing plus badge/category/thread-id on both clients, mirroring the proposal deep-link that already works.

clusters.title: Tone tokens fail WCAG AA at the sizes they are used, and light-default is not the default in several hosts
clusters.root_cause: app/console/console.css:40-73 defines tone text on soft fills that measures 3.68-4.34:1 (independently recomputed) at 11px/12.5px — below the 4.5:1 bar since neither size is 'large text' — including the Stop/Start Agent control; the Approve button's LIVE tag is 9.5px (console.css:578) and input borders are 1.5:1 (console.css:612). iOS uses system Color.green/Color.orange (ios/SocraticTrade/AppComponents.swift:13) and requests Lato weights the bundle does not ship. On the theme side, 'System' is stored by deleting the key so it reads back Light (app/console/lib/useConsoleTheme.ts:37), ⌘K's toggle writes a different hook instance, and <Toaster theme="system"> (app/layout.tsx:80) plus TickerLogo's dark-first default (ui/ticker-logo.tsx:21) render dark inside the light-default app.
clusters.one_change: Darken the tone tokens to at least 4.5:1 at the app's own micro sizes (open PR #2795 already does the console half) and make one theme resolver the single source for the console, the toast host, TickerLogo and iOS so light is the shipped default everywhere.

clusters.title: The phone build inherits desktop control sizes and ignores the visual viewport
clusters.root_cause: app/console/components/chrome.tsx:326 renders the full 'Stop Agent'/'Resume Agent' label in a flex-shrink:0 button (console.css:471-484) alongside a non-shrinking StateChip, avatar and ⌘K trigger, so the only min-w-0 sibling — the account scope selector, the control naming which brokerage account is loaded — collapses at 360-390px; the file's own comment computed its ~73px budget against the older short STOP label. The coarse-pointer 44px floor covers only .con-btn (console.css:458), overlays neither lock scroll nor size with dvh (console.css:858, :1220), inputs at 15px/11px trigger iOS auto-zoom (console.css:1251), and sheets ignore browser history.
clusters.one_change: Apply the coarse-pointer 44px floor and a 16px input minimum to every interactive class rather than just .con-btn, truncate or icon-ify the chrome run-state label below the sm breakpoint, and give every overlay scroll-lock plus dvh/visualViewport sizing and a history entry.

clusters.title: Shared console overlay and menu primitives skip the keyboard and announcement contract
clusters.root_cause: The primitives every page composes are non-conformant: app/console/ui/sheet.tsx:116's focus sentry and Escape handler are not stack-aware, so Escape on a drawer or palette above a Sheet closes the Sheet underneath; app/console/components/shell.tsx:180 has no skip link past ~22 focus stops; app/console/ui/toast.tsx:38 announces errors politely and auto-dismisses in 9s with no hover/focus pause, and typed-confirm server refusals are never announced at all; approval cards have no accessible name and repeat a bare 'Reject' (approval-card.tsx:455); the account-scope menu uses role=menu with no arrow-key handling plus an invisible full-screen focusable button (chrome.tsx:235).
clusters.one_change: Fix the shared primitives once — an overlay stack for focus/Escape in sheet.tsx, assertive non-auto-dismissing error toasts, accessible names on menu/dialog/card roots and a skip link in shell.tsx — so all 20+ call sites inherit the behavior.

clusters.title: Entry paths lose their destination or dead-end: expired sessions, OAuth errors, and iOS first-run
clusters.root_cause: middleware.ts:412-419 answers an unauthenticated /api/* with a bare 401 and drops the destination on page redirects, so a push deep link lands on the dashboard after sign-in and app/console/lib/useConsoleData.tsx:139-150 treats that 401 as any transient error — the tab polls stale data forever and Run once reports a generic 'The run failed'. Every Auth.js error routes to /access-denied (src/lib/auth/auth.ts:197) with no way out, and /login renders for already-authenticated users. On iOS the first-run checklist says to connect a broker 'in Account & Settings' (ios/SocraticTrade/HomeView.swift:87) while that very screen's empty state says to use the website (:844), and readiness ignores the LLM key entirely (src/lib/mobile-api.ts:1315).
clusters.one_change: Carry the destination through sign-in and special-case 401 in the console fetch client (stop polling, route to /login), and make the iOS first-run checklist either open the AdminPortalView cookie-sharing web view or state plainly that connecting happens on the website.

clusters.title: Model choice, receipts and cost each derive from a stale or partial source
clusters.root_cause: src/lib/model-rotation.ts:73 hardcodes a 'dead' OpenRouter list that drops slugs the live catalog still serves; app/console/components/approval-card.tsx:127 asserts 'this run's rotation pick, not a failover' even when an implicit fallback answered; src/lib/chat/llm.ts:655 routes Coach to native providers while the engine and the save-gate assume universal OpenRouter; late post-soft-timeout responses are audited but never metered (src/lib/strategy.ts:6594) and OpenRouter's billed usage.cost is never requested or stored (src/lib/llm-usage.ts:180), so /console/usage is derived from a hand-maintained price table with no embedding/rerank row; and Red Team re-sends the entire Green user content (strategy.ts:6318) that RedTeamReviewContext documents as a subset.
clusters.one_change: Make the live OpenRouter catalog plus the response's own billed cost the source of truth for rotation, receipts and the Usage page, and compact the Red Team payload to the documented RedTeamReviewContext subset.

clusters.title: The suite covers shapes but not money paths, reaches the live internet, and serializes 14 minutes into every run
clusters.root_cause: vitest.config.ts has no setupFiles at all — only a globalSetup that plumbs TMPDIR — so nothing prevents a test from reaching SiliconFlow, SEC or Yahoo (STATUS.md still records those 404s), and maxWorkers:1 serializes ~7,000 tests into ~14 minutes of every CI run. 63 of 122 routes have no route-level test including single-proposal approve (app/api/proposals/[id]/approve/route.ts:11), TestBrokerGateway always fills instantly (src/lib/robinhood.ts:920) so only the happy path is reachable, MobileStore.submit/load are untested despite an existing URLProtocol harness, there is no coverage tooling, and the codex-autofix workflow fails on every review event.
clusters.one_change: Add a vitest setup file that fails any un-mocked outbound fetch plus a partial-fill/reject mode on TestBrokerGateway, then write route tests for approve/replace/pause and re-enable parallel workers behind the per-worker temp DB the config already provisions.

clusters.title: One transient response or one bad row degrades the whole iOS app
clusters.root_cause: A single failed background reload flips snapshotLoadFailed and the 3-minute staleness gate then disables Approve/Run/Watchlist/Policy (ios/SocraticTrade/MobileStore.swift:223) with no polling fallback; GETs have no 5xx retry and the Cloudflare mapping stops at 523 (MobileAPIClient.swift:373), so deploy-swap 502/503s reach the user raw. SSE reconnects on a fixed 5s loop and every scene-active tears down a healthy stream (MobileStore.swift:343), while every SSE frame triggers a full snapshot reload. Decoding is all-or-nothing: one null required field inside any list element fails the entire snapshot (MobileModels.swift:240) and duplicate command ids trap outright (MobileStore.swift:46).
clusters.one_change: Make decoding element-tolerant — drop and count bad rows instead of failing the payload — and add bounded retry with backoff for idempotent GETs and SSE, so a deploy swap or one malformed row degrades a section rather than the app.

clusters.title: Console pages disagree about where things live, how they save, and how they are searched
clusters.root_cause: Three different save models coexist across the Configure pages (app/console/guardrails/page.tsx:335), and two numeric fields PATCH on every keystroke against the blur-commit pattern every sibling uses (app/console/settings/page.tsx:874 and strategy/overlays-panel.tsx:170, where a mid-edit empty field saves the fallback 2). /console/decisions is orphaned from the nav (decisions/page.tsx:1), the proposal lifecycle spans five surfaces, a bare 'r' key fires a strategy run with two mounted RunOnce buttons (command-palette.tsx:128), blotters cannot be searched, filtered or exported (activity/page.tsx:216), the Positions blotter lives only on Home without last price or exit action, and Results has no drawdown/profit factor/window.
clusters.one_change: Standardize the page contract — one save model (local draft plus explicit commit), one hotkey/verb registry, one blotter component with search/filter/export — and put every route in the nav section it belongs to.

clusters.title: iOS renders a read-only subset of the screens it mirrors
clusters.root_cause: Coach replies print raw markdown (ios/SocraticTrade/CoachView.swift:272) and its Suggested Draft cannot be staged although the copy says to approve it in Proposals (:323); the Scan header advertises three side-by-side columns that every row stacks vertically (ScanView.swift:158); the Activity tab is described as everything the agent did but shows only fills and the phone's own commands (MobileControlView.swift:64), so a run_failed push lands on a screen that cannot show the failure; Positions omit per-position P&L (MarketsView.swift:140); Results has no equity curve (ResultsView.swift:57); the symbol sheet offers no actions (SymbolInfoSheet.swift:46); triage is one-at-a-time; and Account & Settings is reachable only from the Home toolbar avatar.
clusters.one_change: Close the parity list against the console screens these mirror — a shared markdown renderer, the decision-journal feed, per-position P&L and an equity curve — and surface Account & Settings from More as well as Home.

clusters.title: iOS project-level hygiene: no privacy manifest, hardcoded production origin, no strict concurrency
clusters.root_cause: ios/project.yml:39 ships no PrivacyInfo.xcprivacy although the app uses UserDefaults, a required-reason API — ITMS-91053 on upload; the production origin is hardcoded in LoginView.swift:265, AdminPortalView and DeepLink with no debug override, so every simulator run hits production despite MobileAPIClient.productionBaseURL existing to prevent that drift; project.yml:18 builds in Swift 5.9 language mode with no strict-concurrency checking; and MobileStore/PushNotificationCoordinator/TabPreferences are ObservableObject against the repo's own @Observable rule, re-publishing on every SSE line.
clusters.one_change: One ios/project.yml pass — add the privacy manifest, a build-configuration-driven base URL and strict concurrency — plus the @Observable migration the repo rule already requires.

clusters.title: Owner copy rules are unenforced on the web: two-space gaps, Title Case, money format, Central time
clusters.root_cause: SENTENCE_GAP is used in 9 files against roughly 600 web copy strings (app/console/lib/format.ts:54), and the double ASCII spaces typed into JSX collapse to one at render (app/console/components/consent-gate.tsx:107) so source looks compliant and the screen is not; public pages have zero NBSP gaps. Headings and buttons are sentence case against the Title Case rule and against iOS (chrome.tsx:789), one run state carries three names and one stop control four (derive.ts:171), the same guardrail is labeled differently on web and iOS (GuardrailsView.swift:69), compact money renders uppercase suffixes (drilldown-data.ts:674), and app/console/settings/legal.tsx:40 calls toLocaleString() with no timeZone against the Central-time ruling every sibling honors.
clusters.one_change: Add the copy-rule lint the iOS suite already has — two-space gap, Title Case headings and buttons, lowercase compact money, Central-time timestamps, one term per concept — and run a single pass to make the strings pass it.

clusters.title: Phone layouts are the desktop tree at desktop density
clusters.root_cause: app/console/console.css:90 defines no phone type-scale bump, so 412 uses of 11px and 185 of 12.5px render at desktop sizes on a 6-inch screen; /console/watchlist keeps a 5-column table whose row actions scroll off (watchlist/page.tsx:227); Home buries portfolio value and day P&L under the readiness hero and strategy bar (page.tsx:217); Scan's phone branch is an unsorted, unfilterable, unvirtualized card wall mounted alongside the hidden desktop tree (scan-table.tsx:505); the equity chart scales to ~70px tall (equity-chart.tsx:11); the Coach composer's Enter always sends with no way to type a newline; and two full-viewport animated gradient orbs keep animating under the opaque console (app/globals.css:155).
clusters.one_change: Give the phone breakpoint its own type scale and card variants, and render one tree per breakpoint instead of mounting both.

clusters.title: Document structure and accessible names are stylistic rather than semantic
clusters.root_cause: Every console route shares the document title 'Socratic Trade' (app/console/layout.tsx:5, WCAG 2.4.2); 68 heading-styled divs carry con-card-title against 16 real h2/h3 and the collapsible Card demotes its h2 to a span (ui/primitives.tsx:35); none of the 23 console tables has a caption or aria-label and 105 of 106 th elements lack scope (components/positions.tsx:89); the Meter progressbar has no accessible name at any call site (primitives.tsx:201); roughly 147 explanations live only in native title= on non-interactive elements (primitives.tsx:485); readiness state is conveyed by icon and border color alone (readiness-checklist.tsx:27); and the login page has no heading.
clusters.one_change: Fix the primitives and the layout metadata once — per-route titles, real heading elements inside Card, caption/scope in the table primitive, names on Meter and Tooltip — so every page inherits the structure.

clusters.title: First console paint waits on a large bundle and then a single blocking snapshot
clusters.root_cause: app/console/layout.tsx:22 makes HTML → ~1.5 MB raw JS → /api/dashboard a strict waterfall, and routes that fetch their own data still wait behind the full-screen snapshot loader (components/shell.tsx:67). The single console context re-renders every page three times per poll and once per SSE event because fetching and stream health share the context value with snapshot (lib/useConsoleData.tsx:341). Sentry Session Replay (~38 KB gz) ships although replay is env-disabled (instrumentation-client.ts:31), framer motion (~40 KB gz) loads on every page for one tooltip fade (ui/primitives.tsx:7), three heavy client libraries are declared but never imported, and a 1 MB PNG is the primary favicon.
clusters.one_change: Split the context so data and transport health do not re-render together, drop the disabled Replay bundle, the motion dependency and the unused libraries, and let self-fetching routes paint before the snapshot resolves.

clusters.title: The public site's two halves do not connect and its metadata is stale
clusters.root_cause: An anonymous visitor never reaches the marketing page (app/page.tsx:14), /welcome offers only a mailto 'Request access' with no Sign in (welcome/page.tsx:114) and /login never explains the product, while /framework — the accurate explainer — is orphaned and /how-it-works is the only linked one (welcome/page.tsx:137).
