gap_findings.title: "Import from account" silently flips a live account into Autopilot and imports every guardrail with zero typed confirmation
gap_findings.evidence: doImport() calls importAccountSettings(policy.connectedAccountId, source.id) behind only a plain warning box and an "Import settings" button — no TypedConfirm phrase, no reality.tone==='live' gate. Server side, src/lib/db-profiles.ts:895-901 does `stripIdentityFields(stripUserFields(sourcePolicyRaw))` (ACCOUNT_IDENTITY_POLICY_FIELDS = only connectedAccountId/accountNumber/activeBroker, db-profiles.ts:785) then `mergePolicy({...cleaned, systemState: targetSystemState, ...})` — `strategyAuthority` is neither an identity field nor a USER_LEVEL_POLICY_FIELD, so it passes through unstripped and overwrites the target's authority.
gap_findings.why: Every other place in the app that can flip an account from Ask-first to Autopilot (guardrails/page.tsx AutonomyCard) requires typing the literal word "AUTOPILOT", and every other place that loosens a guardrail on a live account requires typing CONFIRM (`needsTyped = reality.tone === "live" && hasLooser && policy.requireTypedConfirmation !== false`, used identically in policy-form.tsx:335 and strategy/page.tsx:1259 for the AI Review Apply flow). Import bypasses both rituals: one click copies a source account's entire policy — including strategyAuthority, all riskRules caps, brokerBracketsEnabled, shortSellingEnabled, stop-loss percentages, etc. — onto a live brokerage account. A user importing from a permissive paper-testing account onto a live one can unintentionally enable autonomous order placement and loosen every cap on real money without ever being asked to confirm, directly contradicting owner rule #1 ("harden correctness — never place an unintended order").
gap_findings.recommendation: Route importAccountSettings through the same needsTyped/TypedConfirm gate used by PolicySaveBar and AiReviewPanel: diff the source policy against the target's current policy the same way reviewChanges() does, and require the CONFIRM phrase whenever the target is live and any changed field is a loosening (including strategyAuthority propose→decide). At minimum, explicitly preserve the target's own strategyAuthority the same way systemState is already preserved.

gap_findings.title: "Show results net of estimated tax" toggle saves successfully but never changes any number on Results
gap_findings.evidence: tax-settings.tsx:210-225 renders a Toggle labeled "Show results net of estimated tax" with title "On: P&L on the Results screen is shown after subtracting estimated taxes at the rates above", bound to policy.taxSettings.subtractFromResults and auto-saved via savePolicy. Grepping the whole repo, `subtractFromResults` is only ever read/validated in src/lib/mobile-api.ts (input validation) — results/page.tsx's BucketCard (940-994) and TaxBlock (1048-1160) render `performance.paperRealizedPnl`/`liveRealizedPnl`/etc. and `tax.estimatedTaxLiability` completely unmodified by the flag; no code path subtracts anything from the P&L stats when the toggle is on.
gap_findings.why: This is a control whose label makes an explicit, verifiable claim about what it does to the money numbers on Results, and the claim is false in both directions — flipping it on shows no different Realized/Unrealized P&L, and flipping it off doesn't restore anything either, because nothing ever reads it in the display path. A user trying to see their after-tax performance has no way to do so despite the setting existing, saving, and reporting success.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either wire subtractFromResults into BucketCard/TaxBlock (subtract tax.estimatedShortTermTax/estimatedLongTermTax pro-rata from the realized figures shown, or add a distinct 'net of tax' stat) or remove the toggle and its copy until it's implemented.

gap_findings.title: Webhook channel's copy promises rich Discord/Slack embeds it never sends, and "Send test" never exercises the one webhook field that actually does that
gap_findings.evidence: delivery.tsx:37 CHANNEL_TITLE.webhook = "An HTTPS POST with a JSON payload to any URL you control (chat webhooks get rich embeds)." — describing the toggle-based "Webhook" channel. But that channel's actual sender, CHANNELS.webhook.send in src/lib/notify.ts:262-290, always POSTs plain `{source, kind, title, body, data, sent_at}` JSON with no Discord/Slack special-casing. The Discord rich-embed logic (`isDiscord` + `formatDiscordPayload`) lives only in the SEPARATE, always-on legacy path `sendLegacyWebhook` in src/lib/notifications.ts:330-372, driven by the different field `policy.notificationSettings.webhookUrl` (WebhookUrlRow, delivery.tsx:95-129). The "Send test" button (delivery.tsx:268-275, title "Fires a test alert through every enabled, saved channel") calls POST /api/notifications/test, which calls `notify()` (src/lib/notify.ts:558) — this only iterates `prefs.channels` (the toggle-based system) and never touches the legacy webhookUrl field at all.
gap_findings.why: A user who fills in the legacy "Webhook URL (optional)" field expecting the promised rich embeds (which really do exist, just on the other field) gets a plain JSON POST from the toggle-based channel instead if they toggle it on with the same/a different URL — and if they rely on the legacy field alone (as the always-on mechanism it's documented to be), "Send test" gives false confidence: it reports success/failure for every OTHER channel but silently says nothing about whether that legacy webhook — which is what actually fires for every enabled event — is even reachable. On a real-money app, a broken alert channel that the UI claims was tested is a real notification-reliability gap (kill_switch, fill, pending_approval alerts could silently never arrive).
gap_findings.recommendation: Either move the Discord rich-embed logic into the toggle-based CHANNELS.webhook.send so the copy is true, or have the test endpoint also probe policy.notificationSettings.webhookUrl and report it as its own row in the test results.

gap_findings.title: Decisions index and trace pages merge every connected account's decisions into one list/detail with no account label or filter
gap_findings.evidence: page.tsx:28 calls `fetch("/api/socratic/decisions?limit=100")` with no `connectedAccountId`, even though app/api/socratic/decisions/route.ts explicitly supports that query param (`listSocraticDecisionCases(userId, { limit, connectedAccountId, runId })`). decisions-list.tsx never renders `decision.connectedAccountId` or `decision.accountNumber` (both present on SocraticDecisionCase, types.ts:1816/1819) anywhere in the row. app/console/decisions/[id]/page.tsx never references account either (zero hits for "account" in the file).
gap_findings.why: Every other console page explicitly scopes to the active account and says so ("Showing the active account only — switch the account scope (top bar) to see another account's orders", orders/page.tsx:311-316; Activity's unified feed labels "Account: {label}" per row, activity/page.tsx:284-290). The console's own glossary states "Active account: Exactly one account is active at a time; the entire console... is scoped to it" (settings/help.tsx:181-185). Decisions breaks that invariant silently: a user with a paper account and a live account sees both accounts' BUY/SELL decision traces interleaved in one reverse-chron list with no visual distinction, which directly undermines the "every screen states which money it is in words" money-reality philosophy (help.tsx:27-28) for the one screen that shows full reasoning traces for real trades.
gap_findings.recommendation: Pass the active account's connectedAccountId to /api/socratic/decisions by default (with an explicit "all accounts" toggle if cross-account viewing is intentional), and render an account/environment chip per row and on the trace page, matching Activity's pattern.

gap_findings.title: Strategy → Presets has no way to create, rename, or delete a preset — view/apply only, despite full CRUD existing server-side
gap_findings.evidence: The Presets card (925-985) only renders `snapshot.profiles` and an "Apply to this account" button calling copyProfileToAccount/activateProfile. Grepping app/console for any call to `POST /api/profiles` (create) or `DELETE /api/profiles/[id]` (delete) turns up nothing, yet app/api/profiles/route.ts implements POST createStrategyProfile and app/api/profiles/[id]/route.ts implements PUT updateStrategyProfile and DELETE deleteStrategyProfile — a complete CRUD surface the UI never calls.
gap_findings.why: The page's own copy ("A saved strategy bundle... Applying one COPIES it onto the active account", help.tsx:193-196) implies presets are something the owner builds and manages, but there is no button anywhere in app/console to save the current account's strategy as a new preset, rename an existing one, or delete one — the library can only ever contain whatever got seeded some other way. This is a real "can the owner do the job this section exists for" gap: the answer today is no.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add "Save current strategy as new preset" (POST /api/profiles with this account's policy/prompt/weights), and rename/delete actions per row, wired to the existing PUT/DELETE routes.

gap_findings.title: Legal acceptance timestamp renders in the browser's local timezone, not Central Time
gap_findings.evidence: `legal?.accepted && legal.acceptedAt ? \`Accepted on ${new Date(legal.acceptedAt).toLocaleString()}.\` : ...` — no `timeZone` option. Every other timestamp helper in the console routes through app/console/lib/format.ts's CENTRAL_TIME_ZONE-pinned formatters (format.ts:10, "Owner ruling (2026-08-11): every timestamp shown to the user displays in Central Time"), which this card bypasses entirely, calling `toLocaleString()` raw.
gap_findings.why: Directly violates the standing owner ruling that every user-facing timestamp displays in Central Time regardless of the viewer's device timezone — this is the one console timestamp that instead shows whatever timezone the browser is set to.
gap_findings.recommendation: Replace with the shared format.ts helper (e.g. fmtExact/formatTimestamp) used everywhere else in the console.

gap_findings.title: Macro's "How the strategist uses this label" disclosure repeats the same inaccurate "vetoed outright" claim the regime meaning text already got flagged for
gap_findings.evidence: REGIME_USAGE entry "It gates entries": "In Risk-Off or Crisis, buys scoring below the scan median are vetoed outright, and an optional cap limits how large any new position may open in Crisis/Inverted regimes." This is the same overstated claim as regimeInfo()'s meaning text at indicators.ts:698/706 ("hard-vetoed"), which the register already flags as inaccurate (advisory tag-not-drop in the actual engine, not a hard veto) — but it is a second, independent copy of the claim on a different UI surface (the collapsible disclosure under the Regime card vs. the chip's own tooltip/meaning text), so a reader who never opens the meaning tooltip but does open "How the strategist uses this label" still gets the same wrong mental model.
gap_findings.why: Same underlying inaccuracy (advisory, agent-decides-and-logs, not a hard block — per the owner's standing "guardrails: nothing hard" ruling) surfacing at a second, unfixed location; fixing only line 698/706 would leave this one still wrong.
gap_findings.recommendation: Same fix as the registered finding, applied to both locations: change "vetoed outright"/"hard-vetoed" to advisory language consistent with ADVISORY_NOTE used elsewhere in field-defs.ts.

gap_findings.title: Two auto-saving number fields fire a write on every keystroke instead of on blur, breaking the app's own established pattern
gap_findings.evidence: settings/page.tsx:866-880 (DataSourcesCard number row): `onValueChange={(n) => { if (Number.isFinite(n) && n !== Number(row.value)) void saveOne(row.id, n); }}` — RawNumInput's onValueChange fires on every keystroke (primitives.tsx:310-315 confirms `onChange` calls `onValueChange` per input event), so saveOne (a PATCH) runs mid-typing rather than on blur. overlays-panel.tsx:170-180 "Max Active" uses a plain `<TextInput type="number">` whose onChange directly calls `patchTuning({ maxActiveOverlays: ... })` on every keystroke too, with `Number(event.target.value) || 2` silently coercing a momentarily-empty field (normal mid-edit state when replacing a value) to 2 and saving that.
gap_findings.why: Every other numeric auto-save field in the app (ScanShapeCard settings/page.tsx:593-598, tax-settings.tsx short/long-term rates, llm-budget.tsx, learning-review.tsx, Strategy's own scoring-weights inputs) deliberately holds local text and commits on blur specifically to avoid firing a save per keystroke. These two fields silently deviate: typing a two-digit number issues multiple PATCH requests, and for Max Active a normal "select-all, retype" edit gesture can transiently save the fallback value 2 instead of what the user meant to enter.
gap_findings.recommendation: Switch both to the same local-draft-until-blur pattern already used by every sibling numeric field (RawNumInput + explicit onBlur commit).

gap_findings.title: Chat Transcript admin page bypasses requireAdmin and does not actually show "every chat turn"
gap_findings.evidence: const res = await fetch("/api/chat-history?limit=200");  -- app/api/chat-history/route.ts:8 is `const userId = resolveRequestUserId(request);` with no requireAdmin call at all; app/admin/layout.tsx:101-103 describes the nav item as "Every chat turn, with the model that produced each assistant reply."
gap_findings.why: Every other admin data probe (connections-health, llm-usage, rag-coverage, server-metrics, r2-usage, data-catalog, enrichment-coverage, backup-status, server-knobs) is behind the shared requireAdmin() gate and correctly 403s a non-admin session -- app/admin/page.tsx even has dedicated `allForbidden`/`probeErrors` handling to show "Operator access required" for exactly that case. `/api/chat-history` has no admin check and is scoped to resolveRequestUserId(request), the CALLER's own account, not "every" turn. So (a) any signed-in non-admin user who opens /admin/transcript, or the Overview page's Chat Transcript card (which fetches the same endpoint at app/admin/page.tsx:104), gets a normal 200 response instead of the operator-access notice every sibling widget shows -- confirmed by the code's own comment at app/admin/page.tsx:208-215 that explicitly carves this endpoint out of the all-forbidden check; and (b) if a second admin is ever added via the documented ADMIN_USER_EMAILS allowlist (src/lib/auth/admin.ts:44-50), their "Chat Transcript" view would silently show THEIR OWN (likely empty) history rather than the primary trading account's actual coach conversations, defeating the feature's stated audit purpose with no error surfaced anywhere.
gap_findings.recommendation: Gate an admin-scoped transcript read behind requireAdmin, explicitly reading the primary/local user's turns (or accepting an explicit userId param) instead of reusing the per-caller /api/chat-history endpoint.

gap_findings.title: RAG purge-legacy is an irreversible corpus-wide vector deletion reachable only by curl, guarded by a confirm string the code itself says is scope-mismatched
gap_findings.evidence: "SCOPE WARNING: despite the token's historical name it deletes vectors from EVERY non-current embedding space for the covered docTypes ... not only voyage-finance-2's." -- the POST handler at lines 80-88 gates this solely on `body.confirm === "purge-voyage-vectors"` plus the shared admin token/email check; there is no admin nav entry or page for this route (grep of app/admin/**/*.tsx for /api/admin/reembed returns nothing).
gap_findings.why: This action bulk-deletes RAG vectors across every embedding space that isn't the currently-active one for the covered doc types -- broader than its own confirm string implies, per the route's own comment. It is reachable only by hand-crafting an authenticated curl POST with that exact (misleadingly-named) confirm string; there is no UI that shows what would be deleted before it happens, no dry-run visible outside a JSON response, and no button an operator could accidentally NOT click. A stale runbook or copy-pasted curl command using the confirm string's literal (narrower) meaning could delete far more than intended with zero UI guardrail to catch the mismatch.
gap_findings.recommendation: Surface this as a guarded Admin panel (in the style of Operations' knob resets) that lists the exact embedding spaces/docTypes about to be purged before firing the destructive POST, and/or rename the confirm string to match actual scope.

gap_findings.title: Several real, cost/state-mutating operator capabilities (learning-ledger revert, tuning dry-run, congress-score-eval, RAG/EarningsCalls backfills) have zero admin UI -- curl-only, JSON body shape read out of code comments
gap_findings.evidence: NAV_ITEMS lists exactly 10 pages, none of which reach learning-ledger, tuning-dry-run, congress-score-eval, congress-share, refresh-websource, sec-ingest, reindex-8k, reindex-10k, or earningscalls. app/api/admin/learning-ledger/route.ts:9 literally calls itself "panel P0-4" and app/api/admin/tuning-dry-run/route.ts:9 calls itself "panel P1-1"; app/api/admin/congress-score-eval/route.ts:11 calls itself "item 2".
gap_findings.why: learning-ledger's POST reverts a live scoring-weight mutation (with before/after weight vectors) and is admin-gated specifically "because a revert mutates live policy" (route.ts:16) -- exactly the kind of action the rest of this admin surface (e.g. Operations' real toggle switches) treats as something an operator should be able to see and act on from a page, not something they curl. The same is true of the RAG/EarningsCalls backfills, which spend real Voyage/bge/EarningsCalls.dev budget. The "panel P0-4"/"panel P1-1"/"item 2" naming in the code strongly implies these were meant to get admin pages that were never wired up.
gap_findings.recommendation: Wire learning-ledger (list + revert) and tuning-dry-run into the Admin nav first, since both already have complete read+act backend pairs; the naming suggests this was the original plan.

gap_findings.title: Overview's CPU-load number drops the "scaling unverified, may read up to 8x low" caveat that the Server Stats detail page carries for the identical value
gap_findings.evidence: {server?.metrics?.cpu ? `${currentCpu.toFixed(1)}%` : "Unavailable"} -- no caveat text or title anywhere on this card, versus app/admin/server/server-metrics-client.tsx:175-178's CPU_SCALING_CAVEAT ("...this value may read low") and the visible caption "per-core average; scaling unverified" at lines 848-852 of the same file.
gap_findings.why: app/api/admin/server-metrics/route.ts:604-613 documents this transform as an explicitly UNVERIFIED 8x risk ("the only support ... is an uncited comment ... which would make this an 8x under-report on this 8-core cx43 and keep the meter green through a saturation incident"). The Server Stats detail page was carefully rewritten to disclose that risk inline. The Overview page -- the one literally named to give status "at a glance" -- renders the same field from the same API with no caveat at all, so an operator who only checks Overview sees a confident, uncaveated percentage the codebase itself says it does not trust.
gap_findings.recommendation: Reuse CPU_SCALING_CAVEAT (or a shortened title-only version) on the Overview card, or replace the bare percentage there with the same "unverified" language used on the detail page.

gap_findings.title: Admin chrome never shows which admin identity is signed in, despite the allowlist supporting multiple distinct admins and knob writes already being mis-audited as a fixed user
gap_findings.evidence: fetch("/api/auth/session").then((res) => res.json()).then((s) => setImageUrl(s?.user?.image)) -- only `image` is read and stored; the profile dropdown (lines 262-303) renders "Profile" / a theme picker / Back to Console / Sign Out, and no email or name string anywhere in the component.
gap_findings.why: src/lib/auth/admin.ts:44-50 (ADMIN_USER_EMAILS) is a documented allowlist that supports more than one distinct admin identity, and app/api/admin/server-knobs/route.ts:80 already audits every knob write under a hardcoded userId of "local" regardless of who actually flipped it. With no on-screen identity anywhere in the admin chrome, an operator using powerful tools (knob flips today; ledger reverts and backfills if admin-03 is addressed) has no way to visually confirm which session is acting, compounding the existing audit-attribution gap.
gap_findings.recommendation: Show the resolved session email in the profile trigger or dropdown header -- the fetch already receives it in `s.user.email`, it is just discarded.

gap_findings.title: The tamper-evident audit hash-chain has no admin viewer, and verifyAuditChain() is never called outside a unit test
gap_findings.evidence: return NextResponse.json(listAudit(200, resolveRequestUserId(request))); -- no requireAdmin call, capped to 200 rows, no `kind` filter, scoped only to the caller's own userId. Repo-wide `grep -rn "verifyAuditChain"` (excluding node_modules) returns only its definition at src/lib/db.ts:3372 and test/audit-chain.test.ts -- no route, cron, or admin page calls it. No app/admin/**/*.tsx file fetches /api/audit either.
gap_findings.why: src/lib/db.ts's audit() builds a genuinely hash-chained audit_events table (chain_hash/prev_chain_hash, see auditChainMaterial at db.ts:3344) precisely so a knob change, a learning-ledger revert, or a securities import can be proven untampered. That investment is currently invisible in the product: there is no Admin > Audit Log page, no nav item, and the one HTTP route that reads audit_events is unused by any UI and isn't even admin-scoped. If the chain ever silently broke -- a bad migration, a manual DB edit, real tampering -- there is today no automated check and no manual UI path by which the owner would find out; verifyAuditChain only runs inside `npm test`.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add an admin-gated Admin > Audit Log page (list recent audit_events, filterable by kind, admin identity) that also surfaces verifyAuditChain()'s result; consider running the chain check on a schedule with an alert on mismatch.

gap_findings.title: Enrichment Coverage report is a single unscoped process-global with no account/run attribution in a multi-account app
gap_findings.evidence: let lastCoverageReport: EnrichmentCoverageReport | null = null; -- the EnrichmentCoverageReport interface (lines 123-135) has fields for asOf/symbolCount/fields/sourceWinTotals/providerFailures/contributingSources but no userId, connectedAccountId, or policy identifier of any kind.
gap_findings.why: app/api/admin/enrichment-coverage/route.ts serves getLastEnrichmentCoverageReport() verbatim -- whichever scan (any connected account, any user) ran most recently across the whole process overwrites the single in-memory report with no attribution. In a multi-connected-account app (the product's own stated model), an operator viewing Admin > Enrichment Coverage cannot tell which account's cascade run produced the numbers on screen, and a scan from one account can silently mask another account's actual coverage state with no indication that happened.
gap_findings.recommendation: Key the last-report cache by (userId, connectedAccountId) and show which account/run produced the displayed report, or keep a short history instead of a single overwritten snapshot.

gap_findings.title: A route under /api/admin/ intentionally skips the shared requireAdmin gate with no marker distinguishing it from the ~25 sibling routes that all use it
gap_findings.evidence: import { verifySecuritiesImportToken } from "@/lib/securities-import-auth"; -- this file has no `requireAdmin` import at all, unlike every other route.ts under app/api/admin/ (confirmed: `grep -n requireAdmin` across all app/api/admin/*/route.ts files returns a hit in every route except this one).
gap_findings.why: This route is a legitimate, well-documented inter-app (Congress.Trade -> Socratic-Trade) ingest endpoint with its own bearer-token auth, default-closed when unconfigured -- not a defect on its own merits. But it lives at a URL prefix (/api/admin/) that every other route treats as "gated by the shared operator requireAdmin() check," which is exactly the assumption this review started from before reading the file. A future engineer (or agent) grepping for "is every /api/admin/ route admin-gated" and pattern-matching on the URL prefix rather than reading each file could reasonably conclude this route is covered when it uses an entirely different auth model.
gap_findings.recommendation: Move this route out of the /api/admin/ prefix (e.g. /api/integrations/congress-trade/securities-import) so the prefix reliably means "gated by requireAdmin" for every route under it, or add a header comment making the divergent auth model impossible to miss on a prefix-based audit.

gap_findings.title: draft_order silently coerces any non-"sell" side value (case-sensitive) to "buy", including "short"/"cover"/typos
gap_findings.evidence: const side = input.side === "sell" ? "sell" : "buy";  // line 92; line 94 has the same pattern: const order_type = input.order_type === "limit" ? "limit" : "market";
gap_findings.why: This is a strict, case-sensitive equality check with no rejection path. Any side value that is not the exact lowercase string "sell" -- "Sell", "SELL", "short", "cover", a typo, or an out-of-schema value a less-compliant provider emits -- is silently mapped to "buy", the OPPOSITE economic direction from a sell/short. The Coach model catalog includes Gemini, Grok, Mistral, DeepSeek, Moonshot, and any free-typed custom model id (app/console/assistant/chat.tsx custom-model field), several of which are known to be looser about strict JSON-schema enum adherence in tool-calling than Anthropic/OpenAI. The draft_order JSON schema itself only declares side enum ["buy","sell"] (tools.ts:64) -- there is no server-side rejection of an out-of-enum value, only silent coercion. Contrast with create_alert's op handling, which normalizes via normalizeAlertOp and fails closed with {error:"INVALID_OP"} on anything unrecognized (src/lib/alerts.ts:31-34) -- draft_order does the opposite. The same pattern also silently discards a limit price: if order_type arrives as anything but the exact string "limit" (e.g. "Limit"), order_type resolves to "market" AND limit_usd is forced to null (tools.ts:96), dropping a limit price the user gave. The downstream human-approval ticket (draft-card.tsx) does display the coerced side/order_type, so a careful reviewer can catch it, but the assistant's own natural-language reply is generated independently of the coerced fields and can describe the order differently than the ticket -- exactly the kind of ticket-vs-prose mismatch a rushed approval misses.
gap_findings.recommendation: Reject the draft (return {error:"INVALID_SIDE"}) when input.side is not exactly "buy" or "sell" (case-insensitive compare, then fail closed on anything else, mirroring create_alert's normalizeAlertOp pattern), and do the same for order_type. If short/cover intent is out of scope for chat, say so explicitly in the draft error rather than silently rewriting the order to a buy.

gap_findings.title: Neither the chat "Cancel" button nor the 120s turn deadline actually aborts an in-flight LLM provider request
gap_findings.evidence: async function defaultTransport(body, apiKey) { const res = await llmFetch("https://api.anthropic.com/v1/messages", { method: "POST", headers: {...}, body: JSON.stringify(body) }); ... }  -- no `signal` is ever passed, so llm-request.ts:402 falls back to `signal: init.signal ?? AbortSignal.timeout(LLM_TIMEOUT_MS)` (LLM_TIMEOUT_MS = 60_000, llm-request.ts:367). makeOpenAITransport (llm.ts:688-705) has the identical gap.
gap_findings.why: AnthropicLLM.run/OpenAILLM.run only check `args.abortSignal?.aborted` (llm.ts:395, 537) and the deadline budget (via decideStageBudget) at the TOP of each tool-loop step, BEFORE calling `this.transport(...)`. The Transport type itself is `(body, apiKey) => Promise<any>` -- it never receives the AbortSignal, so once a provider HTTP call is in flight there is no way to interrupt it; it can only be interrupted by its own 60s AbortSignal.timeout. For the dominant case (a single-step reply, no tool calls), the abort/deadline check never gets a second chance to fire before the loop naturally exits after that one call completes -- so clicking "Cancel" in chat.tsx (line 649-655, which just POSTs /api/chat/cancel and has no client-side AbortController on its own `fetch("/api/chat", ...)` either) has essentially no effect: the user keeps waiting for the original request to resolve normally, and the reply still gets appended to the transcript as if nothing happened. The same missing signal wiring means the advertised CHAT_TURN_DEADLINE_MS (120s default, app/api/chat/route.ts:166) is not a hard ceiling either -- worst case a turn can run up to MAX_STEPS x LLM_TIMEOUT_MS (5 x 60s = 300s) before anything intervenes, since decideStageBudget's step 0 always runs (stage-budget.ts:23-25) regardless of remaining budget and in-flight steps are never preempted.
gap_findings.recommendation: Thread `args.abortSignal` into the Transport signature and pass it as `signal` on every llmFetch call in defaultTransport/defaultOpenAITransport/makeOpenAITransport (composed with the existing timeout signal via e.g. AbortSignal.any). Also give the client's `/api/chat` fetch its own AbortController tied to the Cancel button so cancel takes effect locally without waiting on the server.

gap_findings.title: ChatDraft ships permanently-hardcoded placeholder fields ("Test (local)" account_label, is_real:false, blocked:false, warnings:[]) that no client renders
gap_findings.evidence: account_label: ctx.deps.accountLabel ?? "Test (local)", is_real: false, blocked: false, warnings: [],  // tools.ts:105-108; ctx.deps.accountLabel is itself hardcoded to the literal string "Test (local)" in buildProductionDeps (src/lib/chat/orchestrator.ts:770), so account_label is ALWAYS "Test (local)" for every production draft, live account or not.
gap_findings.why: These four fields are set exactly once at draft creation and never mutated anywhere else in the codebase (grep confirms zero other writers). account_label is always the literal string "Test (local)" regardless of the actual connected account (which could be a real live broker account) -- a hardcoded test/paper-mode label the owner's rulings explicitly forbid attaching to real data. is_real is always false and blocked/warnings are always empty/false, so they can never reflect an actual policy verdict. Today this is largely inert: draft-card.tsx (web) and CoachDraftCard (iOS) both independently recompute the real account label/scope from live snapshot state rather than reading these fields, so nothing user-facing currently shows "Test (local)" for a real account. But the fields are still serialized verbatim in the /api/chat JSON response, are decoded on iOS (DeskModels.swift:120,133,149-151) into a ChatDraft.accountLabel/isReal that a future screen could plausibly surface, and an operator inspecting the raw API/admin transcript would see a real-money draft literally labeled "Test (local)" / is_real:false.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either wire real values through (pass the caller's actual account label/environment into ToolDeps.accountLabel from the active connected account rather than a hardcoded default, and drop is_real/blocked/warnings from the tool's output entirely since policy evaluation genuinely happens later in /api/proposals/from-draft), or remove the dead fields from the ChatDraft type so the wire contract doesn't advertise information nothing computes.

gap_findings.title: Chat conversation history has no account scoping -- the last-10-turn context replayed into every prompt spans ALL of a user's connected accounts
gap_findings.evidence: export interface ChatTurn { id: string; userId: string; role: ChatTurnRole; text: string; citations: string[]; intent: string | null; redacted: boolean; model?: string | null; clientTurnId?: string | null; createdAt: string; }  -- no connectedAccountId field anywhere on the row; orchestrator.ts:143 does `listTurns(userId, 10)` (userId only) and replays that as `history` to the model on every turn, while every read tool (get_positions/get_portfolio/get_reflection/get_performance_summary/get_quote's broker branch) is scoped to `getPolicy(userId)`'s CURRENTLY ACTIVE account.
gap_findings.why: A user with multiple connected accounts (e.g. a live account and a paper/practice account) who switches the active account mid-conversation gets a multi-turn LLM context that silently mixes both accounts' answers with no account-boundary marker in the replayed text -- the model has no way to know a prior turn's positions/P&L/portfolio numbers belonged to a different account than the one the current tool calls now resolve against. The client's own Clear-conversation toast concedes this design ("it is one conversation shared across all your accounts", chat.tsx:357) but that disclosure only appears at clear time, not on send, and it does not prevent the model from anchoring a follow-up answer (e.g. "what's my P&L now?") on stale account-A numbers still sitting in the replayed history text after a switch to account B.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either scope chat_turns (and the 10-turn replay window) by connectedAccountId so switching accounts starts a fresh context, or inject an explicit account-boundary marker into the replayed history whenever the active account differs from the account each historical turn was answered under (would require persisting connectedAccountId per turn either way).

gap_findings.title: Dead, unauthenticated POST /api/chat-history lets a user forge arbitrary chat turns -- including fabricated "assistant" replies -- into their own persisted transcript
gap_findings.evidence: export async function POST(request: Request) { const body = ...; const userId = resolveRequestUserId(request, body); if (body.role !== "user" && body.role !== "assistant") return ...400; ... const turn = appendTurn(userId, { role: body.role, text: body.text, citations: ..., intent: ... }); return NextResponse.json({ turn }, { status: 201 }); }
gap_findings.why: This handler accepts an arbitrary role ("user" OR "assistant") and arbitrary text/citations straight from the request body and writes it into the caller's own chat_turns via the same appendTurn used by the real orchestrator -- with no check that this ever went through an actual model call. Grepping the whole app/ios tree shows nothing calls it: chat.tsx only GETs and DELETEs /api/chat-history, and the real assistant turn is always persisted server-side from within makeOrchestrator (orchestrator.ts:479-505). Because this route is live and reachable by any authenticated user for their own account, a user (or a stray script/extension) can insert a fabricated "assistant" turn claiming the model said something it never said. src/lib/chat-history.ts's own header comment calls this table the transcript that "powers chat reload + auditability" -- a forgeable assistant turn breaks that guarantee, is displayed as real in the admin transcript viewer (app/admin/transcript/transcript-client.tsx), and -- more materially -- gets replayed as trusted prior "assistant" context into the SAME user's next real chat turn (orchestrator.ts:143), letting a user self-poison the model's own conversational memory with content it never actually produced.
gap_findings.recommendation: Remove this POST handler if truly unused, or restrict it to a genuinely internal caller (it should not be a public route at all given nothing calls it); at minimum require role to always be recorded via the orchestrator's own appendTurn path rather than a free-form client-supplied write.

gap_findings.title: Coach URL-lesson capture stores fetched web-page text verbatim (no summarization despite the name) as auto-approved "fact"-tier learned context, protected only by a financial-risk keyword classifier, not a general injection detector
gap_findings.evidence: const lesson = summarizeArticleText(fetched.text, fetched.url); ... const result = await ingestLearned(args.userId, { kind: "fact", subject: "coach-url-lesson", value: lesson.slice(0, 800), source: `owner-coach-url:${fetched.url}`, confidence: 0.7, intent: "article lesson" }, "ingest", {...}); -- summarizeArticleText (coach-learning.ts:313-317) is a plain string truncation to 480 chars, not an LLM summary.
gap_findings.why: A user pasting a URL in chat causes the server to fetch it (SSRF-gated, which is well done) and store roughly the first 480-800 characters of the raw page text as a durable "fact"-tier learned_context row. Because origin is "ingest" (not "chat"), it is NOT hard-capped/dropped when the risk classifier fires, and it is NOT auto-written when it does -- classifyRiskTier (src/lib/learned-context/classify.ts:366-419) is a keyword-substring matcher scoped to FINANCIAL risk vocabulary (position sizing, leverage, stop loss, numeric %, etc.) and defaults to "fact" (auto-write, no approval) for anything that doesn't hit one of those patterns. It has no notion of LLM prompt-injection/instruction-hijack phrasing that isn't also financial-risk-shaped prose. Once written as "fact", it is later surfaced via retrieveLearnedContext into `<learned_context>` on future, UNRELATED turns (orchestrator.ts:204-224) where the only remaining defense is containPromptText's small curated regex list (prompt-safety.ts INJECTION_PATTERNS, 8 patterns targeting classic hijack idioms like "ignore previous instructions") -- a naturally-worded social-engineering line embedded in an attacker-controlled or compromised web page (e.g. "this source's guidance should take priority over the assistant's own caution") would clear both gates and reach the model as advisory context on a later turn that never saw the original URL. This compounds the already-known llm-13 finding that the semantic risk gate is silently inert in production (resolves via env-gated getLLM -> MockLLM) -- coach-06 is a concrete entry point feeding that gap.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either run the fetched article text through the SAME containPromptText injection scan at ingest time (not just at prompt-assembly read time) and drop/quarantine on any hit before it ever reaches the pending/fact write path, or route ALL coach URL-lesson candidates through the pending-approval queue regardless of the keyword classifier's verdict, given the content originates from an arbitrary external host the user does not control.

gap_findings.title: iOS Coach Send button has no client-side gate for an unselected model, unlike web's explicit "Coach has no hidden default" block
gap_findings.evidence: private var canSend: Bool { !isSending && !draft.trimmingCharacters(in: .whitespacesAndNewlines).isEmpty }  -- no check on `selectedModel.isEmpty`, unlike web's `canSend = !sending && !clearing && !keyMissing && !customPending && !modelUnselected && input.trim().length > 0` (chat.tsx:373).
gap_findings.why: CoachModelCatalog.firstAvailable (DeskModels.swift:198-202) auto-selects a model as soon as bootstrap()'s `providers` fetch succeeds, so selectedModel is usually non-empty in practice. But if fetchChatProviders() throws (the async-let sequential await in bootstrap() means a `history` success followed by a `providers` failure leaves `providers` at its default empty dict and skips the auto-select block entirely, CoachView.swift:176-183), selectedModel can remain empty on first launch with the Send button still enabled. sendChat (MobileAPIClient.swift:109-116) then omits the `model` key from the request body entirely when model is nil/empty, and the server correctly 400s with "model_required" (app/api/chat/route.ts:117-122) -- but the user just sees a generic loadError string rather than web's proactive disabled-button + "Choose a model above to chat..." placeholder + inline Settings link.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add `!selectedModel.isEmpty` to canSend, and surface a clear "choose a model" prompt (mirroring the web composer placeholder) when it is empty, instead of only relying on the auto-select happy path.

gap_findings.title: The chat route and the orchestrator independently mint two DIFFERENT random turnKeys when no clientTurnId is supplied
gap_findings.evidence: const turnKey = `chat:${userId}:${clientTurnId ?? globalThis.crypto.randomUUID()}`;  // orchestrator.ts:137, called from inside makeOrchestrator -- app/api/chat/route.ts:155 computes the SAME expression independently before calling registerChatTurn/orchestrate, so when clientTurnId is undefined each side calls globalThis.crypto.randomUUID() separately and gets a different value.
gap_findings.why: In normal web/iOS usage this is latent because both clients always generate and send a clientTurnId, so the two computations agree. But any direct API caller (a script, a future integration, or a test) that omits clientTurnId gets a turnKey back in the HTTP response (route.ts:176, used for turn-registry lookups and Cancel) that does NOT match the turnKey embedded in that same turn's own `chat.turn`/`chat.evidence_pack`/`chat.tool_evidence_pack`/`chat.reply` audit rows (all keyed off the orchestrator's separately-generated turnKey) -- making those audit rows uncorrelatable with the turnKey the caller actually has, and making Cancel-by-turnKey a no-op for such a caller since cancelChatTurn only knows the route's turnKey, not the orchestrator's.
gap_findings.recommendation: Generate the turnKey once in the route (already done, route.ts:155) and pass it into orchestrate()/handleTurn() as an explicit argument instead of having the orchestrator recompute its own copy from clientTurnId.

gap_findings.title: When the tool loop needs more than MAX_STEPS provider round-trips, the reply silently collapses to just the bare disclaimer with no partial-answer or truncation signal
gap_findings.evidence: for (let step = 0; step < MAX_STEPS; step++) { ... if (resp.stop_reason !== "tool_use" || toolUses.length === 0) break; ... /* execute tools, push results, loop continues */ }  -- MAX_STEPS = 5 (llm.ts:50). If step index 4 (the last allowed iteration) STILL returns tool_use, the tool results are executed and pushed to `messages` but the `for` loop then exits on its own condition without ever sending those results back to the model for a final text turn. OpenAILLM.run has the identical shape at llm.ts:536-628.
gap_findings.why: `text` retains whatever the LAST model response contained -- typically empty or near-empty, since a response whose stop_reason is tool_use rarely carries prose alongside the tool call. The function then returns `withDisclaimer(text)` (Anthropic) or `text || DISCLAIMER` (OpenAI), i.e. the user's answer is silently reduced to just "This is general information, not personalized financial advice." with zero substantive content, after having spent up to 5 provider calls and however many tool executions (get_quote/get_fundamentals/kb_search/get_positions/etc. -- a plausible chain for a multi-part question) worth of latency and token cost. The API still returns 200 and the chat UI renders it as a normal, if terse, answer -- there is no "I ran out of steps" signal anywhere in the reply, onStage callback, or UI.
gap_findings.recommendation: On exiting the loop specifically because the last step still wanted tools (rather than because the model naturally stopped), either allow one final no-tools completion call to summarize what was gathered so far, or set an explicit flag/text ("I gathered partial information but ran out of steps -- ask again for more detail") instead of falling through to a bare disclaimer.

gap_findings.title: draft_order has no dollar-notional field or guidance, risking share-count/dollar-amount confusion when a user says "buy $X of SYMBOL"
gap_findings.evidence: const DRAFT_ORDER_SCHEMA: Record<string, unknown> = { type: "object", ..., required: ["symbol","side","qty"], properties: { symbol:{...}, side:{...}, qty:{type:"number"}, order_type:{...}, limit_usd:{...}, rationale:{...} } };  -- qty is unlabeled (no units), there is no notional_usd field, and the tool description (tools.ts:85-88) and system prompt (prompt.ts) never instruct the model to convert a dollar amount to shares via a fresh get_quote before drafting.
gap_findings.why: Users very commonly speak in dollar terms ("buy $1000 of TSLA", "put $500 into AAPL"). Since draft_order only accepts a raw share `qty`, the model must either ask a clarifying question (not enforced by anything) or silently compute qty = notional/price itself, and nothing in the tool contract requires it to fetch a fresh quote first -- under time/step pressure (MAX_STEPS=5, see coach-09) a model could plausibly pass the dollar figure straight through as `qty` (e.g. interpreting "$500" as qty:500), producing an order roughly 100-1000x the intended size for a normally-priced stock. The downstream policy caps at stage time (evaluateTradeProposal) would catch an order that blows past maxOrderNotional, but for a lower-priced stock or a generous cap, a materially wrong-sized order could still pass the preview and be presented to the user as "Passes policy preview" for approval.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add an optional `notional_usd` field to the draft_order schema, and have the tool (server-side) fetch a live quote and compute qty itself when notional is given instead of trusting the model's arithmetic; update the tool description to explicitly require calling get_quote before converting any dollar-denominated request to a share qty.

gap_findings.title: kb_search's k parameter has no upper bound, unlike every sibling numeric tool input in the same file
gap_findings.evidence: k: { type: "integer", minimum: 1 }  -- tools.ts:155, forwarded unclamped: `k: typeof input.k === "number" ? input.k : 5` (tools.ts:165) straight into retrieveContextDetailed(args.query, symbol, args.k ?? 5, ...). Compare get_earnings_calendar's days (`Number.isInteger(days) && days !== 0 && days >= -31 && days <= 31 ? days : undefined`, tools.ts:305) and search_instrument's limit (`limit >= 1 && limit <= 20`, tools.ts:354) -- both explicitly clamp their untrusted numeric input server-side; kb_search does not.
gap_findings.why: Every other numeric chat-tool input in this file is treated as untrusted model output and explicitly range-checked server-side per the file's own stated philosophy ("Server-side validation -- the model's input is untrusted regardless of any schema claim.", tools.ts:90). kb_search's k breaks that pattern: a model (or a prompt-injected instruction steering it) requesting an unreasonably large k would forward straight into the RAG retrieval pipeline's fetch-size scaling (managedVersionTopKCap in vector-db.ts scales its cap with the caller's requested limit) with no clamp at the chat-tool boundary, risking disproportionate embedding/rerank spend and an oversized tool-result payload for a single call.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add a maximum to the k schema (e.g. 1-20, matching search_instrument's pattern) and clamp server-side in the same style as the other tools in this file.

gap_findings.title: Price alerts silently stop evaluating when no broker account is active
gap_findings.evidence:
const accountNumber = policy.accountNumber;
  if (!accountNumber) return [];
gap_findings.why: checkPriceAlerts() calls getPolicy(userId) with no connectedAccountId, which resolves to whichever connected account is currently 'active' for that user (src/lib/db-profiles.ts resolveAccount -> getActiveConnectedAccount). PriceAlert rows are user-scoped, not account-scoped (types.ts:127-138), and the watchlist page banner literally says 'yours across every account' -- yet evaluation is gated on one account's accountNumber. A user with zero connected accounts, or whose active account was disconnected/removed, or who simply switches the active account to one not yet fully linked, still has armed.length > 0 but the function returns [] before ever calling the broker. Every armed alert for that user goes dark, with no error, no audit row, and no UI signal that alerts are paused.
gap_findings.recommendation: Evaluate price alerts against an account chosen explicitly for quote purposes (not the mutable 'active' pointer), or fall back to any workable connected account, and emit an explicit 'alerts paused: no account' audit/UI state when none exists at all.

gap_findings.title: checkPriceAlerts swallows broker-quote errors with zero logging
gap_findings.why: Any exception from the broker gateway (auth failure, rate limit, network outage) is caught and discarded with an empty catch block -- no console.error, no audit() call, nothing recorded anywhere. checkAllUserPriceAlerts()'s own .catch() (alerts.ts:120) never fires because checkPriceAlerts() resolves normally with []. A persistent broker problem on one user's active account means every armed alert is silently re-checked and silently skipped every 60 seconds forever, with no operator-visible signal -- exactly the 'alert never fires and nobody can tell why' failure mode this review targets.
gap_findings.recommendation: At minimum audit()/console.error the caught exception, mirroring how checkAllUserPriceAlerts already logs per-user errors, so a sustained broker failure is discoverable instead of indistinguishable from 'nothing to check.'

gap_findings.title: Price-alert push deep link's ?symbol= is dropped by both web and iOS
gap_findings.evidence:
case "price_alert":
        return routing.symbol
          ? `/console/watchlist?symbol=${encodeURIComponent(routing.symbol)}`
          : "/console/watchlist";
gap_findings.why: The server builds a symbol-specific URL and the file's header comment calls the query param 'additive' routing for 'a client that prefers structured routing.' Neither client honors it: app/console/watchlist/page.tsx never calls useSearchParams or reads the URL, so tapping a 'Price alert: NVDA' notification on the web lands on the full unfiltered watchlist/alerts list. ios/SocraticTrade/DeepLink.swift:75-77 matches the 'watchlist' path and returns only `.tab(.markets)`, discarding the query entirely -- unlike the 'approvals' case (DeepLink.swift:58-73) which DOES parse `?proposal=` into a highlighted destination. A user with several armed alerts gets no indication which one just fired, on either surface.
gap_findings.recommendation: Implement symbol-aware routing on both the watchlist page (scroll-to/highlight via useSearchParams) and DeepLink.swift (a `.watchlist(symbol:)` destination mirroring `.proposal(id:)`), or stop implying finer-grained routing exists in the push-deep-links.ts comment.

gap_findings.title: iOS watchlist/alert commands queue behind a 30-minute strategy run
gap_findings.why: watchlist.add, watchlist.remove, alert.create, and alert.delete are not in IMMEDIATE_MOBILE_COMMAND_TYPES, so from iOS they go through the single, strictly-serial mobile_commands worker (claimNextQueuedCommand picks the globally oldest queued row one at a time, mobile-api.ts:701-717) alongside strategy.run_once, which the same file documents as legitimately taking up to STALE_MOBILE_COMMAND_THRESHOLD_MS = 30 minutes (line 1171). If a run_once is queued ahead of or already running when a watchlist/alert command is submitted, the action sits queued for the full duration. The web app calls POST /api/watchlist and /api/alerts directly and synchronously with no equivalent delay. This mirrors the already-flagged proposal.approve/reject queuing issue but for a different, previously-uncovered set of command types.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add watchlist.add/remove and alert.create/delete to IMMEDIATE_MOBILE_COMMAND_TYPES -- none of them touch the broker or need serialization with a strategy run.

gap_findings.title: checkPriceAlerts/checkAllUserPriceAlerts have zero test coverage
gap_findings.evidence: describe("price alerts", () => { it("normalizes comparison operators"...); it("creates, lists, and deletes alerts"...); it("rejects invalid alert input"...); }) -- grep across test/ for checkPriceAlerts|checkAllUserPriceAlerts returns zero hits anywhere in the repo.
gap_findings.why: The entire money-relevant behavior of this feature -- does a crossing get detected, does a missing/invalid quote get skipped instead of false-triggering, does a broker error leave the alert armed for a later retry, does a trigger call sendNotification exactly once -- lives in checkPriceAlerts/checkAllUserPriceAlerts (src/lib/alerts.ts) and is completely untested. Only CRUD (create/list/delete) and input validation are covered. A regression in the evaluation loop, including the account-gating and error-swallowing behavior flagged above, would ship without a single failing test.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add unit tests covering: a crossing that should fire, a quote below/above threshold that should not, a missing/zero quote (skip), a broker-gateway throw (should not crash and should leave the alert armed), and no-active-account (should return [] without calling the gateway), using an injected fake gateway/policy the way other broker-dependent tests in this repo already do.

gap_findings.title: Price alerts fire against raw quotes with no staleness check
gap_findings.why: The order-placement path has a dedicated staleness gate (quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate in src/lib/quotes-cascade.ts, applied in policy.ts:395-475) that checks quote age before acting on a price. checkPriceAlerts uses none of that infrastructure -- it takes whatever `.price` the broker gateway returns with no age check at all. A delayed/cached quote (a provider outage falling back to a stale cached value, or a venue-delayed feed) can trigger an alert against a price that is actually minutes old, or fail to trigger promptly against one that has already moved, with no staleness annotation surfaced the way the order path already provides.
gap_findings.recommendation: Reuse quoteAgeSecForStalenessGate (or the quote's own asOf/timestamp) to skip evaluating an alert against a quote older than a small threshold, and/or annotate the triggered notification with quote age so a delayed trigger is honestly labeled.

gap_findings.title: An alert is marked 'triggered' before delivery is attempted, with no retry if every channel fails
gap_findings.why: markPriceAlertTriggered flips the alert's DB status to 'triggered' (one-shot, non-reversible per src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1777-1781) before sendNotification is even awaited. Since price alerts never re-arm by design, if every enabled delivery channel fails at send time (a revoked Pushover token, a wrong ntfy topic, an expired APNs cert, or simply zero channels configured yet), sendNotification records a status:'failed'/'skipped' notification_events row but there is no compensating retry of the notification for an already-triggered alert. The only way the user learns their alert fired is by manually opening the Watchlist or Activity page.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either don't flip the alert to 'triggered' until sendNotification reports at least one successful channel (retrying next tick if delivery fully failed), or surface undelivered-but-triggered alerts more prominently on the Watchlist page instead of blending in with delivered ones.

gap_findings.title: Price alerts can only be created or deleted -- no edit, pause, or snooze
gap_findings.evidence: export async function GET... export async function POST... export async function DELETE... -- no PUT/PATCH handler; src/lib/alerts.ts exports only createAlert/listAlerts/removeAlert, no updateAlert.
gap_findings.why: Changing an armed alert's price/note, or temporarily pausing it without losing it, requires delete + recreate on both web and iOS, discarding the original id/createdAt. The review brief specifically asks about edit/mute/snooze lifecycle actions and none exist for price alerts -- the Alert Center's 24h mute is display-only, for a different set of event types, and doesn't apply to price_alert at all.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add a PUT/PATCH /api/alerts endpoint (and a matching mobile-api.ts alert.update command) for price/op/note edits, and consider a simple armed/paused toggle for snoozing without deleting.

gap_findings.title: Watchlist and price-alert symbol validation use two different regexes
gap_findings.why: The watchlist validator (isValidAppSymbol, used by watchlist.ts and mobile-api.ts's watchlist.add/remove decode) requires a leading letter and rejects '..' or a trailing '.'. The price-alert validator (SYMBOL_RE, used by createAlert for both the web route and the iOS alert.create command) allows any 1-10 character string of letters/dots, including '...', a leading dot, or a bare '.'. A malformed symbol like '...' passes alert creation, gets stored armed, and can never match a real quote -- it sits armed forever, visually indistinguishable in the UI from a working alert (another way an alert can silently never fire).
gap_findings.recommendation: Have createAlert call the same isValidAppSymbol used by the watchlist path instead of maintaining a second, looser regex.

gap_findings.title: A price-alert's notification row is tagged with whatever account happened to be active, not with anything meaningful to the alert
gap_findings.evidence: const connectedAccountId = options.connectedAccountId ?? policy.connectedAccountId;
gap_findings.why: checkPriceAlerts calls sendNotification without an explicit connectedAccountId, so it falls back to policy.connectedAccountId -- whichever account was 'active' at the moment the 60-second tick ran. PriceAlert rows are user-scoped, not account-scoped (types.ts:127-138), so this tag is incidental, not meaningful. app/console/activity/page.tsx:213 filters the Activity feed to the currently active account, so a price-alert notification can fall out of the default Activity view the moment the user switches accounts (a 'N events from your other accounts' banner mitigates discoverability, but the underlying account tag is still semantically wrong for a cross-account watch).
gap_findings.recommendation: Pass connectedAccountId: undefined explicitly for price_alert notifications so they are never filtered by account-scoping logic, matching their actual account-independent semantics.

gap_findings.title: Price-alert note length is capped on iOS (500 chars) but unbounded on the web API
gap_findings.why: createAlert() itself never truncates note (`input.note?.trim() ?? ""`), so the web REST endpoint accepts an arbitrarily long note while the iOS mobile-command decode path caps the same field at 500 characters before it ever reaches createAlert. A very long note created via the web can then break the Discord webhook embed, which renders it verbatim (`description = String(alert.note)` in notifications.ts's formatDiscordPayload price_alert case) -- Discord embed descriptions have their own hard cap the code doesn't guard against.
gap_findings.recommendation: Cap the note length once, inside createAlert() (or the price-alert insert in db-api-keys.ts), so both entry points share the same limit instead of iOS silently being stricter than the API it calls.

gap_findings.title: A disconnected ('draining') account can be reactivated and becomes the live trading target while the scheduler is still tearing it down
gap_findings.evidence: setActiveConnectedAccount(id, userId) only checks the row exists for this user, then flips is_active — it never reads or clears is_draining: `db.prepare("UPDATE connected_accounts SET is_active = 0 WHERE user_id = ?").run(userId); db.prepare("UPDATE connected_accounts SET is_active = 1 WHERE id = ? AND user_id = ?").run(id, userId);`. Clicking Disconnect calls deleteConnectedAccount (line 1373), which only sets `is_draining = 1, is_active = 0` — the row and its encrypted apiKey/apiSecret persist until a later scheduler tick (scheduler.ts:846-870) cancels open orders and calls purgeConnectedAccount. Nothing in between blocks reactivation: brokers.tsx's 'Load' button (lines 300-319) is gated only on `!account.isActive`; chrome.tsx's ScopeSelector lists it under 'Other Accounts' (`others = snapshot.connectedAccounts.filter(a => !a.isActive)`, line 91) and its 'Switch' button (line ~143 `disabled={isActive || busyId !== null}`) has no isDraining check either; iOS's ConnectedAccountSettingsRow (HomeView.swift:1028-1032) even prints "draining — existing orders wind down before removal" right next to a fully enabled 'Use' button (line 1049) that is never disabled for isDraining. None of execution-mode.ts, strategy.ts, or policy.ts reference isDraining, so a Run Once against the reactivated account places orders normally.
gap_findings.why: A user who clicks Disconnect then immediately re-Loads/re-Uses the same account (e.g. changed their mind, or it's still showing in the list because purge hasn't run yet) makes that account the full policy target (getPolicy -> resolveAccount -> getActiveConnectedAccount, which also has no isDraining filter) while the scheduler's drain routine is independently cancelling its open orders and racing to delete the row's credentials. A trade placed through Run Once in that window can be placed and then have its account's connection yanked out from under it mid-run, and a subsequent scheduler tick can silently purge the very account the UI just told the user is 'active' -- violating the owner's correctness bar ('never place an unintended order... keep persisted state consistent').
gap_findings.recommendation: Have setActiveConnectedAccount reject (or auto-clear is_draining and cancel the pending purge) for a draining row; disable Load/Use and grey the Switch/Use rows client-side wherever isDraining is true (brokers.tsx, chrome.tsx ScopeSelector, HomeView.swift) instead of only checking isActive.

gap_findings.title: Settings > Broker connections mislabels every non-loaded account 'Inactive' even when it is actively trading in the background
gap_findings.evidence: `const stateInfo = isCurrentLoaded && snapshot?.policy ? deriveStateInfo(snapshot.policy) : null;` (isCurrentLoaded === account.isActive). The chip render at lines 271-280 falls back to `<Chip tone="muted">{account.isActive ? "Loaded" : "Inactive"}</Chip>` whenever stateInfo is null -- which is every row in the 'Other Accounts' section, unconditionally. But the app schedules and runs each connected account's strategy independently of which one is 'loaded' (scheduler.ts loops `for (const account of listConnectedAccounts(userId))`, not just the active one), and the dashboard snapshot already carries the correct per-account state in `connectedAccountPolicies` (dashboard.ts:350-368), which chrome.tsx's ScopeSelector correctly reads (`policy = snapshot.connectedAccountPolicies?.[account.id]`) to show real per-account chips like 'Autopilot'/'Ask-first'/'Paused - market closed' (derive.ts deriveStateInfo, e.g. line 132-153).
gap_findings.why: A second connected account (e.g. a live Roth IRA) that is genuinely running Autopilot right now shows the same static 'Inactive' chip as an account that has never been armed. For a real-money multi-account trading app this is a materially misleading state readout on the exact screen (Settings > Broker connections) a user checks to answer 'is anything happening in my other account.'
gap_findings.recommendation: Compute stateInfo from `snapshot.connectedAccountPolicies?.[account.id]` for every row (as ScopeSelector already does), not only for the currently-loaded one.

gap_findings.title: First-broker auto-activation is inconsistent: Robinhood auto-loads the first connected account, Alpaca/Tradier/eToro/Public/Webull never do
gap_findings.evidence: Robinhood connect: `isActive: body.isActive ?? existing?.isActive ?? !getActiveConnectedAccount(userId)` -- auto-activates when nothing else is active. The generic (Alpaca/Tradier/eToro/Public/Webull) upsert at line 212 uses `isActive: body.isActive ?? false` -- never auto-activates, even for a brand-new user's very first connection.
gap_findings.why: Alpaca is the most prominent 'Connect' button in the brokers.tsx header (listed before Tradier/Public), so most first-run users will complete readiness step 1 ('Connect a broker') via Alpaca and land on an unexplained-feeling extra manual step (readiness step 2, 'Select an active account') that a Robinhood-first user never sees. The checklist itself doesn't call out that this differs by broker.
gap_findings.recommendation: Make the generic branch auto-activate on first connect too, matching Robinhood: `isActive: body.isActive ?? existing?.isActive ?? !getActiveConnectedAccount(userId)`.

gap_findings.title: Website session expiry inside an already-open console tab has no recovery path -- stuck behind a stale 'Unauthorized' banner, Run Once fails with a misleading generic message
gap_findings.evidence: middleware.ts:412-419 answers an unauthenticated `/api/*` request with a plain 401 (`new NextResponse("Unauthorized", { status: 401 })`), never a redirect (redirects only fire for page navigation, not fetch()). useConsoleData's runFetch (lines 139-150) treats that identically to any other transient error: it keeps the last-good snapshot on screen and sets `error = "Unauthorized"`. `grep -rn '"/login"' app/console` returns zero hits -- nothing in the console SPA ever navigates to /login. chrome.tsx's freshness label (line ~1043-1044, 1106-1107) shows this only as `error && <span ... title={error}>` next to a 'delayed' badge. If the user then clicks Run Once, classifyRunFailure("Unauthorized", 401) (chrome.tsx:619-703) matches none of its specific branches and falls to the generic default at the end: `{ title: "The run failed", detail: message, fixHref: "/console/activity", fixLabel: "See the full story in Activity" }`.
gap_findings.why: A session that expires (or is invalidated) while the console tab stays open never tells the user to sign back in -- it just quietly degrades to stale data forever (polling every 15s, 401 every time) and, if they try to act, sends them to Activity to investigate 'why the run failed' instead of back to /login.
gap_findings.recommendation: Have the console's fetch client special-case 401 (distinct from other ConsoleApiErrors): stop the poll loop and route to /login (or show an explicit 'sign in again' banner) instead of the generic staleness/failure paths.

gap_findings.title: iOS readiness checklist has no way to represent (or fix) missing LLM key / Green-team model, unlike the website's 5-step checklist
gap_findings.evidence: `struct Readiness: Decodable { let hasAccount: Bool; let hasUniverse: Bool }` -- no llm/model field at all. The server's mobileReadiness (src/lib/mobile-api.ts:1315-1316) only ever computes `hasAccount`/`hasUniverse`, matching the client shape. HomeView.swift:9 gates the entire 'ready' vs 'setup' UI on `!snapshot.readiness.hasAccount || !snapshot.readiness.hasUniverse` -- once those two are true it renders ReadyHomeHero with a live Run Once CTA. Compare the website's 5-step checklist (app/console/lib/derive.ts, step `id: "llm"` around line 710-724) which explicitly blocks 'ready' on `hasLlmKey && hasGreenModel`. Separately, `grep -rln "OpenRouter|apiKeys|LLM.*[Kk]ey" ios/SocraticTrade` returns zero files -- there is no LLM-key management screen anywhere in the iOS app.
gap_findings.why: A first-run iOS user who connects a broker and sets a universe sees the app declare itself fully 'ready to trade' and offers Run Once, even though no LLM key/model is configured -- the only way they discover the real blocker is a failed Run Once, and even then there is no in-app screen to fix it (they must switch to the website).
gap_findings.recommendation: Add an llmConfigured/hasGreenModel field to the mobile snapshot's readiness payload and gate the iOS 'ready' state on it too, or explicitly acknowledge in the checklist copy that LLM configuration must happen on the website.

gap_findings.title: iOS first-run checklist tells the user to connect a broker 'in Account & Settings' but that screen has no broker-connect UI at all
gap_findings.evidence: Checklist row detail (line 87): "Connect Alpaca or Robinhood in Account & Settings, then select it here." But AccountSettingsView's accountsSection (lines 818-848) only ever renders ConnectedAccountSettingsRow for EXISTING accounts (activate-only, via 'Use') -- there is no Connect Alpaca/Robinhood/Tradier button anywhere in the sheet. The screen's own empty-state text at line 844 contradicts line 87: "No connected accounts.  Connect one in Socratic-Trade, then return here to select it." -- i.e. the true instruction is 'leave the app and use the website'.
gap_findings.why: A first-time iOS-only user (downloaded the app without ever visiting the website) hits a genuine dead end: the checklist's own copy claims the fix is inside the very screen it links to, and only the empty-state variant of that same screen tells the truth.
gap_findings.recommendation: Already tracked in the review register as ios-hig-ux:ios-09 (same file/line, broader remediation options incl. reusing AdminPortalView's cookie-sharing web view). Cross-confirming from the account-lifecycle trace: fix the misleading line-87 copy at minimum even if a full in-app connect flow isn't built.

gap_findings.title: Disconnect confirmation claims immediate credential removal; actual deletion is deferred to a background scheduler drain/purge
gap_findings.evidence: Confirm-dialog copy: "This removes the connection and its stored credentials from this app." Server-side, deleteConnectedAccount (src/lib/db-api-keys.ts:1373-1380) only sets `is_draining = 1, is_active = 0`; the row (including encrypted api_key/api_secret) and purgeConnectedAccount's actual DELETE only run later, from the scheduler's per-tick account loop (scheduler.ts:846-870), after any open orders are cancelled and reconciled.
gap_findings.why: The word 'removes ... from this app' reads as immediate, but nothing is actually deleted at click time -- the window this leaves open is exactly what lifecycle-01 exploits (the account is still fully live and reactivatable during the drain).
gap_findings.recommendation: Either make the disconnect path synchronous when there is nothing to drain (no open orders), or change the copy to say the removal completes once open orders are settled, and surface a visible 'disconnecting' state on the row in the interim.

gap_findings.title: No self-service data export exists before the irreversible, typed-phrase account deletion flow
gap_findings.evidence: danger.tsx:156-161 describes deletion as permanently removing "stored API keys, broker connections and OAuth tokens, settings, strategy profiles, watchlists, alerts, chat history, memories, proposals, fills, snapshots, notifications, and private learned context." `grep -rln "export\|dataExport\|GDPR" app/api src/lib -i` (excluding TS `export function` module syntax) finds no personal-data export feature anywhere. The only stated recourse is database backups, and legal-notice.ts:22 sets `BACKUP_RETENTION_DAYS = 7` -- an operator-side restore, not user self-service.
gap_findings.why: A user who wants to keep a record of their decision trace / fill / P&L history before deleting has no in-app way to get it out first; the only fallback (asking the operator to restore a 7-day backup) doesn't scale past a single-operator deployment and isn't mentioned anywhere in the deletion flow itself.
gap_findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight 'export my data' (JSON/CSV) action to Settings, offered as a step before the deletion flow's typed confirmation.

gap_findings.title: Alpaca/eToro/Public/Webull connect never validates credentials against the broker's API before marking the account 'connected' (Tradier does)
gap_findings.evidence: The Alpaca/eToro/public/webull path (lines 190-213) calls `upsertConnectedAccount(...)` directly with whatever the user typed, with no live probe. Compare the Tradier path (lines 218-250), which explicitly calls `gw.getAccounts()` against the real API to resolve the account number and will surface an error if the token is bad.
gap_findings.why: A typo'd Alpaca key/secret sails straight through readiness checklist step 1 ('Connect a broker' -> complete) and step 2 ('Select an active account' -> complete once loaded); the first real signal of trouble is a failed Run Once, at which point classifyRunFailure's generic 'account' bucket (chrome.tsx ~line 690) gives a vague 'Account problem' rather than 'these credentials were never checked.'
gap_findings.recommendation: Add a lightweight getAccounts()-style probe on Alpaca/eToro/Public/Webull connect, matching the Tradier path, and surface a clear 400 if it fails.

gap_findings.title: Switching into a live (real-money) account requires an explicit confirmation on iOS but is a single click on the website
gap_findings.evidence: iOS: tapping 'Use' on a non-paper account sets `confirmingLiveActivation = true`, which shows an alert ("Use Brokerage Account? ... Approved actions will use this account.", lines 1066-1071) before calling activate(). Website: chrome.tsx ScopeSelector's switchTo (lines 115-127) and brokers.tsx's Load button (lines 300-319) both call activateAccount(id) immediately on click, with no confirmation step, live or paper.
gap_findings.why: The exact same action -- making a live brokerage account the one Run Once/approvals will trade through -- has meaningfully different friction depending on which client the owner happens to be using, which is confusing on its own and, per the owner's 'no extra are-you-sure ceremony beyond a normal order confirmation' ruling, worth resolving in one direction deliberately rather than leaving as an accidental platform drift.
gap_findings.recommendation: Pick one behavior (most likely: no confirm, matching the owner's stated preference against extra ceremony) and align both clients.

gap_findings.title: iOS account-deletion confirm silently marks all five web acknowledgement checkboxes 'true' server-side without ever showing them to the user
gap_findings.evidence: The mobile confirm route hardcodes every acknowledgement the web flow requires the user to individually tick: `deleteAppData: true, deleteBrokerConnections: true, understandBrokerPositionsRemain: true, understandProviderRevocation: true, understandCanSignInAgain: true` (lines 47-51), gated only on typed identity + typed phrase matching. Compare app/console/settings/danger.tsx's ACK_ITEMS (lines 42-48), five separate checkboxes the web user must explicitly check, including "I understand I may need to revoke Google, GitHub, Apple, or broker access in those providers' settings too" -- on iOS this is only ever shown as read-only numbered step text (HomeView.swift:932-935), never an interactive checkbox, yet the server records it as affirmatively acknowledged.
gap_findings.why: For a permanently irreversible, typed-phrase-gated action, the server treats an iOS user as having made five specific acknowledgements (including provider-revocation and broker-positions-remain caveats) they were never asked to individually confirm -- a real consent-integrity gap between what the record says and what the user did.
gap_findings.recommendation: Either surface the same five items as toggles the iOS user must check before Delete becomes enabled, or accept a single narrower 'I understand this is permanent' acknowledgement server-side instead of claiming all five were individually confirmed.

gap_findings.title: Settings > Broker connections' pending-proposal count for non-loaded accounts is dead code -- it always reads zero
gap_findings.evidence: `const pendingCount = isCurrentLoaded ? (snapshot.pendingProposals ?? []).length : (snapshot.pendingProposals ?? []).filter(p => p.proposal?.accountId === account.id || p.accountId === account.id).length;` -- but `snapshot.pendingProposals` is built server-side in dashboard.ts:690 as `accountNumber ? listPendingProposals(accountNumber, userId) : []`, where `accountNumber` is the ACTIVE account's number. It structurally can never contain a proposal for any other account, so the `.filter(...)` on the 'Other Accounts' branch always operates on an array with zero matching entries.
gap_findings.why: The pending-proposal Chip on every non-loaded account row (line 281-285) will show nothing even when that account genuinely has pending proposals waiting (the scheduler runs every connected account's strategy independently of which is loaded) -- worse than simply omitting the count, this silently implies 'zero pending' when the true number is unknown. This is the same underlying gap the register already tracks at a UX level (desktop-web-ux:dweb-12, 'a pending Roth proposal is invisible while Paper is loaded'); this entry pinpoints the specific dead filter responsible.
gap_findings.recommendation: Fetch (or have the snapshot include) a per-account pending-proposal count across all connected accounts, not just the active one's, and wire brokers.tsx's non-loaded rows to it.
